## Quick 260719-nwe — Streaming chat scroll: follow-the-stream (pin-the-question REVERSED) + user-bubble + send-scroll fixes

> **Final `7ca67720` (REVERSING rejected `b7edb2dd` + `15ab25cb`) + `bbc7a80f` + `7614d968`, docs `7ecc589e`, on `feat/ui-2`.** FE-primary run-lane fix (plus a 6-line BE `event_id` carry in `bbc7a80f`) for two glitches m0o's streaming exposed — a jittering run-summary footer and the user's own question scrolling off-screen. Ships the ACCEPTED "follow the stream" scroll after the user REJECTED an initial "pin the question" approach. Cluster li0→m0o→nwe→rqo.

- **What / Why (settled).** Once the reply streamed (~192 chunks in ~2s), `ChatPanel`'s auto-scroll effect fired on every `[messages, streamingContent, isStreaming]` change doing `scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth" })` — ~192 stacked SMOOTH animations interrupting each other janked the pinned Run-summary card (glitch #1), and because the anchor sits BELOW the footer every scroll went past it, pushing the user's question off the top (glitch #2, verified NOT a deletion — the DOM still held the text). Initial fix "pin the newest question to the top on a new turn" (`b7edb2dd`, hard-held by `15ab25cb`) was REJECTED by the user; the accepted FINAL (`7ca67720`, net −86/+56 removing the pin-by-selector logic) is standard follow-the-stream: stick-to-bottom that RESPECTS a scroll-up, instant (never smooth) during streaming. `bbc7a80f` then stopped the streamed reply overwriting the user's bubble (the reply reuses the user turn's `message_id`; a bare-id fallback key collided → BUG-018 regression on the streamed-POST path); `7614d968` force-scrolls to bottom + re-arms follow on a fresh send.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx` (current tree): the scroll LISTENER maintaining `stickToBottomRef` (near-bottom < 120px) at :121-131; the fresh-user-turn effect (`lastUserIdRef` :116) that force-scrolls `messagesEndRef` with `behavior:"auto"` + re-arms `stickToBottomRef=true` on a changed last-user id (:137-163, deps reduced to `[messages]` :163); `messagesEndRef` (:445) sits below `{transcriptFooter}` (:442). NOTE the FINAL follow-stream removed ChatPanel's pin-by-selector `querySelector('[data-message-id=…]')`; the `data-message-id` ATTRIBUTE remains (harmless, still asserted by a ChatPanel test) on `MessageBubble.tsx` :202/:226/:319 and `ErrorMessage.tsx` :29. `bbc7a80f`: BE `backend/app/api/run_commands.py` carries `event_id: chat-reply:{message_id}` on the streamed frame (~:1286 region) + FE `frontend/src/hooks/useRunChat.ts` hardens `upsertNarratorMessage` to mint the same `chat-reply:{message_id}` key when `event_id` is absent (:275-276) rather than fall back to the bare id. (Continuous chunk-following was LATER superseded by rqo's ResizeObserver — see Quick 260719-rqo; the current :137-163 effect only detects the fresh turn.)
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** UX REVERSAL — the accepted model is "follow the stream, respect scroll-up," NOT "pin the question to the top." Do not re-introduce the pin (`scrollIntoView({block:"start"})` on the newest user turn, or a `handledTurnRef`/data-message-id pin query in ChatPanel): the user explicitly rejected it (`b7edb2dd`/`15ab25cb` superseded by `7ca67720`). A single scroll-up flips `stickToBottomRef` off so streaming NEVER yanks the user back down (< 120px gate). Instant (`behavior:"auto"`), never `"smooth"`, during streaming — smooth animations stack and jank. FE-only except the intentional 6-line BE `event_id` carry; the reducer/transport in `useRunChat.ts` transport layer is otherwise untouched. Chat is out of the characterization goldens (INV-3) — the glitch was purely scroll behavior.
- **Verification.** RED→GREEN in `ChatPanel.test.tsx`/`useRunChat.test.ts` where jsdom allows (it stubs `scrollIntoView` as a no-op and lays out no scroll geometry, so the VISUAL scroll is orchestrator-proven): rows expose `data-message-id`, the effect does not throw when `scrollIntoView` is absent, the new-user-turn branch asserts `behavior:"auto"`, and `bbc7a80f`'s +25-line test asserts a streamed reply does NOT overwrite the user's bubble. Existing ChatPanel/RunChatLane suites stay green; `tsc --noEmit` clean. LIVE-PROVEN by the orchestrator (live DOM + screenshots: the question stays visible, the footer no longer jitters, the user bubble survives the reply). ## Quick 260719-rqo — Left-chat streaming polish: reading-run-data indicator + typewriter smoothing + footer-jitter ResizeObserver

> **Commits `312271aa` (typewriter) + `eddc13db` (reading indicator + hook test) + `fa55332e` (footer-jitter RO), docs `846dde7d`/`93ab1d74`, on `feat/ui-2`.** FE-only polish on the m0o/nwe streaming reply — a "reading run data…" indicator fills the mid-reply read-tool freeze, `useSmoothText` typewriter-smooths coarse deltas, and a ResizeObserver follows the RENDERED height so the run-summary footer stops jittering. Last of the cluster li0→m0o→nwe→rqo.

- **What / Why (settled).** Live cadence: the reply emits ~59 chars, FREEZES ~1.3s while the Concierge calls a read tool (`read_events`/`list_refs`), then streams the answer — the freeze read as dead air, and the raw chunk deltas were coarse/bursty. (A) A mid-reply chunk-gap on the Concierge path is ALWAYS a read-tool call, so the FE can accurately show "reading run data…" during a gap with no backend signal. (B) `useSmoothText` reveals a growing target at a steady rAF pace (~1/6 of the buffer per frame) so bursts flow as a typewriter. (C) The typewriter INTRODUCED a residual footer jitter — a two-clock desync: rendered height grows on the rAF typewriter clock but the auto-scroll "follow" only fired on the chunk clock (`messages` updates), so between chunks the content grew unfollowed (footer drifts down) and each chunk re-pinned it (snaps up) — orchestrator live-measured 31 up/down reversals, up to 57px. Fix: a ResizeObserver drives continuous following off the actual rendered height so BOTH clocks pin the bottom through ONE path.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/hooks/useSmoothText.ts` — the hook at :24 (rAF reveal :47; jsdom/no-rAF or `enabled=false` → returns the target verbatim :30); wired in `frontend/src/components/chat/MessageBubble.tsx` (import :18, `const smoothedContent = useSmoothText(displayContent, isAssistant)` :142). `frontend/src/components/chat/RunChatLane.tsx` — the `ReadingIndicator` component ("reading run data…") at :268-299; window constants `READING_GAP_MS = 700` (:264) / `READING_MAX_MS = 15_000` (:265); `isReading` state :916; the gap-window effect at :924-940 (hide/show/safety `setTimeout`s, keyed on the per-chunk-minted `replyStreaming` object, deps `[replyStreaming]` :940 — setState fires ONLY inside timer callbacks, react-hooks-lint-safe); a `viewedRunId`-keyed reset :947-950; rendered `{isReading && <ReadingIndicator />}` at :1514. `replyStreaming` plumbing in `frontend/src/hooks/useRunChat.ts` (`ReplyStreamingState` :53-56, state :348, set per `chat_reply_chunk` :398-401). `frontend/src/components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx` — `scrollContentRef` (:113) attached to the transcript content wrapper `<div ref={scrollContentRef} className="mx-auto max-w-4xl">` (:402); the ResizeObserver effect at :180-191 (`container.scrollTop = container.scrollHeight` while `stickToBottomRef` is set, deps `[showGreeting]` :191); this DELETED nwe's chunk-follow branch so the fresh-turn effect's deps reduce to `[messages]` (:163). New test `frontend/src/hooks/useSmoothText.test.ts`.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** INV-12 — the ResizeObserver is the SINGLE continuous-follow path; nwe's chunk-clock `scrollIntoView` follow was DELETED (no dual follow paths). The RO reads `stickToBottomRef` but never writes the observed element's SIZE, so no RO feedback loop; the nwe scroll-listener (< 120px, respect scroll-up) and the fresh-user-turn re-arm are KEPT untouched (the RO cannot force-scroll a new send). SC-001/INV-1 — generic: "reading run data…" is a fixed UI string, no workflow/agent-name literal; the reading state is derived from an elapsed chunk-gap, not a backend flag. The reading indicator is a SEPARATE mid-reply state, never doubled with li0's pre-reply `replyPending`/`TypingIndicator` (before the first chunk) and never shown after finalize; `READING_MAX_MS` caps a pathological stall (never a stuck indicator — mirrors li0's safety-net philosophy). Timers cleaned on unmount/run-switch; purely additive to rendering — `useSmoothText`, the reducer message shape, and the SSE transport are unchanged. Strict react-hooks lint: no ref-write during render, setState only in callbacks/timers.
- **Verification.** RED→GREEN. `fa55332e` reworks `ChatPanel.test.tsx` with a fail-before/pass-after guard: a simulated TYPEWRITER FRAME (rendered height grows with NO `messages`/`streamingContent` change) is unfollowed before the fix (RED) and pinned by the RO after (GREEN, `scrollTop === scrollHeight`); the scrolled-up contract is preserved (RO does not pin when `stickToBottom` is cleared). `eddc13db` adds `useSmoothText.test.ts` (static target → verbatim; `enabled=false` → verbatim; growth under a mocked `requestAnimationFrame` → shown is a strict PREFIX advancing toward target, ~1/6 per frame). Offline (from `frontend/`): the ChatPanel/RunChatLane/useRunChat/useSmoothText suites green; `tsc --noEmit` 0; `eslint` 0 errors on touched files. LIVE-PROVEN by the orchestrator (footer-Y telemetry flat after the RO; the reading indicator fills the read-tool freeze; typewriter smooths the bursts). ## Phase 51 — User-Composable Fan-Out in the Composer (Path B)
**Folder:** `.planning/phases/51-user-composable-fan-out-in-the-composer-path-b/` · **Status:** Complete + offline gates green + **LIVE-PROVEN on real Bedrock**; on `feat/ui-2`, **PUSHED** (origin tip `4cfaad2c`). · **Plans:** 7/7 (5 waves). FANOUT-01..07.

Commits `e5fb306d` (register) .. `4cfaad2c` (live-found fix); scope `15836424`.
- **The crux — `_apply_selections` overlay at BOTH sites (51-04, `973bdbae`).** `engine._apply_selections` (`engine.py:6208`, widened with a 3rd `run_agent_ids` arg) now carries `strategy`/`fanout`/`task_source` onto the run-plan step at the in-plan overlay (guarded patch lines `engine.py:6311-6316` — each fires ONLY when the user selected that lever, so the empty-selections path stays byte-identical, INV-3) AND at the absent-agent synthesis site (`engine.py:2299` consults the trust-compiled `_user_steps_by_agent` map BEFORE the bare `single_shot` fallback `:2300`) — the COMMON case for `custom`, since `allowed_custom_agent_ids("custom")` unions all non-revision base-pipeline agents (its stale docstring corrected in-file). 2-tuple return (`return compiled, {}` `:6237/:6276`); the single caller `engine.py:1467` threads `[s.id for s in agents]` and unpacks. ## Quick 260720-c72 — Surface the run-lane chain (DS chips) + Concierge chain-awareness + chat-input auto-grow

> **Commits `b03fdf82` (FE) + `d713f714` (BE) + docs `ff345cc2` on `feat/ui-2` — NOT pushed (3 ahead of origin `4cfaad2c`).** MVP (Option A) that SURFACES an already-existing chain — render the already-wired chain chips + auto-grow the chat input + make the Concierge name the chainable follow-up workflows via a generic `chain_hints` data block. Root-caused by 3 verified deep-investigation agents (memory `chaining-investigation`); the first user-facing slice of Track B (chaining).

- **What / Why (settled).** Three run-screen LEFT-chat-lane gaps. (1) The chainable next-workflow chips were ALREADY computed in `DashboardLayout` (`laneSuggestions`, from the static `frontend/src/lib/workflowChaining.ts` `CHAIN_OPTIONS`) and ALREADY passed into `RunChatLane` as `suggestions`/`onSuggestion` — but NEVER rendered: Phase 39's mock-fidelity pass deleted the "Suggested next steps" chip block from the settled composer (`RunChatLane.tsx` complete-state comment: "kept here, unrendered"), leaving the chips live only in the History detail view. (2) The chat input was a fixed `rows={1}` `resize-none` textarea (no growth). (3) The run Concierge was chain-blind — its system prompt received nothing about downstream workflows, and there is NO server-side "which workflow can consume this output" logic anywhere (only the static FE `CHAIN_OPTIONS`; the per-agent `produces`/`consumes` metadata is intra-pipeline only). MVP scope = surface the EXISTING chain; build no new chaining machinery.
- **Where (as-built).** FE `frontend/src/components/chat/RunChatLane.tsx`: new `renderChainSuggestions()` (`:1113`) renders DS `Pill`-idiom chips (`--radius-pill`, `border-line-control`, `bg-surface-white`, `text-[11px]`, brand hover; primitive `frontend/src/components/ui/Pill.tsx`) under a "Chain into" label, gated `runState === "complete" && suggestions.length`, each wired to `onSuggestion(id)`; invoked at `:1537` between `renderHeldRefinement()` and `renderComposerBody()` in the `chat-composer` container (just above the input). `FreeTextComposer` auto-grows via a `taRef` + an imperative `autoGrow()` (`el.style.height="auto"` → `min(scrollHeight, 132)` px on change) reset to `auto` in `handleSend` — benefits every composer state. The concierge "ask" branch of `handleFreeText` folds `chain_hints` from the `suggestions` prop onto `sendMessage(..., { concierge: true, chain_hints })` (preserving the `setReplyPending(true)` typing-indicator). FE `frontend/src/hooks/useRunChat.ts`: `SendMessageOptions.chain_hints?: {id,label}[]` folded onto the `/messages` payload ONLY when non-empty. BE `backend/app/api/run_commands.py`: `MessageCommand.chain_hints` (additive optional) → `_ConciergeCtx.chain_hints` threaded from `body` at the fresh-Concierge ctx-build site (`:1211`). BE `backend/app/agents/chat/concierge.py`: `_compose_system_prompt` (`:450-466`) reads `getattr(ctx, "chain_hints", None)` and, only when non-empty, appends ONE generic block built purely from the labels (cap 8 entries × 60 chars, drop empties). Tests: `RunChatLane.test.tsx`, `useRunChat.test.ts`, `test_concierge_capability.py`, `test_chat_messages_endpoint.py`.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** Chose **BE-1** (thread FE-computed hints) over BE-2 (server-compute from the workflow catalogue) — NON-DUAL (INV-3 no dual impl): the FE static `CHAIN_OPTIONS`/`laneSuggestions` stays the SINGLE source of truth, so the chips and the Concierge can never suggest divergent sets. INV-1/SC-001: the Concierge chain block is GENERIC DATA — labels are read from `ctx` and joined; NO `pipeline_type`/`spec.id`/workflow-name branch anywhere in `concierge.py` (banned-pattern grep on `concierge.py` stays 0). INV-3: the no-hints `_compose_system_prompt` is byte-identical (block appended only when non-empty, after all existing blocks). Additive-only: `MessageCommand.chain_hints` is optional-with-default → every non-Concierge POST branch keeps its exact JSON contract; NO migration, NO new SSE/WS event type (a chain-aware reply rides the existing `chat_reply_chunk`/`chat_reply` stream). Prompt-injection defense (T-c72-01): cap count + per-label length, inert DATA, Concierge is proposal-only + told to treat run content as untrusted. Did NOT touch `DashboardLayout`'s `laneSuggestions`/mount wiring, the History chain UI, `handleChainPipeline`, or `getChainContext` (out of scope). Deferred (by the user's Option-A choice): Option B (server-side deliverable-KIND eligibility catalogue) + Option C (typed feed-forward seed).
- **Verification.** gsd-quick (plan-checked PASS-WITH-CONCERNS, ZERO anchor drift; 3 concerns folded into the executor: preserve `setReplyPending(true)`, no workflow-name literal in `concierge.py`, stub+restore `scrollHeight` in the jsdom auto-grow test). Executor RED→GREEN both tasks. Offline gates: FE vitest 64 (RunChatLane + useRunChat), BE targeted 64 (concierge capability / chat endpoint / escalation / proposal channels), 5 characterization goldens 10/10 (`SNAPSHOT_UPDATE` unset), banned-pattern grep on `concierge.py` = 0 + `test_banned_patterns.py` green, lint-imports 4/0. **LIVE-PROVEN** on real Bedrock (orchestrator, fresh `user_stories` run `9bca8865`, Done 4m27s): 5/5 proofs — chips render + sit cleanly above the input; the input auto-grows to 4 lines; the Concierge answers "what can I do next?" by naming the Presentation + Prototype follow-up workflows; and BOTH `user_stories→prototype` + `user_stories→ppt` handoffs carry the `=== CONTEXT FROM PREVIOUS PIPELINE (user_stories) ===` block into the chained launch wizard (screenshots `chain-c72-0[1-5].png`). The reopen-from-history stale-`workflowType` risk did NOT manifest (chips present on reopen). Cosmetic observation (not a defect of this change): the Concierge paraphrased approximate deliverable counts (25 vs the actual 27 stories) — its general grounding behavior, orthogonal to chain-awareness. ## Quick 260811-mxg — `update_specs` prior-spec injection + resume planning-context rehydration + `:rev{N}` thread (FIX-217)

> **Commits `46fb310c` (RED tests) + `7badc86a` (D1+D3) + `7333f313` (D2) + `9f12051f` (verifier findings) + docs `f009c8e4` on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes the defect where the review gate's "Update the Specs" produced a from-scratch, SHORTER spec that then drove the planner and the finished prototype, with no UI signal. **Not data loss — a routing bug.** Diagnosed read-only from live run `6e38b9a7`; LIVE-PROVEN on Bedrock by a full incident reproduction (run `5ecb990f`).

- **What / Why (settled).** Three compounding defects on the in-run revision path. **D1 (primary, environment-independent):** `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` set only `ectx.spec_revision_context = analysis_report` (`engine.py:5054` pre-fix), and `_compose_context_message` rendered that with prose instructing the agent to *"Focus your output on fixing the identified issues rather than regenerating from scratch. Preserve unchanged sections."* — of a document never placed in the prompt. `prototype-specify` declares `consumes: []` AND `tools: []`, so it had neither a routing channel nor `read_file`; the instruction was literally unsatisfiable. **D2 (checkpointer-independent, hits Postgres too):** any resumed run took `skip_planner = … or _resuming` → `_default_planning_context` (`inferred_intent = user_message[:200]`, every list empty); the injected block collapsed **4,591 → 291 chars** across **16 of 18** dispatches (`kernel_services.py:189` stores the object once and hands the same one to every agent). The user's clarification answers live in `planning_context["explicit_constraints"]` and went with it. **D3 (why it surfaced only now):** the revision re-run reused the IDENTICAL checkpoint `thread_id` (log-proven `13:13:21` and `13:52:45` both `…:prototype-specify`), so the only thing that had EVER carried the prior spec into a revision was the LangGraph conversation — in-memory on sqlite, emptied by the restart. **Crucially, nothing was lost:** at compose time the process held spec v1 (43,670), the `planning_context` row (37,105) and the `clarifications` row (2,029) in `ectx.artifacts`, hydrated by `_hydrate_artifacts_from_store`. Three durable artifacts in the process's own graph, none routed into the prompt.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/agents/execution_engine/context.py`: two additive consume-once scratch fields `spec_revision_prior_artifact: str` and `revision_attempt: int`, joining the `redo_directive` / `spec_revision_context` / `steering_notes` family. `backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py`: (D1) `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` publishes the prior artifact from `_latest_typed_content(ectx, specify_spec.id)` for the specify sub-dispatch ONLY (object identity `sub_spec is specify_spec`, so plan/analyze cannot inherit it), rendered by `_compose_context_message` BEFORE the untouched analysis-report block, cleared in the existing `finally`; wired at BOTH `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` call sites — the live post-stream consumer and the RESUME-17 gate re-entry. (D2) new `_rehydrate_planning_context` rebuilds from the ALREADY-hydrated in-memory graph and re-merges every clarification round through the ONE existing `ClarifyEngine._merge_answers` (INV-12) — a pure read: **no new store call, no write, no migration, no new table or column**; gated on `_resuming` only. (D3) `revision_index` promoted from dead parameter to a live `:rev{N}` thread suffix, dormant at 0, and the false docstring claiming this already happened corrected. Tests: `backend/tests/agents/test_spec_revision_context.py` (new, 4) + `backend/tests/agents/test_restart_resume.py` (+7).
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **Do NOT fix D1 via `consumes`** — `_filter_consumed_outputs` breaks on `upstream.id == spec.id` and specify is `ordered_agents[0]`, so self-consumption is structurally impossible through that path; `_latest_typed_content` (filters by `producer_agent`) is the seam that works. **Do NOT give the spec writer filesystem tools instead** — `spec.md` is written by the build step's `task_loop` strategy and did not exist on disk until ~1h40m AFTER the revision pass needed it (verified by mtime), and a second on-disk copy would duplicate what `artifact_refs` already versions. **Do NOT re-run the planner on resume for D2** — that regresses BUG-R05 (quick `260719-hd5`) and reddens `test_offset0_gate_resume_does_not_replan_or_reclarify`; rehydrate, never re-invoke. That same BUG-R05 fix added artifact-graph hydration but NOT planning-context hydration — that asymmetry IS the gap closed here. F2 is gated on `_resuming` alone; `_replaying_clarify` is a deliberate, recorded exclusion (the two flags provably cannot co-occur). The import-time `ClarifyEngine as _ClarifyEngineImpl` bind is LOAD-BEARING — a late binding resolves through the `clarify_engine` module attribute the resume tests monkeypatch, silently yielding a resumed run with ZERO clarification answers; the existing lazy import at `engine.py:1924` must STAY (`_FakeClarify`/`_ParkingClarify` depend on it). No bare `except` around the merge (narrow `(AttributeError, TypeError, KeyError)`). Known lossiness, accepted: `_persist_qa` writes the raw responses BEFORE `_merge_answers` auto-fills `recommended_answer`, so SKIPPED questions cannot be reconstructed and `clarified_topics` returns empty — documented in the helper docstring; the alternative (persist the merged context on the clarify path) was rejected to honour "no new storage".
- **Verification.** gsd-quick VALIDATE (planner → plan-checker ×2 with one revision iteration → executor → verifier PASSED-WITH-CONCERNS 8/8 must-haves). 5 tests written FIRST and observed RED with verbatim output in `260811-mxg-BASELINE.md`; 2 more added to close verifier findings C1/C2 (malformed planner row raising `TypeError` out of the "never raises" helper — a crash path D2 itself created by becoming that row's first reader on resume; and the uncovered import-time bind), both proven RED/discriminating against the pre-fix engine. **Baseline re-measured independently in a detached worktree at the pre-change commit `edc44daa` rather than trusted:** goldens **5 failed / 5 passed with identical failing ids at both commits** (the remembered "10 failed / 6 passed" was stale `dev` data), lint-imports **3 kept / 1 broken at both** with `kernel imports only capability ports` KEPT, `test_restart_resume.py` same 7 reds with passed 41 → 48. Re-run identically after merging `origin/dev` (`84f4bbe3`). **LIVE-PROVEN on Bedrock** — run `5ecb990f`, full incident reproduction (launch → clarify → spec v1 → plan v1 → deliberate SIGTERM at the plan gate → resume → analyze → "Update the Specs"), with a planted `KESTREL` product-name sentinel as the analogue of the incident's "Spinnaker": spec **31,742 → 36,640 (+15.4%)**, **19 → 19 headings (0 lost)**, **97.6% verbatim carry-over**, sentinel **4× → 4×**, `task_list` **45,229 → 87,567 (+93.6%)**, run completed with a rendered deliverable — against the incident's 8 headings lost, "Spinnaker" 4× → 0×, 29.3% carry-over and a 10.4% shrink. Mechanism confirmed from `agent_input` events: the revision dispatch carries the prior spec AND a rich planning context, the exact inverse of incident seq 14357; `resume rehydrate:` logged *"1 clarification round(s) merged, 10 explicit constraint(s), 4634 chars of planner JSON (stub would have been 200 chars of intent)"*; thread ids `…:prototype-specify` vs `…:prototype-specify:rev1`. Record: `.planning/quick/260811-mxg-fix-update-specs-prior-spec-injection-an/` (PLAN/BASELINE/SUMMARY/VERIFICATION) + brief `.planning/BUGFIX-SPEC-REVISION-CONTEXT.md` + memory `update-specs-regenerates-spec`. **Carry-forward:** ISS-064..053 (silent no-op at the re-opened gate; nested-revision `:rev1` collision; the redundant double analyze gate; `update_specs_eligible` not server-enforced) — ISS-064/051 planned as quick `260811-si4`.

## Quick 260811-si4 — flat sibling revision cycles + an in-flight affordance fence + a re-entrant sub-pipeline (FIX-218)

> **Commits `30159b36` (RED tests) + `9be1b458` (engine fix) + the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Successor to FIX-217 / quick-`260811-mxg`; closes its carry-forward **ISS-064** and **ISS-051**. Brief: `.planning/BUGFIX-NESTED-REVISION.md`. Plan + baseline + RED evidence + post-change comparison + the deferred live-acceptance recipe: `.planning/quick/260811-si4-fix-nested-revision-thread-collision-and/`. New coverage: `backend/tests/agents/test_spec_revision_cycles.py`.

- **What / Why (settled).** Two `update_specs` defects, both offline-REPRODUCED before any fix. **Defect B (primary):** a second "Update the Specs", clicked at the analyze gate the engine RE-OPENS after a revision cycle, was a silent no-op — that third `_gate_update_specs` branch only re-seeded `spec_revision_pending_output` and `break`ed, so the gate closed, instantly re-opened on identical content and ran nothing, and the build then proceeded from the unrevised spec. Invisible on screen precisely because the FE sends the analyzer's OWN output as the report, so the re-opened gate looks unchanged. **Defect A:** a revision pass can re-enter itself, because the analyze re-run inside it is a full `_run_agent` that opens its own gate — and the gate ACTION is client-controlled. Both levels computed `revision_index == 1` from a per-`_run_agent` local and minted duplicate `:rev1` checkpoint threads (measured 7 dispatches / 4 unique ids), while the inner `finally` zeroed the outer pass's `revision_attempt` and `spec_revision_context` with the outer pass still on the stack.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/agents/execution_engine/context.py`: `spec_revision_context: str` PROMOTED from an undeclared attribute (it worked only because `ExecutionContext` is a non-slots dataclass) to a declared field; new `revision_high_water: int = 0`, a monotone per-run mark. `backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py`: (1) new `_update_specs_eligible(artifact_kind, ectx)` — one structural predicate replacing the expression inlined at all THREE gate call sites, adding `and not ectx.revision_attempt`; (2) `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` made re-entrant — the effective index derives from the high-water mark (`revision_index if it exceeds the mark else mark + 1`) and the `finally` RESTORES the three scratch fields instead of clearing them; (3) new `_consume_update_specs` — the ONE `_gate_update_specs` consumer, replacing two near-identical ~50-line copies and the broken stub, so exactly ONE `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` call site remains (net **-139 lines** in `engine.py`); (4) the re-open branch now drives that shared consumer, which IS the Defect-B fix. Tests: 5 new in `test_spec_revision_cycles.py`; `test_redo_gate_safety.py` gained `**kwargs` on its four `_fake_gate` stubs (test-only).
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **The brief's central premise was WRONG and was corrected with evidence — do not re-adopt it.** It claimed "Defect B's obvious fix is exactly what creates the depth-2 nesting Defect A is about", so A must be fixed first or B fixed some other way. Three probes disproved it: (i) nesting is ALREADY reachable today and does not depend on fixing B — the in-pass analyze gate advertised `update_specs_eligible=True`, so A is an independent live defect that option (ii) would have left untouched; (ii) wiring B creates NO nesting — the sub-pipeline's `finally` runs BEFORE its terminal `_revision_analyze_output` yield and the driving `async for` exhausts the generator before `break`ing, so `ectx.revision_attempt` is measurably back to 0 at the re-opened gate and the call is a SIBLING at the same stack depth (the REDO-GATE F2 flat-loop shape); (iii) withdrawing the affordance would have been dishonest — `engine.py` already documents the re-opened gate as existing so the user can "request another revision cycle", and a second cycle already ships and already runs one gate earlier. **Do NOT "tidy" the terminal `yield` into the `try`** — the `finally`-before-yield ordering is the entire reason the re-opened gate is a sibling and not a nested frame. **`revision_high_water` must NEVER be cleared or restored** — that is its whole job. **`_update_specs_eligible` is an ADVISORY affordance fence, not a server-side check** — `_run_review_gate` acts on `action == "update_specs"` without consulting it, so the engine is made correct for the nested case regardless (threat T-si4-01); a crafted or replayed POST now causes a redundant revision, never a corrupted one. **Deliberately NOT done, and left OPEN as ISS-052 / ISS-053:** collapsing the redundant double analyze gate (a behaviour change outside the brief, and it must NOT be driven off `ectx.revision_attempt` alone because the specify and plan gates also fire inside the pass and ARE wanted), and server-side ENFORCEMENT of the eligibility flag. Also out of scope and untouched: bounding the number of cycles (the redo loop is deliberately unbounded and this matches it), the frontend (`InlineGateActions.tsx:130` already drives the button purely from the server flag), and everything in `260811-mxg`.
- **Verification.** gsd-quick VALIDATE (planner → plan-checker with one revision iteration, VERIFICATION PASSED → executor). Four defect tests written FIRST and observed RED, verbatim output in `260811-si4-BASELINE.md`; the RED gate was strict — exactly 4 failed / 0 passed, REJECTING a pytest collection or fixture error as not-RED, because a swallowed stub error looks like a failing assertion from outside. Every predicted pre-fix reason matched: 4 dispatches instead of 7 with no `:rev2`; eligibility `[True, True, True]`; 7 thread ids of which only 4 unique. The fifth test (`single_cycle`) was GREEN before the engine change and after — dormancy at the test level, not only at the golden level. **INV-3 dormancy is machine-asserted, not eyeballed:** Task 1 wrote `GOLDENS-BASELINE` / `LINT-BASELINE` lines at `bf51a170` and Tasks 2 and 3 string-diffed against them (counts AND failing ids, so a swapped red cannot slip past) — goldens **5 failed / 5 passed** identical, lint-imports **3 kept / 1 broken** identical. Non-regression: `test_spec_revision_context.py` **4 passed** and `-k rehydrat` **7 passed**, so FIX-217 is intact. `test_redo_gate_safety.py` + `test_steering_seam.py` went **3 failed / 10 passed → 13 passed** — three regression guards, including the flat-stack guard this design leans on, had been DEAD since KAN-101 (a stale stub signature produced a silently-ZERO gate count because `_run_agent` swallows the `TypeError` into an `agent_error` event). `test_restart_resume.py` 7 failed / 48 passed and `tests/unit/test_execution_engine.py` 3 failed / 11 passed, both unchanged. Zero regressions; every non-passing test classified one-per-line in the baseline file. Structural gates: exactly 1 `_run_spec_revision_sub_pipeline` call site, 3 `_consume_update_specs` sites, 0 inlined eligibility expressions, 0 workflow-name or agent-id literals added, no migration, no new table/column/artifact kind, no frontend change. **Live Bedrock acceptance is DEFERRED** per the end-of-milestone rule; its recipe (the in-pass button must be ABSENT, the re-opened one PRESENT, cycle 2's threads must carry `:rev2`, and spec versions pulled via `GET /api/runs/{id}/artifacts` not the UI) is recorded in `260811-si4-BASELINE.md`.

## Quick 260812-12t — `update_specs` eligibility becomes BINDING: an engine fence + one shared ingress predicate (FIX-219)

> **Commit `82b5eb8c` (code + tests) + the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Successor to FIX-218 / quick-`260811-si4`; closes its carry-forward **ISS-053** and REVERSES its T-si4-01 accept-as-designed on evidence. Files **ISS-070** + **ISS-071**. Plan + measured baseline: `.planning/quick/260812-12t-fix-iss053-enforce-update-specs-eligibility/`. New coverage: `backend/tests/agents/test_update_specs_enforcement.py`, `backend/tests/unit/test_update_specs_ingress_fence.py`.

- **What / Why (settled).** `_update_specs_eligible` computed a verdict, `_run_review_gate` stamped it onto every `review_gate_ready`, the FE read it — and nothing ever read it back. The gate branched purely on the client-supplied `action` string, so a gate POST ran the spec-revision sub-pipeline at firings the rule excludes. It needed no crafting: `gate_key = f"{run_id}:{agent_id}"` names a gate SLOT, not a FIRING, so replaying a legitimate earlier click resolves whichever firing is armed now. **si4's premise that this is merely redundant was falsified three ways** — (i) at the two DEFAULT-gated agents the `index < 2` early-return revises nothing yet still blanks the agent's output and re-opens the gate empty, so every stock prototype run was exposed with zero configuration; (ii) at a build/validate gate one POST re-runs the build (~$3.68 vs ~$0.03, and there is no rate limiting anywhere in the API layer); (iii) it already happened live on run `d5dbc9f2` — gate advertised `eligible=0`, action accepted 6.05s later.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py`: `_run_review_gate`'s wait/dispatch tail moved inside a `while True:` so ONE firing can consume more than one response; an ineligible `update_specs` logs, `event.clear()`s and continues — the gate KEEPS WAITING. `backend/app/api/run_engine.py`: new `_review_gate_advertises_update_specs(gate_key)` beside the owner/terminal fences (same `_get_db` + direct-ORM idiom), reading the highest-`seq` `review_gate_ready` payload back. `backend/app/api/run_commands.py`: new `_deny_update_specs_not_offered` 409 helper called from ALL THREE `set_review_response` ingresses — `resolve_gate`, the `CHANNEL_GATE` route in `post_message`, and `_dispose_concierge_proposal`. `backend/agents/capabilities/gates/{human,approval}.py`: `_UPDATE_SPECS` consumed alongside `_REDO`, `redo_seen` renamed `unwired_action_seen`.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **The degrade is KEEP WAITING — never approve, never reject.** Approving is fail-open on a HITL gate (exactly what the Phase-23 F1a redo defence exists to prevent, and against WR-07's fail-closed rule); rejecting would cancel the user's run, a semantic change nobody asked for. **The RULE lives in exactly one place, `_update_specs_eligible`** — the engine layer reads the parameter that helper produced, the ingress layer reads the value it published; neither restates it, so changing the rule changes both layers and no third copy can drift (INV-3/INV-12). **The ingress predicate MUST abstain, never fabricate a denial**, when the durable log cannot answer (no row — event persistence is best-effort; a different gate_key; a pre-KAN-101 payload): a fabricated denial would 409 a LEGITIMATE revision whenever a durable write degraded. That abstention is only safe because the engine layer never abstains — the two properties are load-bearing for each other, so do not "tighten" the predicate to deny on unknown. **The predicate must read the HIGHEST-seq ready row**, because the same `gate_key` fires repeatedly with different verdicts. **si4's nesting safety (`revision_high_water`, the restoring `finally`) is RETAINED and still tested** as defence in depth, not deleted — it is what keeps the engine correct if a future call site ever passes the flag wrongly; `test_nested_revision_keeps_distinct_threads_and_restores_the_outer_pass` stubs the gate out and so still reaches it. **Deliberately NOT done, and filed rather than smuggled in:** the unknown-action fail-open + unvalidated `GateCommand.action`/`analysis_report` (**ISS-070** — note that fix is not purely additive, a lenient client would start getting 422s), and the over-broad advertisement on non-prototype workflows where `_artifact_kind_for`'s `summary` fallback makes every gate eligible (**ISS-071** — explicitly rejected as the fix for ISS-053, since narrowing the advertisement changes nothing about enforcement).
- **Verification.** 18 tests written FIRST and observed RED with verbatim output — engine file 4 failed / 1 passed → 5 passed, ingress file 3 failed / 10 passed → 13 passed. The single pre-fix pass in each file is deliberate: they are the DORMANCY guards (green before AND after), which is how INV-3 was proven here, **because the goldens are structurally blind to this change** — all 10 golden files contain ZERO `review_gate_ready` events (the harness runs `gate_agent_ids=[]`, `_scripted_model.py:649`), so INV-3 could NOT be argued from golden dormancy. Goldens **5 failed / 5 passed with identical failing ids** and lint-imports **3 kept / 1 broken**, both compared against the pre-change commit `d62bfe4d`; no golden regenerated. Adjacent suites re-measured in a **detached worktree at `d62bfe4d`** rather than assumed: sweep A 10 failed / 159 passed before AND after (diff showed only the elapsed-time line), sweep B 10 failed / 83 → 101 passed with the same ids, the +18 being exactly this fix's new tests. The reachability proof is `test_three_gate_vector_is_enforced_and_leaves_a_second_cycle_reachable`: it HARVESTS the eligibility values the engine actually computes at the outer / in-pass / re-opened analyze gates and feeds each into the REAL `_run_review_gate`, asserting **honored / REFUSED / honored** — so enforcement provably does not make a second revision cycle unreachable. Live Bedrock acceptance DEFERRED per the end-of-milestone rule.
- **Correction to the register (evidence, not opinion).** **ISS-062 is a MISDIAGNOSIS.** Its row claims run `d5dbc9f2` seq 20360 is the RE-OPENED analyze gate advertising `eligible=False`, making FIX-218's fence an over-firing regression. Re-queried read-only against `backend/dev.db`: seq **20359 is `agent_complete` for `prototype-analyze`**, immediately before that gate — so 20360 is the **IN-PASS** gate, where `False` is FIX-218's intended behaviour, and seq 20362 is `agent_start prototype-specify`, i.e. the second `update_specs` started another pass. That run never reached a re-opened analyze gate at all. The `True/False/True` vector is independently re-confirmed green at `d62bfe4d` by `test_update_specs_not_offered_while_a_revision_is_in_flight` and again by this fix's vector test. **Do NOT change `_update_specs_eligible`'s rule to "fix" ISS-062** — that re-opens the nesting recursion ISS-051 closed. The ISS-062 row itself was left untouched (another workstream owns it).

## Quick 260812-1nz — the doubled analyze gate becomes identifiable: a per-FIRING revision stamp (FIX-220)

> **Commit `1b786e30` (code + tests) + the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Successor to FIX-219 / quick-`260812-12t`. Closes the **disambiguation half of ISS-052** and carries the valid substance of **ISS-062** (closed as a misdiagnosis, whose real complaint was that the two firings are indistinguishable while carrying opposite affordances). Hands **ISS-063** the durable per-cycle signal it needs. Files **ISS-072** (the deferred collapse), **ISS-073**, **ISS-074**. Plan + baseline: `.planning/quick/260812-1nz-fix-iss-052-disambiguate-the-doubled-ana/`. New coverage: `backend/tests/agents/test_gate_revision_discriminator.py`.

- **What / Why (settled).** One "Update the Specs" click opens the analyze gate THREE times — `[0]` outer, `[1]` the analyze re-run INSIDE the sub-pipeline, `[2]` the gate re-opened once the pass returns — and **nothing on the wire told `[1]` from `[2]`**. `gate_key` is `f"{run_id}:{agent_id}"`: it names a gate SLOT, not a FIRING, so the two arrived with the same key AND byte-identical output (live `5ecb990f` seq 24652/24655 — 11,974 chars, sha1 `0136795fc392`, 5 ms apart, zero events between) while carrying OPPOSITE affordances (`update_specs_eligible` False vs True). Cost: one apparently-ignored Approve, 84 s of live user hesitation on the duplicate, and a wrong `major` issue (ISS-062). **Root cause is a modelling gap, not a mechanism:** the sub-pipeline was designed HEADLESS — its own comment says the review gate "is not expected during a revision cycle" (`engine.py:5310-5313`) — and the re-open step exists precisely to give the user the review the pass would not provide. But the pass re-runs each agent through the full `_run_agent` path for behaviour reuse (INV-12), so every one of them DOES gate; the re-open re-presents a review that already happened, and the event vocabulary had no field distinguishing a firing from a slot. **Second, untested harm found by the investigation and fixed here:** `InlineGateActions` reset its one-action `submitted` latch on `[output, gateKey]` — NEITHER changes between `[1]` and `[2]` — so the re-opened gate rendered with every action disabled.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/agents/execution_engine/engine.py`: `_run_review_gate` gains `revision_cycle: int = 0` + `revision_in_flight: bool = False` and stamps both onto `review_gate_ready.data`; ONE new resolver `_revision_stamp(ectx) -> (int, bool)` sits beside `_update_specs_eligible` and is called at the THREE inline gate sites (`:3363` restart re-entry, `:3487` pending re-open, `:4385` live post-stream). Values come from scratch that already exists — `revision_high_water` (monotone, never restored, so it still names the cycle after the pass unwinds) and `revision_attempt` (non-zero for exactly the pass's duration). `backend/tests/agents/characterization/_normalize.py`: both keys added to `_VOLATILE_STRIP_KEYS`. Frontend, all additive: `types/index.ts` (`ReviewGateReadyData`), `app/dashboard/page.tsx` (two local decls + the `gateData` map), `hooks/useRunStateStore.ts`, `components/layout/DashboardLayout.tsx` (prop type, `GateContext` map, and the approve-label correction), `components/chat/RunChatLane.tsx` (the exported `GateContext`), `components/results/StepsOverviewSpine.tsx` (pass-through), `components/chat/InlineGateActions.tsx` (props, the reset-effect dependency array, and a `chat-gate-revision` badge). Tests: 6 new in `test_gate_revision_discriminator.py`, 2 new in `InlineGateActions.test.tsx`, `**kwargs` added to three `_gate` stubs in `test_restart_resume.py` and two recorded fields to the `_drive_cycles` harness (test-only).
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **BOTH keys are required — do not "simplify" to one.** `revision_cycle` alone cannot separate `[1]` from `[2]` (both are cycle 1); `revision_in_flight` alone cannot separate `[0]` from `[2]`. The PAIR is the identifier, and the FE latch depends on it. **Do NOT suppress `[2]`** — it is the only `update_specs_eligible=True` firing, so removing it deletes the sole entry to a second cycle and regresses ISS-064, closed the same day. **The genuinely redundant firing is `[1]`, which INVERTS ISS-052's own text**; suppressing it is a different, larger change with its own brief (**ISS-072**) because it rewrites six assertions in `test_spec_revision_cycles.py`, forces deletion of condition 2 of `_update_specs_eligible` by INV-12, and must resolve the empty-analysis backstop. **NEVER dedupe on the frontend** ("same gate_key + same output"): it converts a redundant gate into a HANG — the engine is still blocked on `event.wait()` and swallowing the frame removes the only UI that can resolve it — and it would eat legitimate restart-resume re-opens, whose signature is identical (live-proven at `5ecb990f` 8402/8406 and `d5dbc9f2` 24788/24792, each preceded by `workflow_validated` + `pipeline_start`). **The key names are deliberately NOT `revision_index` / `spec_revision_attempt`:** `chat_narrator._revision_index` (`:106-118`) reads those two and would have silently turned every in-revision gate card into a "Revising spec — cycle N" card. Verified by reading, not assumed. **The declared/user gate path keeps the `(0, False)` default** exactly as it keeps `redoable=False` — `run_human_gate` passes neither key, and a declared gate is not inside a revision pass, so the default is truthful AND renders no badge. **INV-3 could NOT be argued from the goldens** — all 10 golden files contain ZERO `review_gate_ready` events (`gate_agent_ids=[]`, `_scripted_model.py:649`), so golden silence proves nothing about a `_run_review_gate` change; it is proven by the strip-set guard and the dormancy defaults instead. **ISS-063 must CONSUME `revision_cycle`**, not invent a third counter — `dashboard/page.tsx:357` holds `specRevisionCount` in `useState(0)`, incremented only from a live FE-armed inference and never back-filled; the server field is on the durable `run_events` log and survives a reopen (SSE re-emits `payload_json` verbatim, `run_stream.py:244`).
- **Verification.** 6 backend tests written FIRST and observed RED — 6 failed → 6 passed, each failing for its OWN reason (stamp vector `[(None,None)×3]`, cycle vector `[None×5]`, `TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'revision_cycle'`, "expected a 0 default; got None", "never appears in engine.py", and the missing strip-set entry) rather than one shared import error. 2 frontend tests likewise seen red first; the load-bearing one covers the latch hole the investigation flagged as untested. Goldens **5 failed / 5 passed with identical failing ids** and lint-imports **3 kept / 1 broken**, both compared against the pre-change commit `28c0111c`; no golden regenerated and `git status` on `characterization/golden/` clean. Adjacent suites measured in a **detached worktree at `28c0111c`**, both sides: ISS-053 set 32 passed; engine-adjacent (redo_gate_safety, steering_seam, restart_resume, spec_revision_context, execution_engine) **10 failed / 76 passed** before AND after; wider gate surface (11 files) **8 failed / 92 passed** before AND after; full frontend vitest **147 failed / 779 passed → 147 failed / 781 passed** (same 29 red files, +2 = exactly this fix's new cases); `tsc --noEmit` identical 2 pre-existing errors. **A mid-work regression was caught by that baselining, not by luck:** the first engine-adjacent sweep read 17 failed / 69 passed (+7) because three `_gate` stubs in `test_restart_resume.py` have FIXED signatures and raised `TypeError` on the new kwargs; given `**kwargs` — the idiom the sibling stubs already document — the sweep returned to 10 / 76. Live Bedrock acceptance DEFERRED per the end-of-milestone rule; the check is one query (the run's `review_gate_ready` rows must read `(0,f)/(N,t)/(N,f)`). **Deliberately NOT fixed, and filed rather than smuggled in:** the chat-lane milestone card still reads "Paused — needs approval" for both firings (`chat_narrator.py:171-173`; the data to disambiguate now rides the event, so it is a pure render follow-up — recorded on the ISS-052 row); a stale FE test proven pre-existing at `28c0111c` (**ISS-073**); and the live harness's review-gate wrapper, whose 4-positional signature cannot absorb the gate's own kwargs and has been broken since REDO-GATE (**ISS-074** — two tokens to fix, but unverifiable offline).

## Quick 260812-2ci — a revision becomes visible while it happens, and afterwards (FIX-221 + FIX-222)

> **Commits `6e9baff5` (FIX-221) + `2ab7c56b` (FIX-222), code + tests, plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-063** and **ISS-065**. Successor to FIX-220 / quick-`260812-1nz`. **Frontend-only: zero backend files, zero new event types, alembic head stays 0030.**

- **What / Why (settled).** Two rows, one defect family: *a revision happened and the screen does not say so*. **ISS-063** — the violet "Spec Revision Cycle N" banner was not merely absent on reload as filed; it was **dead on every path** for `od_prototype` since `219702a4` (2026-08-03), because FIX-164's arming predicate required every agent `"done"` while still `isRunning` and the update_specs gate sits at agent 2 of 5. **ISS-065** — `artifact_refs` versions every artifact and the REST route already returns each version with its body, but no UI consumed it, while `useWorkflow.ts` clears an agent's `output` on every `agent_start` (FIX-039), so an update_specs cycle destroys the only in-memory copy of the earlier spec. **They were fixed as ONE change on purpose:** they share the design decision (*revision visibility derives from durable state, never from live-session state*), they validate each other (`max(spec.version) - 1 == specRevisionCount`, now a test assertion), and this family had already produced a dead counter **twice** — sequencing them was the identified path to a third.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/types/index.ts`: `PipelineRunState.agentStartCounts?: Record<string, number>`. `frontend/src/hooks/useWorkflow.ts`: the `agent_start` case increments that map **inside the existing `setPipelineState` updater** (reading `prev`, never a ref), the `pipeline_start` case **carries** it when the frame names the same run, and a new exported `deriveSpecRevisionCount(counts)` holds the one derivation rule. `frontend/src/hooks/useRunStateStore.ts`: `handleFrame` writes `entry.specRevisionCount` — the single writer — into the field that had existed dead at `:81`/`:170` since the store was built. `frontend/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`: the detector, its two refs, the setter ref, the `useState` and the arm effect are **deleted**; the banner prop now reads `runStore.viewed.specRevisionCount`. `frontend/src/components/results/ArtifactVersionPicker.tsx` (NEW, ~250 lines incl. docs) mounts in the `AgentDetailPanel` card header; the panel gains an optional `runId`, a `viewed` state, and renders `viewed?.content ?? agent.output`; `AgentThinkingTab` passes the `runId` it already computed.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **(1) The banner's cycle count is derived from the EVENT STREAM, not from FIX-220's `revision_cycle`.** Both were live candidates and the choice was made on measurement, not taste: FIX-220's pair rides **only** on `review_gate_ready`, and the durable log of run `d5dbc9f2` shows the revision beginning at seq 9285 (20:54:51) with the next gate frame not arriving until seq 13353 (20:56:25) — a **94-second window with no gate event at all**, which is precisely the window the banner exists to cover. It also lives on `ReviewGateData`, which is per-firing and replaced. FIX-220 is untouched and keeps its own, different job (telling apart three gate firings that share a `gate_key` *and* their output bytes, on the gate card). **Two facts, two surfaces, one writer each — `specRevisionCount` has exactly one writer.** **(2) A `pipeline_start` naming the SAME run must CARRY `agentStartCounts`, not rebuild it** — the trailing resume frame lands last on every replay and rebuilding there is what zeroed the counter before. **(3) Artifact versions dedupe by `content_hash`, never by `(kind, version)`** — every artifact is written twice (typed kind + `produces` alias) and the two series do NOT stay in lockstep: `html_file` reaches v23 while `prototype-build` reaches v11 on a real run. Accepted consequence: byte-identical re-runs collapse to one entry. **(4) Artifact content is fetched lazily on click and memoised per kind** — `?kind=html_file&include=content` was measured at **2.89 MB** against the live backend; the list call is ~22 KB. **(5) `resp.artifacts ?? []` is load-bearing, not habit** — `e2e/fixtures/mockApi.ts:708` answers every unmatched `/api/**` with `json({})`, so without it the protected mocked suite throws a TypeError on every agent-detail open. **(6) The picker returns `null` at ≤ 1 version**, which is what keeps the blast radius at zero for every un-revised run, the fidelity captures and the e2e suite. **(7) Do NOT put artifact versions on the run-header "Version" chip** — that is the run-FAMILY axis under locked decision **D2** (`:2531`), and `handleSelectVersion` calls `getWorkflow(memberId)`, so an artifact-ref id would 404 into a dead control and corrupt the state behind `FilesTab` and `StartingPointCard`. **(8) The `ReadOnlyVersionBanner` is REUSED, not re-implemented** (INV-12).
- **Verification.** 27 frontend tests written FIRST and observed RED as one run with verbatim output — **4 files failed, 18 failed / 1 passed** → **4 files passed, 27 passed**. (19 → 27 because `ArtifactVersionPicker.test.tsx` could not even load before the fix; the single green-at-red case is the deliberate no-regression guard "renders no picker without a `runId`".) Full frontend vitest compared **by failing test ID**, not by count: 928 → 955 tests, 781 → 808 passed, **147 failed both sides with a byte-identical failing-ID set — 0 new reds**. Mocked Playwright compared the same way against a **properly isolated** baseline at `b13d5c33` (own Next server on `:3100`): 33 failed → 31 failed, the after-set a strict **subset** of baseline, **0 new failures**. Goldens **5 failed / 5 passed** and `lint-imports` **3 kept / 1 broken**, both identical to `b13d5c33` and re-measured after the change. `tsc --noEmit`: 2 errors, both pre-existing in files this change never opened. Retired palette: 0 hits across every changed file. Live Bedrock acceptance **DEFERRED** (end-of-milestone rule) — the browser check is: reopen `d5dbc9f2`, expect "Spec Revision Cycle 2" on the Steps spine and a `spec · v3 of 3` picker in the Spec Writer detail.
- **Method note worth more than the counts (now ISS-076).** `playwright.config.ts` sets `reuseExistingServer: true` on `:3000`, so running the mocked suite from a baseline worktree **silently tests the main tree's code** through the already-running dev server and returns a confirmatory answer regardless of the commit checked out. That nearly produced a false "pre-existing" verdict here; the first `ts-u` baseline taken this way was discarded. A real baseline needs its own server on another port, and a **symlinked `node_modules` will not work** (Turbopack: *"Symlink [project]/node_modules is invalid, it points out of the filesystem root"*) — clone it with `cp -Rc` (~6 s on APFS).
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-075** (major) the trailing resume `pipeline_start` carries `resume_offset = 0`, so reopening a run should repaint the whole Steps trace as idle — confirmed in code and data, **not yet observed on screen**, and arguably more serious than the banner defect it was found beside. **ISS-076** (major) the mocked Playwright suite's real baseline on this branch is 33 red, not the "132 green" the records claim, plus the `reuseExistingServer` trap above. **ISS-077** (minor) `ArtifactNode`'s declaration disagrees with the wire on `derived_from` / `children` / `task_id`; nothing reads them today, so it is latent. The build agent's ~12-entry version list was raised as a readability risk during investigation and is **handled in-line** by a `max-h-[280px] overflow-y-auto` scroll cap on the listbox — the fix the investigation itself recommended, and explicitly **not** a workflow-name or agent-id special case (SC-001).

## Quick 260812-35u — the golden oracle becomes an oracle again, and the import contract is restored (FIX-223 + FIX-224)

> **Commits `8394af13` (FIX-223 C1+C2) + `a52c53ff` (FIX-224) + `a6b2097e` (FIX-223 C3, the golden regeneration, deliberately its OWN revertable commit), plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-068**. Successor to FIX-221/222 / quick-`260812-2ci`. **Goldens 5 failed/5 passed → 10 passed/0 failed; lint-imports 3 kept/1 broken → 4 kept/0 broken.** Alembic head stays 0030; zero frontend files.

- **What / Why (settled).** The 5 characterization event goldens are this project's **INV-3 parity oracle**, and all 5 had been red on `dev` for weeks — so INV-3 could only be checked by diffing failure counts against a hand-captured baseline instead of by a clean green run. The whole risk of this task was that **regenerating a golden to match current behaviour, when the code is what is wrong, permanently pins a regression as expected behaviour.** So the 5 failures were decomposed first: they reduce to exactly **3 causes** (proven exhaustive by counterfactual — undoing all 3 makes every one of the 5 files byte-identical), and each was adjudicated **on its own evidence** per the **ISS-029** method, which had resolved this exact situation once before and explicitly **REJECTED regen-only**. Verdicts: **1 stale normalizer, 1 real code regression, 1 genuinely stale golden.** Four of the five files had no problem of their own at all.
- **C1 — stale NORMALIZER (all 5 goldens); neither golden nor engine wrong.** `c71f3d9c` added an additive `pipeline_start.resume_offset` so the FE can mark already-completed agents done on resume. It is 0 on every non-resumed run and the harness never resumes — but **a key whose value is 0 is still a NEW key**, and the snapshot compares whole canonical-JSON dicts, so all 5 went red. The emit-site comment (`engine.py:2049`) asserts *"0 on every normal run → byte/event-identical (INV-3)"*, which is **false as written and is what misled the author**. Fixed the project's way: added to `_VOLATILE_STRIP_KEYS` in `tests/agents/characterization/_normalize.py` — the **7th** instance of a 6-precedent convention (`deliverable_mimetype`/`deliverable_filename`, `redoable`/`update_specs_eligible`/`artifact_kind`, `revision_cycle`/`revision_in_flight`, the `cache_*` quartet, `image_count`, `message_id`/`replayed_through_seq`). Safe because `_REQUIRED_DATA_KEYS` has **no `pipeline_start` entry at all** (verified at `test_phase3_cutover_verify.py:258-271`), so stripping cannot weaken the required-keys assertion, and resume-offset behaviour is pinned directly by `test_restart_resume.py`. **Zero golden bytes touched.**
- **C2 — a REAL REGRESSION; the golden was RIGHT (`prototype`, `od_prototype`).** `f608e4bc` (FIX-190, ISS-056) appended an `accessibility` guardrail to 4 prototype-family agents. In three of them the `+` line was a pure insertion (`1 +` in `--stat`); in `prototype-build/AGENT.md` it is `2 +-` — **the `+` line landed ON TOP OF `icon: "🏗️"`**, deleting it, so the agent fell through to `loader.py`'s `🤖` default and changed the icon in `pipeline_start.agents[]` and both `agent_start`s. `icon` is **contractual** — it is in `_REQUIRED_DATA_KEYS["agent_start"]`. Corroborating sweep, run independently: **86** `AGENT.md` files, **exactly 1** without an `icon:` — that one. That is a deletion, not a design decision. Restored **byte-identical** to the pre-clobber line (diffed against `f608e4bc^`). **Zero golden bytes touched.** Note the commit message's own INV-3 claim (*"H2 safe (ScriptedFakeChatModel is call-index keyed, not content-keyed)"*) was reasoned but wrong: the reasoning covered the guardrail text, not the frontmatter it clobbered.

Adjudicated rather than assumed: whether `planner: skip` might itself be the regression was probed — it is not (it fixes a real CR-02 defect, matches the already-live `ppt_revision` / `od_ppt_revision` siblings, and the manifest documents the reasoning inline), so the verdict stands.
- **Sequencing was load-bearing, not bureaucratic.** C3 was regenerated **strictly after C1**: had it gone first, `resume_offset: 0` would have been **baked permanently into the file**, coupling one of the five goldens to an FE metadata key and diverging it from the other four. It was also done after the branch's queued engine fixes (FIX-219 `82b5eb8c`, FIX-220 `1b786e30`) had landed, so the regeneration cannot silently absorb an unintended event-stream change from them.

A sweep confirmed it was the **only** violation in the whole capability tree. (2) `test_banned_patterns.py::test_capabilities_do_not_import_kernel_or_web_layer` puts the import-linter contract into **pytest**, with a non-vacuity guard that replays the exact ISS-068 statements and a false-positive guard for comments / sibling capability imports / `app`-prefixed third-party modules. That second gap is precisely **why a one-line violation survived ~3 weeks**: `lint-imports` is a separate binary that must be invoked from `backend/`, and **from the repo root it prints "Could not read any configuration" and exits, which reads as a pass.**

['prototype-build']`, the boundary pin naming `task_loop.py:572` (proven by temporarily reverting the fix and restoring it byte-exactly, sha256-verified; **never `git stash`**). The 3-cause decomposition was confirmed independently by watching the count move per cause: **5F/5P → 3F/7P** (C1) **→ 1F/9P** (C2) **→ 10 passed** (C3). `lint-imports` 3 kept/1 broken → **4 kept/0 broken**. `test_restart_resume.py` **unchanged at 7 failed / 48 passed, same 7 ids**, before and after.
