## Quick 260812-4ss — the revision count becomes identity-keyed and head-scoped; the reopen roster merges (FIX-225)

> **Commit `c46c8160` (code + tests) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-080**, **ISS-081** and **ISS-075**. Successor to FIX-223/224 / quick-`260812-35u`. **Frontend-only: zero backend files, zero new event types, goldens unmoved at 10/10, lint-imports unmoved at 4 kept / 0 broken.**

- **What / Why (settled).** Three defects, ONE change, because two of them live in the same expression and fixing any one alone still leaves a wrong number on the screen. The reopened-run screen showed **"Spec Revision Cycle 5"** for a run with **2** revisions and **"0 / 5 agents"** for a run whose first three agents had all completed — and the idle roster is what made FIX-222's just-shipped version picker unreachable, because `StepsOverviewSpine.tsx:315-316,330-331` renders an idle row as a `disabled` button.
- **The one root cause under all three: a MISSING CONCEPT.** The FE had no predicate for *"this `pipeline_start` re-announces the run I am already showing"*. FIX-221 introduced that test for exactly one field (`useWorkflow.ts:306-309`) instead of promoting it, so the same trailing frame still (a) wiped the event-id dedup seen-set and (b) rebuilt the agent roster. Two of the three sites that needed it were still wrong.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/types/index.ts`: `agentStartCounts?: Record<string, number>` is **REPLACED** by `agentStartEventIds?: Record<string, string[]>` (INV-12 — replaced, not shadowed; zero references to the old name remain). `frontend/src/hooks/useWorkflow.ts`: `deriveSpecRevisionCount` now takes the pipeline state and reads the HEAD agent's entry; a module-private `frameIdentity(msg, positionKey)` resolves `event_id` → `seq` → `unstamped:<n>`; the whole `pipeline_start` roster build moved **inside** the `setPipelineState` updater so it can see `prev`. `frontend/src/hooks/useRunStateStore.ts:424` — still the ONE writer, now passed `entry.pipelineState`. `frontend/src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — `resetReplayState` is gated on the page-side twin of the same predicate.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **(1) The count is keyed on a SET of event identities, never a tally.** The `artifact_refs`-derived alternative (`max(spec.version) - 1`) was considered and REJECTED: it needs an extra REST call, does not exist while the first revision is mid-flight, and requires the UI to know which artifact `kind` is "the spec" — a workflow-specific literal that breaks SC-001/INV-1. It stays what it already was: a cross-check oracle in the test file. **(2) The revision head is POSITIONAL — `state.agents[0]`, the first step of the compiled roster.** Hardcoding `prototype-specify` would be a workflow-name branch and is forbidden. Accepted limitation, recorded not hidden: a workflow whose revision window excludes step 0 under-reports (banner hidden) rather than over-reporting. **(3) The engine is NOT touched.** `resume_offset` has an engine meaning (`_first_incomplete_step`); changing it or adding a field to `pipeline_start` would perturb the characterization goldens FIX-223/224 had only just restored to 10/10. **(4) Only `resetReplayState` is skipped on a same-run frame** — the four sibling clears (`reviewGateData`, `questionnaireData`, `activePipelineRunId`, `lastCancelledRunId`) are still wanted on a genuine resume and deliberately keep running. **(5) The page-side predicate is captured BEFORE the launch-window block re-points `trackedRunIdRef`** — read after that assignment, a fresh launch would misread as "same run" and skip the reset it needs.
- **The test gap was the real defect.** All 15 FIX-221 cases called `runFrames(REAL_FRAMES)` **exactly once**: they varied frame ORDER but never frame MULTIPLICITY — and multiplicity is precisely what a history reopen produces. That is how a fix with 15 green tests still over-counted in a live browser. TEST-009 adds 12 cases; the fixtures now carry the `event_id`/`seq` every real frame has, because an un-stamped fixture cannot express a re-delivery at all. Generalised rule worth adopting repo-wide: **any reducer field that accumulates must have a test that replays its input twice** (now filed as ISS-082 for the two siblings).
- **Verification.** Every new case seen **RED first** with verbatim output — 5 / 8 / `{specify:6, plan:4, analyze:4}` (ISS-080), 10 / 21 / 10 (ISS-081), empty done-list / `completedCount 0` / demoted second agent (ISS-075) — then 21/21 green in the file and 79/79 across the reducer + replay blast radius. Full frontend vitest **147 red before and after**, same 29 files, and `comm` over the sorted failing-id sets shows **zero** new reds and zero coincidental fixes (+12 passing = exactly the new cases). `tsc --noEmit`: 2 errors, both in files this change never touched. Goldens 10/10 and lint-imports 4 kept / 0 broken, both identical to the pre-change commit `f353a1a9`.
- **Live proof, not just unit tests** (the whole point — unit tests are what missed this). Run `d5dbc9f2` reopened from Run History on a fresh load, real backend on `:8010`: banner **"Spec Revision Cycle 2"**, header **"3 / 5 agents"**, specify/plan/analyze rows navigable with real durations and token counts, build/validate correctly still disabled. `scratchpad/verify-4ss-after-02-steps.png` against the pre-fix `live-04-steps.png` is a same-screen before/after pair.
- **The investigation's one open question is now ANSWERED.** REOPEN-REPLAY-ANALYSIS §1.5 could not reconcile "blocking the REST fetch removes the doubling" with `page.tsx:837-841,892` saying REST-replayed `agent_*` frames cannot reach the store. Both are true. The inner `frameRunId` const shadows the function parameter and IS `undefined` for those frames, so the store dispatch at `:892` is skipped — but `isForActiveRun` at `:875` is true *for that same reason*, so `handlePipelineMsgRef` at `:897` DOES apply them to `useWorkflow.pipelineState`; the FIX-201 bridge effect at `page.tsx:1640-1649` then copies that whole state object into the store (`runStore.updatePipelineState(runId, () => pipelineState)`), and the SSE pass increments on top of the copied base. That is the transfer step. There is no third delivery path.
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-082** (minor) the sibling accumulators `agent_chunk` (`output + chunk`) and `hookRuns` (`push`) carry no identity key either and are now protected only by the class-level seen-set fix — an external guarantee, the exact arrangement that failed for ISS-080. **ISS-083** (trivial) `ResultCard.tsx:97-100,119` renders `Revising spec — cycle {cycle ?? 1}` and nothing passes `cycle` — a third, dormant counter in this family; wire it from `runStore.viewed.specRevisionCount` rather than reintroducing a local count.
- **Sibling defused by construction, worth knowing.** `page.tsx:2054-2063` (`handleSwitchToLiveRun`'s deliberately un-deduped direct store replay) was flagged as a likely live-path twin of ISS-080, because its `hasLiveAgents` guard is defeated by ISS-075's all-idle roster. Both halves of that are now gone: the roster merge restores the guard, and the identity-keyed counter makes an un-deduped replay harmless (the frames carry `event_id`, merged onto the payload by `lib/api.ts`).

## Quick 260812-77g — the artifact-version picker moves the WHOLE agent panel, not just the raw output (FIX-226)

> **Commit `e92a9ad0` (code + tests) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-085**. Frontend-only; the backend tree is byte-identical to the pre-change commit `a48965a5`, so goldens 10/10 and lint-imports 4 kept / 0 broken are unchanged by construction, not by sampling.

- **What / Why (settled).** FIX-222 shipped the per-artifact version picker (ISS-065) and it half-worked: choosing v1 repainted the raw "Agent output" section but left the PROMINENT card — "Specification · N pages", "Governance checks" — rendering the newest version. The owner selected v1, saw v3's page grid, and reported *"while changing the version there, i couldnt see the older version's content"*. Nothing was broken about the picker; the panel simply had two answers to one question.
- **The root cause: one screen, two notions of "what am I looking at".** `AgentDetailPanel` computed `shownOutput = viewed?.content ?? agent.output` and passed it to exactly ONE of four consumers (`OutputPreviewSection`). The other three went back to the agent for the same information — `parseSpecSections(agent.output)`, `parseSpecOverview(agent.output)`, `<AnalysisPreview content={agent.output}/>` — because `SettledArtifactCards` was handed the raw `agent`. This is the same shape as FIX-225's "two accumulators, one truth" (INV-12), not a missing feature.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/components/results/AgentDetailPanel.tsx`. `displayed = viewed ? { ...agent, output: viewed.content } : agent` is **the** source; `shownOutput` derives FROM it, so the two names provably cannot disagree. `deriveArtifactCardModel(displayed, …)`, `<SettledArtifactCards output={shownOutput} …>`, `<OutputPreviewSection output={shownOutput} />`. `SettledArtifactCards`' `agent: AgentRunState` prop is **REPLACED** by `output: string` — it is now structurally unable to reach the latest output again, which is the part that makes the fix stick. It is a module-local component with no external caller, so the exported `deriveArtifactCardModel` signature is untouched and the 42-09 card tests needed no edit.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **(1) `discriminateArtifact` DOES follow the selection.** It chooses which renderer draws the content, and an artifact's type is a property of THAT artifact, not of the agent. Pinning it to the latest routes an older version of a different shape through the wrong renderer — and, whenever FIX-039 has cleared `agent.output` for a re-running agent, suppresses the card entirely at exactly the moment ISS-065 exists to serve. **(2) Three inputs stay pinned to the agent, deliberately:** `validationPassed`/`validationIssues`, `protoCompletedTasks`, `dagEdges` — run/agent state that is not versioned anywhere in the FE. Following the selection there would mean inventing data; filed as **ISS-087** instead. **(3) The `(live)` reasoning card keeps reading `agent.output`** — it is labelled live, and pinning it to an older version would leave no way to watch the re-run it announces. All three boundaries are stated in-line so a later reader does not "fix" them.
- **Do NOT fix this class by hiding the cards.** The cards are the information the user came for; the requirement was that they FOLLOW the selection.
- **Verification.** 4 new cases (**TEST-010**) in `AgentDetailPanel.artifactVersions.test.tsx`, all seen **RED first** against unmodified source (`Tests 4 failed | 4 passed (8)` — the 4 pre-existing ISS-065 cases green throughout, so the red is the new gap only), GREEN after (8/8; 50/50 across the 5 `results/` suites). Full frontend vitest **147 failed / 820 passed → 147 failed / 824 passed**, failing-id sets diffing to EMPTY and the same 29 failing files; +4 = exactly the new cases. `tsc --noEmit` 2 errors, both pre-existing and neither in the touched area. Retired-palette grep 0; token-layer 9/9.
- **Live proof, read-only, no money spent.** Completed run `5ecb990f` on the real backend (`:8010`): Spec Kit Analyzer picker `summary · v2 of 2` → `v1 of 2` repaints the Governance-checks card from v2's "Issues Resolution & Revised Findings / Risk Mitigation Plan / Revised Specification Addenda" to v1's "**READY WITH CAUTION** / Summary / Findings / Risk register / Suggested next actions", with the "Viewing v1 (read-only)" banner. Screenshots `scratchpad/iss085-live-01-before-v2.png` and `-03-after-v1.png`.
- **Harness lesson, recorded because it nearly cost real money.** The reusable "sweep every `header button` until Run History appears" idiom in the earlier live scripts clicks the sidebar RUN PILL and opens whatever run is active — during this task that was a `waiting_for_user` prototype parked at a clarify gate, one wrong click away from a 5–21M-token resume. Drive the "Jump back in" card by its exact accessible name (`getByRole('button', { name: /<run title>/ })`) instead, and reach an agent's L2 detail via `getByTestId('steps-agent-row').filter({ hasText: <agent name> })` — a bare `getByText(<agent name>)` matches the chat transcript on the left and is intercepted. Run states were re-read from the API before and after the session to prove nothing was resumed.
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-087** (minor) — the un-versioned halves of the cards (task rows, checks badge, handoff) still show current run state when an older version is selected; closing it needs either a parse of the selected `<tasks>` body (which would move the LATEST-version behaviour the 42-09 tests pin) or the already-registered backend follow-ups F1/F2.

## Quick 260812-7sk — Stop actually stops a run, and the run reaches a terminal state (FIX-227)

> **Commit `ebf83005` (code + tests) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-084 (CRITICAL)**. Files **ISS-088** + **ISS-089**. Goldens **10/10** and lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**, both identical to the pre-change commit `1ed94666`; no golden regenerated.

- **What / Why (settled).** There was no way for anyone — user or operator — to stop a running build once it had crossed a backend restart, and every un-stoppable `od_prototype` build costs 5-21M Bedrock tokens of the owner's money. Measured on run `d5dbc9f2`: 16,530,718 tokens total, **7,510,082 of them billed AFTER the API answered `cancelled: true`**, with zero `pipeline_cancelled` events on the run.
- **The root cause: the signal was structurally absent, not ignored.** `ExecutionEngine._drive_resumed_stream` is the ONE funnel all four resume drivers (`resume_run` branch (b), `_rearm_gate_run` branch (a), `_replay_clarify_run`, the user `POST /resume` wrapper) reach `_execute_impl` through, and it passed **no `cancel_event` kwarg at all** — so the parameter bound its `None` default (`engine.py:1096`) and all twelve cooperative guards, each written `if cancel_event and cancel_event.is_set()`, short-circuited. The guards were never wrong; the value was. Independently, `run_engine._register_resume_task` minted an **orphan** `asyncio.Event` into `_CANCEL_EVENTS` for exactly those runs, so `cancel_run` found one, set it, and reported registry mutation as cancellation. `849e536d`/KAN-88 had simultaneously deleted the working destructive fallback on a premise its own comment asserted and that was false the day it was written; Phase 44's REST port then dropped it entirely.
- **Where (as-built).** `engine.py` — new `ResumeCancelEvent` alias (`:65-78`), `self._resume_cancel_event` slot beside the five existing resume hooks (`:889-896`), `_resolve_resume_cancel_event` helper mirroring `_fire_resume_cleanup`'s best-effort shape (`:8100-8116`), and the resolution + pass-through at the funnel (`:8347-8364`). `run_engine._resume_cancel_event` (`:503-521`) is get-or-create on `_CANCEL_EVENTS`; `_register_resume_task` (`:524-541`) delegates to it. `main.py:211-218` is the one wiring line. `run_commands.cancel_run` (`:342-386`) + `_arm_cancel_escalation` (`:318-337`). `run_shutdown._drain_then_cancel` (`:219-258`) + `stop_run_driver` (`:287-330`).
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).**
  **(1) Resolve at the FUNNEL, not as a parameter threaded through the four drivers.** `_drive_resumed_stream` is the single point every resume driver passes through, so a future resume driver inherits the fix instead of re-opening the hole. Adding a `cancel_event=` parameter to `resume_run`/`_rearm_gate_run`/`_replay_clarify_run` would be a second mechanism and three more places to forget.
  **(2) An INJECTED hook, never an import.** The kernel must not import `app.api` (import-linter contract 1). This is the sixth callback in the same established pattern; `lint-imports` staying **4 kept / 0 broken** is the proof, not the intention.
  **(3) `run_engine._resume_cancel_event` is the ONLY resume-path mint site (INV-12).** The orphan mint is *superseded*, not left alongside. Get-or-create is load-bearing twice: the engine resolving later gets the SAME object the endpoint already holds (asserted by an **object-identity** test), and a double-register cannot reset an Event a Stop has already set.
  **(4) The ack is an ACCEPTANCE, never a claim.** `_is_run_live` (the driver TASK) is the truth condition; the response is `accepted: true` + `status: "stopping"`, or `accepted: false` + `status: "not_running"`. `cancelled` is retained for wire compatibility and is never `true` — it used to be `true` in exactly the case where cancelling was impossible.
  **(5) The destructive escalation is a FALLBACK, strictly after the cooperative signal had its drain budget** — never the primary mechanism. Unconditional `task.cancel()` was REJECTED: it reintroduces the ISS-007 delivery race and leaves the row non-terminal, i.e. it re-creates the defect. `_drain_then_cancel` is the ONE escalation policy, extracted from `stop_pipeline_drivers` and shared with it, so the interactive path cannot drift from the tested one.
  **(6) A cancel that leaves the row non-terminal is not a cancel, it is a delayed re-run.** `restore_non_terminal_runs` re-adopts every non-terminal row on the next boot and drives it to completion — measured, the replacement backend emitted `pipeline_start` two seconds after boot and billed 7.5M further tokens. So `stop_run_driver` calls the existing `_reconcile_terminal_status` once the driver is provably gone (`pipeline_cancelled` → `cancelled`, no clean terminal → `failed`; either way terminal, either way outside `NON_TERMINAL`).
- **Do NOT "fix" this class by cancelling the task from the endpoint.** That is Option B from the investigation and it is rejected on three counts, all recorded: the ISS-007 race, a non-terminal row, and leaving `cancel_event=None` in place so the next resume-path feature inherits the same hole.
- **Verification.** 9 new backend cases (**TEST-011**) across three files, each seen **RED first** — the two end-to-end ones by mutating the single root-cause line back, which reproduces the production symptom verbatim: *"a cancelled resume kept dispatching agents: {'a': 2, 'b': 2} -> {'a': 4, 'b': 4, 'c': 2, 'd': 2}"* and *"the next boot re-adopted a run the owner paid to stop"*. 99 passed across the changed area. Goldens **10/10** and lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**, identical to `1ed94666`. `tests/agents/test_restart_resume.py` held at its **7 failed / 48 passed** ISS-078 baseline. The 4 reds in `test_rest_run_launch.py`/`test_rest_revisions.py` (`'_FakeUser' object has no attribute 'tier'`) were re-baselined in a detached worktree at `1ed94666` and fail identically there.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved.** The whole proof is offline — `test_cancel_stops_resumed_run.py` drives the real `resume_run` over a real in-memory-SQLite ScopedStore with a scripted model, reusing `test_restart_resume`'s `_ResumeHarness` rather than cloning it. This defect was found because a resumed build burned 16.5M tokens; verifying it live would have been the same mistake.
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-088** (major) — the local uvicorn runs without `--timeout-graceful-shutdown` (only `docker-entrypoint.sh:35` passes it) so SIGTERM never reaches `lifespan.shutdown()` while an SSE stream is live, and `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS` defaults `False`; operational, and it changes how the process is launched. **ISS-089** (major) — a cancel is still purely in-process, so a Stop arriving with no live driver is answered honestly but the next boot still auto-resumes the run; closing it needs a DURABLE `cancel_requested` marker checked by `restore_non_terminal_runs` before it adopts. **Not touched, deliberately (one variable at a time; ISS-078's territory):** the four loops that read no cancel flag at all — `engine.py:2492` (strategy-event forwarding), `:3318` (the `_run_agent` redo `while`), `task_loop.py:492` (validator), and the fan-out family (`fanout_batch`, `run_fanout`/`run_worker`, `wave_scheduler`).

## Quick 260812-8j4 — a redo shows the agent its own prior output (FIX-228)

> **Commits `70eb3636` (RED tests) + `38d0166f` (engine fix) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-086 (major)**. Files **ISS-090**. Successor to FIX-217 / quick-`260811-mxg` — it completes the pair FIX-217 established. Plan + measured baseline + verbatim RED evidence + the deferred live recipe: `.planning/quick/260812-8j4-fix-iss-086-redo-must-show-the-agent-its-own-prior/`. New coverage: `backend/tests/agents/test_redo_prompt_contract.py`.

- **What / Why (settled).** "Request changes" at an agent's gate re-ran that agent with the user's instruction and **without** the document the instruction was about, so the model wrote only the delta and the previous work was destroyed. Measured live on run `a0d17afa`: `task_list` v1 → v2 = 12,542 → 3,495 chars, headings **7 → 1**, **0 of 7 kept**; the redo dispatch grew by exactly **106 bytes** — the instruction alone. Broken for **every** agent, proven three ways (no agent/kind/workflow branch at the publish site; a second live run `ec7fb984` shows it at two different agents; the offline repro fails for three agents across two pipelines).
- **The root cause is a DECISION, not a mechanism.** P23 modelled a re-run as a **regeneration** and minted a fresh `:redo{N}` checkpoint thread *specifically* to stop the model seeing its rejected output (the "it's already done" bug). The product then surfaced that action as **"Request changes"** with an instruction box — so blank ⇒ regenerate stayed coherent, but **non-blank ⇒ revise**, and revise without the subject is unsatisfiable. FIX-217 hit the identical fork on the `update_specs` path and resolved it by pairing the fresh thread (D3) **with** an explicit prior-artifact injection (D1). **P23 shipped only the fresh-thread half of that pair.** All three other channels are closed by construction: self-consumption is structurally impossible (`_filter_consumed_outputs` breaks on `upstream.id == spec.id`), the `:redo{N}` thread kills replay, and gated authoring agents declare `tools: []`.
- **Where (as-built).** `engine.py` — new `_consume_redo` (beside `_consume_update_specs`) is **the** one `_gate_redo` consumer, driven by all three gate branches (the RESUME-17 re-entry, the post-revision re-open, the live post-stream gate); the publish site in `_run_agent`'s redo loop save/restores `ectx.spec_revision_prior_artifact` around the one `_compose_context_message` call, inside a `try/finally`; `_compose_context_message`'s `PRIOR ARTIFACT UNDER REVISION` block moved **above** `ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS (REVISE)` with generalised prose. `context.py` — the field's doc now records **two publishers, one field, one renderer**. No new field, no new block, no new event, no migration; alembic head stays 0030.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).**
  **(1) Reuse FIX-217's seam; do NOT mint a second one.** One field (`spec_revision_prior_artifact`), one renderer, two publishers. A redo-specific field plus a `=== PRIOR OUTPUT ===` block would be two things meaning one thing, diverging on the next edit (INV-12). If the *name* is ever the objection, rename it in one commit — do not fork it.
  **(2) SAVE/RESTORE, never clear.** A redo can fire at a gate opened **inside** a revision pass (proven live on `ec7fb984`), and zeroing the field there would strip the outer pass's own subject mid-flight — the exact quick-`260811-si4` defect-A shape. At the outer level the saved value is `""`, so it is byte-equivalent to a clear. **Side benefit:** a redo inside a pass now publishes the *rejected draft* rather than the pre-pass version the pass read once before its loop, which closes the "specify-inside-a-pass staleness" open question from the ISS-086 analysis §14.
  **(3) Block ORDER is load-bearing, not cosmetic.** The REVISE block was appended **above** the prior-artifact block, so reusing the seam without moving it would have read *instructions first, subject second* — the inverse of the rule FIX-217 learned. The move is INV-3-safe because `redo_directive` is empty on the revision path, so PRIOR → REPORT keeps its relative order there.
  **(4) The subject comes from the SAME kind-scoped max-version ref the lineage stamp already computes** — zero extra reads, and **kind-scoped by construction**. A producer-only lookup (`_latest_typed_content`) matches on `producer_agent` alone, and `prototype-build` writes both `html_file` **and** `file_bundle`, so max-version across kinds would serve the wrong document.
  **(5) Withheld in exactly two cases, both name-free.** A **blank** redo — the FE's own placeholder reads *"leave blank to just regenerate"*, and regenerate-from-scratch is precisely the P23 semantics the `:redo{N}` thread exists to enforce, so blank must stay a regenerate. And a **per-task build dispatch** (`ectx.build_task_number` set) — that dispatch already carries a compacted skeleton of the same document, so injecting the full artifact would double-inject the deliverable.
  **(6) Collapsing the three consumers fixed the re-open branch's thin-copy defects for free.** That branch set only the directive, so besides missing the subject it lost `derived_from` lineage, left a **duplicate `results` entry** for the same `agent_id`, and wrote **no audit row** — which under-seeded `_seed_gate_reentry_attempts`, risking a colliding `:redo{N}` after a restart. All three are now asserted.
- **Do NOT "fix" this class by dropping the `:redo{N}` suffix so the checkpointer replays.** It is a one-line deletion that appears to work and is rejected on three counts: it revives the documented P23 "it's already done" failure; it makes correctness depend on replay, which FIX-217 D3 proved is **empty after a restart** on the InMemory saver, so the redo would work in one session and silently fail after a restart — the worst failure shape; and it moves the fix away from the established seam. **Also rejected: adding the agent to its own `consumes`** — structurally impossible, `_filter_consumed_outputs` breaks on `upstream.id == spec.id`. **And do NOT "fix" it by relabelling the button** — amend-don't-regenerate is the desired product behaviour; the engine should honour what the UI promises.
- **Verification.** 11 new cases (**TEST-012**), **8 observed RED first** at `742f0c6e` with verbatim output in the quick task's BASELINE.md — every failure an assertion **inside the test body**, zero pytest errors, because `_run_agent` swallows a stub `TypeError` into an `agent_error` event and a fixture problem therefore *looks* like a failing assertion from outside. The measured `delta first->redo = 101 chars` independently reproduces the analysis's byte formula `79 + len(instruction)`. Generality is asserted, not asserted-about: the primary test is parametrized over agent ids **read from the registry** across two pipelines (SC-001). Baselines re-measured, not trusted: goldens **10/10 identical** (never regenerated), lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken identical**, `test_restart_resume.py` **7 failed / 48 passed with the SAME 7 ids** (compared id-by-id in a detached worktree at `742f0c6e`), `tests/unit/test_execution_engine.py` **3 failed / 11 passed** with the same 3 clarify-engine ids. **INV-3 byte-identity is proven directly, not inferred:** the first (non-redo) dispatch of three gated agents was dumped before and after the change and is identical by sha256 `9f84b82e3736f045bde1c243770de255782252315e11cafceedc1a876b5bd24c` — the one thing the goldens **cannot** show, because `_scripted_model.py:649` drives them with `gate_agent_ids=[]` so no gate ever opens and a redo is unreachable in a golden run. Treat 10/10 as evidence of dormancy only.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved.** The whole proof is offline: the scripted-model harness drives the real `ExecutionEngine._run_agent` redo while-loop end to end, through all three consumer sites. **Live Bedrock acceptance is DEFERRED** to the end-of-milestone pass; its recipe (pull versions from `GET /api/runs/{id}/artifacts`, *not* the UI which wipes v1 on `agent_start` per FIX-039; assert every v1 `Task N:` heading survives into v2; confirm PRIOR renders **before** REVISE; repeat once with a blank instruction and confirm the block is ABSENT) is recorded in `260812-8j4-BASELINE.md`.
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-090** (minor) — `redoable` has no eligibility fence: unlike `update_specs_eligible` (a structural predicate, published and binding since FIX-219) it is an inline `True` literal at all three gate call sites, so any agent named in a per-run `gate_agent_ids` gets a Redo button with no server-side rule. FIX-228 handles the task-loop case defensively inside `_consume_redo`, but that is the engine being careful rather than the affordance being correct. Changing it changes which buttons users see, so it needs its own decision.
- **One brief figure corrected.** The task brief quoted `test_gate_revision_discriminator.py` as **29** tests; it collects **6**. `29` is the sum of the other four suites named in the same bullet. Measured figures were used throughout.

## Quick 260812-9tq — ISS-033-A: the two model calls nobody was billing for (FIX-230 / TEST-014)

> **Commit `80356fda` (code + tests) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-033** (whose row was STALE and is corrected in place). Files **ISS-092** (part B) and **ISS-093** (pre-existing clarify reds); annotates **ISS-034** with its blocking dependency. Plan + measured baselines: `.planning/quick/260812-9tq-fix-iss-033-a-fold-uncounted-model-calls/`.

- **What / Why (settled).** Two call-sites made the reported run cost wrong, both foldable without a product decision. The validation fix-loop drained its sub-agent's stream with a bare `continue`, discarding every `usage` event; `handoff/TestAgent.analyse` still called `llm.ainvoke` raw, so it was neither Bedrock-cached nor counted.
- **The headline the register did not know: ISS-033 was ~70% fixed on 2026-07-15 and nothing said so.** Phase 43-04 shipped `app/agents/cached_invoke.py` (`0aa2072c`) and routed four sites (`8518f29b`); the aux fold is live-proven in `dev.db`. The ISS-033 row still read `OPEN (deferred)` a month later, and the card store did not catch the drift either. **Read the row AND the commits before sizing an old issue.**
- **The 43-04 miss, named.** That plan's wording — "handoff Test(classifier)" — mistook `classifier.py` (the coding-vs-test router) for `test_agent.py` (the real Test agent), so it routed the wrong module and closed. The lesson is procedural: **route by call-site grep (`\.ainvoke(`), not by agent name.** The true direct-call set is **9 sites, not the 3 filed**.
- **Where (as-built).** `engine.py` — `_run_validation_fix_loop` takes an `aux_usage_sink` and routes `usage` events into it; `KernelServices` is constructed with `aux_usage_sink=aux_token_usage.append`. `kernel_services.py` — ctor param stored and threaded through `run_validation_fix_loop`. `app/agents/handoff/test_agent.py` — routed through `cached_invoke`, superseded local `_extract_text` deleted. `tests/agents/test_model_pricing.py` — the dead INV-12 cost-site guard repaired.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).**
  **(1) ONE accumulator.** The fix-loop feeds the EXISTING `aux_token_usage` that the planner/clarify one-shots already use. A future aux source registers by feeding that sink — never by adding a second sum at the cost site.
  **(2) Never `results`.** `agents_completed = len(results)`, so a fix attempt appended there becomes a phantom agent. Pinned by `test_fix_loop_tokens_do_not_inflate_agents_completed` (6, not 10). Note `agents_completed` (6) legitimately exceeds `agents_total` (5): it counts `_run_agent` invocations, and the build agent runs once per task.
  **(3) `cached_invoke` is the ONLY direct-invoke seam (INV-12).** Rows 7/8/9 of the call-site table are `DeepAgentRunner` calls — already cached by the middleware, missing only the *counting* half. Routing them through `cached_invoke` would fork a second agent path and break INV-13 and INV-12 at once. **Do not.**
  **(4) Capture usage BEFORE the cancel check.** A token the model has already reported was already paid for; a cancel must not erase it from the bill.
  **(5) If a token was not observed, it must not be invented.** The rejected shortcut — estimating the fix loop by a fudge factor, or the Concierge from `len(chat_reply)` — is recorded on ISS-092 so it is not re-proposed. Unmeasured spend is reported as unmeasured.
- **The goldens DO exercise the fix loop** (4 sub-agents per prototype golden, read out of the engine's INFO log). The run totals genuinely move there — 220 → 460 input — and stay golden-neutral only because those keys are sentinel-normalized/stripped. **Re-run the goldens after any change to run-token accounting; do not reason about neutrality from the normalizer alone.**
- **Verification.** 8 offline cases green (**TEST-014**), the RED-first ones seen failing first: `assert (220 - 220) == 240` and `TypeError: TestAgent.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'usage_sink'`. Goldens **10/10** and lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**, both re-run and identical to `d24c576a`, no golden regenerated. The 8 protected suites **112 passed / 0 failed**. **Not live-proven, deliberately** — no run launched, resumed or gate-approved.
- **The delta, on real data.** Read-only against the live `dev.db`, priced through the real shared `estimate_cost_usd` (which reproduces the persisted `$2.550421` for `fa66227a` exactly): the fix-loop spend now counted is **~929,000 input tokens = 6.9% of that run's input, +$0.176**. Offline the delta is exact: **+240 input / +100 output** per golden prototype run.
- **Filed, not fixed.** **ISS-092** (major) — the Concierge discards `usage` AND reads unbounded run events (up to **2.3M tokens** available for one chat question; `authz.py:315` has no LIMIT and no type filter), plus the handoff pipeline's total absence of a cost surface. **ISS-093** (minor) — 3 stale clarify-round tests, verified failing at `d24c576a` too.
- **ISS-034 is blocked, and its spec is wrong as written.** On **7 of 9 runs in `dev.db` the cache "saving" is NEGATIVE** (−5% to −8.9%): single-turn text-only agents write a cache entry nothing ever reads, and `cache_write_5m` is 1.25× input. A "saved $Y (Z%)" display would render a wrong-signed number. The FE contract must be a **signed** delta. Recorded on the ISS-034 row.

## Quick 260812-97f — ISS-078's seven reds were THREE causes, and six were the tests (FIX-229 / TEST-013)

> **Commits `1c7569db` (RED tests) + `d3184e10` (reconcile fix) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-078 (major)**. Files **ISS-091**. `test_restart_resume.py` **7 failed / 48 passed → 60 passed / 0 failed**. Plan + measured baseline + the rejected-option evidence: `.planning/quick/260812-97f-fix-iss-078-resume-classifier-stale-stub/`.

- **What / Why (settled).** ISS-078 held that "at least two of the 7 reds may be describing a LIVE PRODUCTION RESUME BUG" — a resume re-invoking completed work and duplicating token spend. **It was not.** The seven decomposed into three independent causes from three commits, and **only one was a product defect** — a different one from the two the row was watching.
- **The load-bearing decision: the resume classifier was NOT loosened.** The prior investigation recommended replacing `c71f3d9c`/FIX-121's conjunction in `_first_incomplete_step` with an interruption test (`in agent_start_events and not in agent_complete_events`), and had measured it green. **Rejected here on evidence the investigation did not gather.** Read-only against the live `backend/dev.db`, that predicate's differential versus HEAD is exactly one set — *artifact producer with **no** `agent_start` **and** no `agent_complete`* — which is **27 rows, all `deep-planner` / `clarify-agent`**, and **neither appears in any `agents/workflows/*/workflow.yaml` step list nor in `registry.PIPELINE_AGENTS`** (grep: 0 hits), so neither is ever a member of `ordered_agents`. Simultaneously, the scenario the proposal was *argued from* — a lost `agent_complete` write making a step permanently unskippable — has a live count of **0**, **and the proposal is a no-op for it regardless** (`agent_start` present + `agent_complete` absent ⇒ `_interrupted=True` ⇒ still re-run, byte-identical to HEAD). **Net: zero production effect; the sole observable consequence would have been five broken fixtures going green.** `engine.py` is byte-identical to `99fcf4a2`.
- **Cause A — fixture drift (5 of 7, from `c71f3d9c`).** Every one of those fixtures persists **zero** `run_events`, so the evidence the classifier requires cannot exist in them. The two the register called "end-to-end" and treated as the strongest support for a live bug drove **`engine._execute_impl` directly** (`:431`, `:3049`); the durable `_RunEventSink` is built in the **public** entry (`engine.py:1020`, persisted `:1065`) and `_execute_impl` persists nothing. **Driving `execute()` makes them pass with the engine untouched — which is the disproof.** The three unit-level ones hand-seeded `ArtifactRef` only; two of them were failing at index 0 on the *plan* step and never reaching the `task_loop` branch they exist to test.
- **Cause B — stale stub (1 of 7, from `2d5b9fcc`).** A 3-tuple milestone-card stub against the 4-tuple contract (`chat_narrator.persist_milestone_card:287-289`). It was breaking the resumed **drive** — `engine.py:8509`, swallowed by `except Exception` — not merely the test.
- **Cause C — the one real product defect (1 of 7, from `bac1e556`).** A user who resumes a run parked at a review gate and **rejects** had it recorded `completed`. `resume_supersedes` asked *"is there a `pipeline_complete` at a higher seq?"* and read the answer as *"a later attempt succeeded"* — **two different questions.** On a rejection both events belong to one attempt. Probe-captured tail: `...5:review_gate_ready / 6:pipeline_cancelled / 7:pipeline_complete` → `completed`.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/app/api/run_commands.py:592-621` — `_reconcile_terminal_status`. `resume_supersedes` gains one clause: a completion supersedes a cancellation only when a `run_resuming`/`pipeline_start` **attempt boundary** lies between them. Tightened in place; no second status decision (INV-12). Everything else in this task is `backend/tests/agents/test_restart_resume.py`.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).**
  **(1) The predicate stays.** Absent terminal evidence ⇒ re-enter, never skip. Re-deriving the "was it interrupted?" relaxation is re-treading measured ground — read the evidence above first.
  **(2) Fix the fixture, not the predicate.** When a resume test fails for want of an `agent_complete`, the question is whether the fixture models a real run. `execute()` persists events; `_execute_impl` does not. A test that calls itself end-to-end must go through the public entry.
  **(3) "Later attempt", not "later seq".** Any future edit to the reconcile must preserve the attempt-boundary distinction; the three-case parametrized pin exists to make a bare-seq regression fail immediately.
  **(4) FIX-229 fixes the record, not the work.** It is deliberately **not** symptom-site surgery: the reconcile's own assumption is provably wrong. The engine emitting a contradictory tail at all is ISS-091 and was kept out on purpose — it changes termination semantics for every workflow.
- **Two coverage gaps closed (ISS-029 discipline).** **FIX-121 and `resume_supersedes` both shipped with no test at all** — `grep resume_supersedes tests/` returned zero hits, and nothing pinned the classifier's fail-safe. Both are now pinned, each seen RED under the mutation it guards, each mutation reverted and confirmed byte-identical by `git diff`. The two later-attempt cases stay **green** under the FIX-229 mutation on purpose: that is what proves the new clause discriminates only the behaviour it changes.
- **Verification.** 60 cases green (**TEST-013**), the RED intermediate measured exactly (`2 failed / 58 passed` at `1c7569db`, the two expected ids). Goldens **10/10** and lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**, both identical to `99fcf4a2`, no golden regenerated. Protected suites **52 passed** and the resume/cancel/shutdown adjacents **44 passed**, both identical to baseline. The 14-file `run_commands` consumer sweep was measured **both with and without** the fix clause — `14 failed / 156 passed` either way, so those reds are pre-existing and untouched rather than merely labelled so.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved.** One build is 5–21M tokens; the parent session had already lost 16.5M to an accident. Every proof here is offline. `dev.db` was read strictly read-only (`file:dev.db?mode=ro`), and neither the running backend nor the frontend was restarted.
- **Filed, not fixed. ISS-091** (major) — **rejecting at a gate does not STOP the pipeline**: measured at `99fcf4a2` (*with* FIX-227 present, so FIX-227 does not cover it), the full fan-out runs after `pipeline_cancelled` and the run ends `pipeline_complete`. `_run_agent`'s `return` ends only its own generator; the consuming loop observes `agent_error` and nothing else; and the step-boundary check that would stop it reads `cancel_event`, which a gate rejection never sets. Steps routed through `_run_agent` are spared by its terminal-state guard — **`wave_scheduler` is not, and has zero cancel/terminal checks**, which is also the true remainder of FIX-227's four-deferred-loops note (`engine.py:2371` and `task_loop.py:275/:376` **do** check).
- **Also observed, unregistered.** 3 pre-existing reds in `tests/agents/test_gates.py` at `99fcf4a2`, unrelated to ISS-078 and in no register row found — recorded on the ISS-078 row rather than given an id, since they were not investigated here.
- **One brief figure corrected.** The task brief quoted the seven protected suites as **41 passed**; they collect **52** at `99fcf4a2` (TEST-011 and TEST-012 landed after that figure was taken). Re-measured rather than inherited, per the brief's own instruction.

## Quick 260812-fbk — the harness gate that reported success without gating (FIX-231 / TEST-015)

> **Commits `3def9d1a` (RED guard + forwarding assertion) + `f36c3a07` (fix) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-074** (whose central claim was wrong — see below). Files **ISS-094**, **ISS-095**, **ISS-096**. Test-only: **0 production modules changed**.

- **The defect.** `tests/agents/live_harness.py:672` pinned `_run_review_gate`'s four-parameter shape from 2026-06-11 and installed the wrapper over `engine._run_review_gate` at `:683` **unconditionally** (so even the `auto_resume_gates=False` manual pass-through seam broke). The engine grew to **ten** parameters and **four** call sites pass them all by keyword — `engine.py:3397`/`:3504`/`:4440` **and `kernel_services.py:1116`**, the declared `gates:[human]`/`approval` delegate the ISS-074 row missed, which is why the declared-gate path broke too. The wrapper also forwarded only the same four **positionally**, so widening the def alone would silently drop them.
- **The damage was a false green, not a crash.** The `TypeError` is swallowed by the engine's per-agent error handler: the gated agent is marked failed and the pipeline runs on to `pipeline_complete` with `gated=False, completed=True`. Every gated harness drive since `f18de868` (2026-06-30, when `redoable` landed) reported a successful run **in which the gate never opened**. Severity raised minor → major on that basis.
- **The row's premise was refuted, and that is the transferable lesson.** ISS-074 said the fix was *"UNVERIFIABLE offline, which is why it was filed rather than patched."* Five tests were **already red at HEAD in 2.19 s** with no credentials and zero Bedrock spend. Neither file is credential-gated: `test_live_harness.py` has no module skip at all, and `test_phase8_live.py` gates only `TestLiveHITL`/`TestLivePipelines`. **The real cause of the 43-day blindness was coverage selection by FILENAME** — `.planning/TEST-REGISTER.md:85` read *"Avoid offline: anything `*_live*`"*, and both files are offline-safe despite their names. A heuristic that excludes by name rather than by skip mark will keep doing this.
- **Both tokens are load-bearing, and that was measured, not argued.** `**kwargs` on the `def` alone greens every pre-existing assertion (**1 failed / 7 passed**, the single red being only the newly added forwarding assertion) while discarding all six extras: `cancel_event` — a gate that cannot honour Stop, silently undoing quick-260720-ec4's BUG-2 Cond B threading — and `redoable`/`update_specs_eligible`, the name-free SC-001 discriminators. The fix widens the def **and** forwards `**kwargs`; the four named parameters stay named because the body reads two of them at `:677`.
- **The guard the row asked for now exists, and it was proven against the NEXT drift.** New `tests/agents/test_gate_stub_signature_drift.py` (4 tests, <1 s, imports nothing it scans): it AST-**derives** the engine's real parameter list — never hand-copied, since restating it would reproduce the very drift it guards — resolves monkeypatched names, factory-returned inner functions **and class-based doubles** (which no assignment census can see), and asserts `inspect.Signature.bind`, the exact operation Python performs at the call site. Unresolvable stubs **fail loudly rather than skip**. Demonstration: a throwaway stub pinning today's ten parameters plus a temporary 11th engine parameter → RED naming the stub and `cannot accept: ['throwaway_drift_probe']`; control with the engine reverted → green. Both the probe and the engine edit were removed and `git status` confirms **0 files changed under `backend/agents/` or `backend/app/`**.
- **The census, mechanically.** **29 assignment sites across 18 files** (the row said 11), resolving to 26 distinct stubs, **plus one class-based stub**: `test_gates.py:920` `_FakeReviewEngine._run_review_gate` pinned 5 of 10 with no `**kwargs` and was one forwarded parameter from the identical failure — widened here. Every other stub already absorbed `**kwargs`. **No production code wraps `_run_review_gate`**, so Ports & Adapters is untouched.
- **Scope limit, stated rather than glossed.** The guard covers **arity only**. It cannot see a wrapper that accepts kwargs into a bag and forwards nothing — that is what the behavioural Part-2 assertion is for — and it cannot see **attribute** drift on hand-rolled doubles (**ISS-094**). A guard whose blind spots are undocumented invites the next false sense of safety.
- **Coverage fix, which is the actual root cause.** `test_live_harness.py` + `test_phase8_live.py` (34 passed / 16 skipped) and the new guard are now in the curated offline suite in `.planning/TEST-REGISTER.md` §1.6, and the filename heuristic was replaced with "check the actual skip marks". Recorded there too: **`lint-imports` must be run from `backend/`** — from anywhere else it prints "Could not read any configuration" and reads as a false pass (hit during this task's own verification).
- **Verification.** Baseline **5 failed / 3 passed → 8 passed / 0 failed** (**TEST-015**). Guard 4 passed, seen RED first. Goldens **10 passed** with **0 golden files modified**, `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken** (215 files, 526 deps) — both identical to `fab9b646` (INV-3 confirmed by measurement, not assumed). Known pre-existing reds re-measured **unchanged**: `test_gates.py` 3/39, `test_declared_gate_streaming.py` 3, `test_wire_parity.py` 4/2.

- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved.** One build is 5–21M tokens. Every proof here is offline.
- **Filed, not fixed. ISS-094** (minor) — the 3 `test_gates.py` reds are `_Ectx`/`_Ctx` **attribute** drift: same family, but the guard cannot catch an attribute, so an attribute-conformance guard is the family-ending move. Acknowledged in prose on the ISS-078 row but had no row of its own until now. **ISS-095** (major) — the 3 `test_declared_gate_streaming.py` reds are labelled *"3 env-reds (sqlite FK, Postgres-gated)"* at `IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md:4075`, but the observed failures assert a **declared human gate never fired** and a **gate rejection did not cancel the run** (possibly the same defect as ISS-091). ## Quick 260812-g1c — a review-gate rejection now stops the run (FIX-232 / TEST-016)

> **Commits `4f058f9a` (RED tests) + `3f37bea4` (primary fix) + `6df1f1a0` (secondary fix) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-091**. Files **ISS-097**, **ISS-098**, **ISS-099**. Production surface: 3 modules, +55 lines, no deletions.

- **The defect.** Rejecting at an inline human review gate emitted `pipeline_cancelled` and then let **every remaining step run**, terminating on `pipeline_complete`. Reproduced byte-identically at `c0bbb6e2`.
- **Root cause, two parts.** (a) The dispatch loop (`engine.py:2523`) observed **only** `agent_error`. The gate's reject handler cancels the run, yields `pipeline_cancelled` and `return`s — but a generator `return` only ends *that step*, so the terminal event was forwarded and ignored and the outer `for i, spec in enumerate(ordered_agents)` advanced to step i+1, falling through to the sole `pipeline_complete` emitter. (b) The only step-boundary termination check (`engine.py:2381`) reads `cancel_event`, and a gate rejection sets none — which is precisely why FIX-227 was orthogonal.
- **The severity was mis-stated in the ISS-091 row, and the correction is the point.** The row's COST line ("worker + merge cost of every wave after a rejected gate") is **materially overstated: the real spend is ZERO model tokens.** Every post-rejection worker short-circuits on `_run_agent`'s terminal guard (`:3329`) — `call_log {}`, `subagent_runs.tokens` all `None`. What the row missed is worse than what it claimed: **the rejection poisons the durable resume record.** Each no-op worker is still written `subagent_runs.status='complete'` and each wave `wave_runs.status='completed'`, and `wave_scheduler.py:251-256` skips completed waves on resume. Reject → restart → resume skipped **both** waves, produced **zero** files, and recorded the run `completed` — silent, permanent loss of a fan-out run's entire output, on the live user-facing Phase-51 fan-out feature. The row's "WHY IT IS NOT WORSE" reasoning is exactly backwards: the terminal guard is the mechanism that turns a wasted run into an unrecoverable one.
- **The row's "SECOND, RELATED GAP" is refuted.** `wave_scheduler` does not need a `cancel_event` check: `run_fanout` already owns that boundary (`fanout.py:231-233 _check_cancel`, called pre-wave / between sequential workers / pre-merge, plus `_await_workers_with_cancel`), and a probe confirms Stop mid-wave IS honoured today at wave granularity. `fanout_batch.py` has no `is_set()` either — which the row did not name.
- **The fix is the row's suggested shape with one correction.** `return`, **not** `break`: `break` falls through to the Step-5 terminal block, which still emits `pipeline_complete`. Flag-then-return rather than breaking mid-generator, so the producer's `finally` blocks (notably `run_agent`'s build-scratch reset) keep their normal path. It is the exact sibling of the declared-gate handler **WR-03** (`engine.py:2454-2479`), whose own comment describes this defect verbatim: the declared path stopped the run, the inline path did not.
- **Secondary fix, and why it is where it is.** `fanout.py::_check_cancel` now consults run terminality via a new `KernelServices.is_run_terminal()`. Deliberately **not** in `wave_scheduler.py`: that is a capability, import-linter forbids it importing the execution kernel, a check there would need a new port, and it would be a *second* fan-out cancel implementation next to the existing one (INV-12) while still missing `fanout_batch` and the `spawn_subagents` tool, which funnel through the same `run_fanout`. Unreachable on the reported path once the primary fix lands, so it got **direct unit coverage** rather than shipping unproven.
- **Safety of the secondary check was verified, not assumed.** Terminal states are absorbing (`state_machine.py:86-90`), so a run only reaches fan-out after transitioning to `generating` at `engine.py:2060` — `is_run_terminal()` can be true only on a genuine mid-run termination. Both `"failed"` transitions (`:2617` BudgetExceeded, `:2650` Step-5) are outside the step loop, so no run is ever `failed` mid-fan-out.
- **Rejected shortcuts, recorded so they are not re-proposed.** Making the gate call `cancel_event.set()` — the seductive "reuse the Stop plumbing" option — inverts app/kernel ownership of `_CANCEL_EVENTS` (`run_commands.py`), flips the outer `except asyncio.CancelledError` re-raise decision that FIX-227 depends on (`engine.py:2608-2609`), and double-emits. Guarding Step 5 on terminal state only fixes the *event* and not the *work*, leaving the data loss entirely. "Nothing runs anyway, so it's cosmetic" is refuted by the resume proof.
- **Blast radius re-verified independently, because it was the one thing that could break the revision flow.** All four `pipeline_cancelled` emitters reachable by the dispatch loop already `return` — `:3413`, `:3520`, `:4458` (the three inline reject handlers) and `:5502` (`_consume_update_specs`, whose `_us_cancelled` caller returns at `:3470`/`:3599`/`:4536`). There is **no producer outside `engine.py`** (every other hit is a comment, a membership set in `gate_pendency.py`, or a consumer). Fan-out workers cannot leak a false positive: `fanout.py::_run_one` reads only `agent_complete` from `run_worker` and drops every other child event. Revision runs nest via the API layer (`run_commands.py:2560` → `engine._handle_revision` → `self.execute(...)`), never inside a parent dispatch loop — `grep` finds no `self._handle_revision` call anywhere in `engine.py`. **Conclusion: no `pipeline_cancelled` that reaches this loop means "continue."**
- **Q1 answered before shipping: yes, an empty `wr.output` is safe, and it is not even a new row shape.** `status='cancelled'` with a null/empty `output` is what the **Stop button already produces today** (`engine.py:2381-2404` returns *before* deliverable resolution, so `_apply_terminal_output_columns` never sees a `pipeline_complete` and `run_commands.py:2085-2086`'s `if final_output:` never fires), and what the declared-gate reject at `:2454-2479` has always produced. The frontend handles it deliberately: `PreviewPanel.tsx:620-643` computes `showCancelledAffordance` and `:424-432` renders purpose-written copy — *"This run was cancelled / The run was stopped before producing a deliverable."* `page.tsx:2367-2369` excludes `cancelled` from `isContentTerminal` **and** truthiness-guards `fullRun.output`, so no renderer receives it; the history list never receives `output` at all (`runs.py:145-176` omits it from the list schema). Existing coverage pins the shape: `WorkflowHistory.test.tsx:246-253` (`status:"cancelled", output:""`) and `e2e/tests/ts-t.history.spec.ts:37-63` (`output: null`). **Behaviour change worth knowing:** a rejected run previously published the *rejected* artifact as its deliverable; it no longer does.
- **Verification.** 7 tests (**TEST-016**), 6 seen RED first with their real output; the 7th is the WR-03 guard, green by design and proven by **mutation** — deleting WR-03's `return` makes it fail. `test_restart_resume.py` **60 → 64 passed**; `test_fanout_cancel.py` **6 → 9 passed**; fan-out/wave/kernel-services/budget sweep **141 passed, 3 skipped**; every other real-`KernelServices` double site **130 passed**. Goldens **10 passed with 0 golden files modified** and `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken**, both identical to `c0bbb6e2`. The 11 known pre-existing reds are **unmoved with identical ids**.
- **The oracle limitation, stated rather than glossed.** The characterization goldens compile `gate_agent_ids=[]` (`_scripted_model.py:649`), so **not one golden contains a `review_gate_ready` or a `pipeline_cancelled`**. They are structurally incapable of detecting this change and prove only that nothing else moved. The seven tests are the only real oracle for FIX-232 — a fact any future reviewer weighing "the goldens are green" must know.
- **Collateral fixed, not worked around.** `test_fanout.py`'s two `_FakeEngine` doubles construct a REAL `KernelServices` and carried no `_state_machine`, so the new predicate raised `AttributeError` there (3 tests). The production predicate was kept **direct** rather than defensively guarded: every other `self._engine.X` access in `kernel_services.py` is unguarded, production's only construction is `engine.py:2101` with `engine=self` (and `_state_machine` is set unconditionally at `:838`), and a silent degrade would make broken engine wiring read as "not terminal" — hiding the exact bug class the check exists to catch. The doubles now carry their own `StateMachine`.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved; no browser was driven.** One build is 5–21M tokens. Every proof here is offline, and the Q1 frontend answer is a code-read finding, explicitly not a runtime one.
- **Filed, not fixed. ISS-097** (major) — `run_worker` builds its worker step with `gates=[]`, but `_should_gate` (`engine.py:4861-4864`) reads `ectx.gate_agent_ids`, and a `fanout: agent: self` worker shares its parent's agent id: ticking that agent in the per-run gate selector may open an inline review gate in **every** worker. Untested; reachable only through the launch wizard's gate selector. **ISS-098** (trivial) — a mid-wave `CancelledError` leaves its `wave_runs` row `running` because `wave_scheduler.py:340`'s `except Exception:` cannot catch a `BaseException`; WR-01's stale-row sweep self-corrects it on resume. **ISS-099** (minor, dormant) — with `step.retry.max_attempts > 0`, `_dispatch_step_with_retry` yields `step_completed` after a `pipeline_cancelled`, recording a rejected step as reusable by `_find_reused_completion`; no shipped manifest declares `retry`, but `agents/workflows/selections.py` accepts one from a composed workflow.
- **Deferred, deliberately.** A live Bedrock gated drive proving the rejection stops a real run, and the history/results view of a gate-cancelled run in a browser. Both belong to the end-of-milestone live pass; the cheap probe is a `user_stories` gated drive, **not** an `od_prototype` build.

## Quick 260812-gsf — the Concierge stops being pre-fed the whole run, and starts being billed for (FIX-233 / TEST-017)

> **Commits `47c7672f` (counting) + `7b79e426` (bounded tool surface) plus the docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-092**. Files **ISS-100** + **ISS-101** + **ISS-102**.

- **The defect, two compounding halves.** (a) `concierge.py:365` drained the runner with a bare `if event["type"] != "chunk": continue`, discarding every `usage` event the adapter emits per model turn — and because `converse` runs in a background task spawned by `POST /api/runs/{id}/messages` **after** the run has settled, outside `execute()`'s lifetime, neither the engine's `aux_token_usage` fold nor `_apply_terminal_completion` could ever reach it. Concierge spend did not merely under-report; it did not exist. (b) `concierge.py:434` called `scoped_store.read_events(run_id, 0)` — no LIMIT, no type filter — and the system prompt at `:509` **ordered** the model to "always call read_events for real progress". Re-derived to the digit from `backend/dev.db`: one question re-fed **9,227,107 chars ≈ 2,306,776 tokens**. On `caa5d175` a single chat read was **144%** of everything the pipeline recorded; on `a7dba362`, **151%**. One question could cost more input than the build that produced the run.
- **The issue row blamed the wrong event type, and the fix design turned on that correction.** ISS-092 said "200k+ `agent_chunk` payloads". Measured: the largest `agent_chunk` payload in that run is **169 chars**; `agent_chunk` matters by count (12,042 rows / 1.47M chars), not size. The payload is **18 `agent_input` rows totalling 7,290,638 chars — 79% of the run's entire event payload — one of them 479,605**, plus one 389,881-char `planner_complete`. **A type filter that dropped `agent_chunk` but kept `agent_input` would have fixed almost nothing**, which is why the fix is an allow-list, not a deny-list.
- **There were THREE unbounded tools, not one.** The row named only `read_events`. `list_refs()` projected `artifact_refs.content` — full bodies inline — **5,804,067 chars ≈ 1.45M tokens in a single call** on run `6e38b9a7`; `get_ref()` returned single bodies up to **389,651 chars ≈ 97k tokens**. A fourth unbounded source was found while planning and never appeared in any row: `workflow_runs.agent_outputs` reaches **7,450,942 chars** and embeds every agent's full `input_prompt`, so the replacement `get_agent_output` projects `output` only.
- **The fix is a tool redesign, not a LIMIT.** `read_events`, `list_refs` and `get_ref` are **DELETED** (INV-12 — nothing shadows its replacement), superseded by seven bounded, on-demand tools: `get_run_progress` (derived COUNTS, not rows), `list_agents`, `get_agent_output`, `list_artifacts` (metadata only, `content` stripped), `get_artifact`, `read_recent_events`, `read_gate_history`. `read_recent_events` intersects its `types` argument **server-side** with a module-level allow-list from which `agent_input`, `agent_chunk`, `tool_call`, `tool_result` and `planner_complete` are absent and therefore unrequestable however the model asks.
- **The authorization invariant was preserved deliberately.** Every tool is a `@tool` **closure over `(scoped_store, run_id)`** — `run_id` is never a tool parameter, which is precisely what leaves the model no syntax for naming another run. `test_no_tool_accepts_a_run_id_argument` introspects each tool's arg schema so this cannot be undone by accident.
- **The bound lives in SQL, via one new sibling — not by capping the replay primitive.** `ScopedStore.read_events_of_types(run_id, types, *, limit, after_seq=0)` mirrors the existing `last_event_of_types`, generalising `LIMIT 1` to `LIMIT n`, same `_scope_owner_ws` default-deny filter, same `_acquire` / `finally: if owned: session.close()` idiom (**mandatory** — `run_stream.py` feeds a session-less store, so a skipped `finally` leaks one pooled connection per live stream). An empty `types` returns `[]` rather than degrading to "everything". **`read_events` itself is untouched**: it is the replay primitive behind SSE resume, the events API, engine resume and `append_event_next_seq`'s own seq allocation — 18+ callers — and capping it would silently truncate replays.
- **Security fix 1, and it was observed rather than inferred.** `exclude_builtin_tools` was never passed, so `deep_agent_runner.py:328` excluded only the sub-agent `task` tool and the model was handed `write_file`, `edit_file`, `read_file`, `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, `write_todos` — **a filesystem WRITE surface on an app REST path**, while this module's own docstring claimed "read + propose only". A fake `BaseChatModel` recording `bind_tools` showed all seven at HEAD. Fixed with `exclude_builtin_tools=True`; the docstring was corrected in the same commit. **The side effect was asserted, not assumed:** `_sanitize_fabricated_xml = exclude_builtin_tools and not self.tools` stays `False` because the Concierge always has custom tools, so the output path is unchanged.
- **Security fix 2.** `ScopedStore.get_ref` (`authz.py:212-227`) filters `owner_id` + visibility but **never `run_id`**, so a `ref_id` injected via untrusted run content could pull an artifact body from a different run of the same owner — and via `visibility in ('workspace','public')`, another workspace. Not cross-owner (no IDOR), but a real cross-run scope escape on a surface whose own prompt declares run content untrusted. `get_artifact` now asserts `row.run_id == run_id`. Fixed in the tool, not in `ScopedStore`, because the closure is the only layer that knows which run is in scope.
- **Multi-turn was the trap, and it was handled rather than discovered later.** The Concierge has **no checkpointer** (`thread_id` is inert) and `_ConciergeCtx` never set `conversation_context`, so cross-turn coherence came **solely** from `read_events` happening to return the chat rows buried inside the flood. Deleting it naively would have killed multi-turn silently. The replacement was **reused, not rebuilt** (INV-12): `converse` resolves the already-registered `context_provider:conversation` + `compaction:chat_history` through the registry (the legal kernel→capability direction this module already uses for `@register`), and `_ConciergeCtx` declares `current_spec_injects={"conversation"}`. The provider's self-gate at `conversation.py:69-71` was **NOT relaxed** — that gate is what keeps it dormant for pipeline agents and the goldens byte-identical; verified that no `AGENT.md` or `workflow.yaml` declares the inject and the only production setter is `engine.py:8955`. The previously-dead `_DEFAULT_CONTEXT_BUDGET` (`concierge.py:61`, referenced nowhere in the repo) is finally wired as the transcript budget.
- **The prompt had to move with the tools.** `_compose_system_prompt` hard-coded `read_events` in two places; left alone, the model would call a tool that no longer exists. Both were rewritten, plus a cheapest-first TOOLS block instructing the model to report `truncated=true` honestly and never state an unfetched number. Kept **verbatim** as out-of-scope: RESPONSE RULES, the revision/chain INTENT ROUTING, the untrusted-content instruction, and the c72 `chain_hints` block. `test_system_prompt_names_only_existing_tools` guards the exact bug this refactor invites.
- **Counting shipped FIRST, as its own commit, and that ordering was the point.** It is ~15 lines and near-zero risk, and the tool redesign's effect is only assertable once the number exists. `converse` **sums** the per-turn usage (a tool-calling Concierge takes several turns; overwriting would report only the last) onto the per-request ctx — never the singleton capability, which still holds no state. `_drive` writes one durable `chat_usage` `run_events` row per answered turn, `event_id=chat-usage:{message_id}`, so `append_event_next_seq`'s existing idempotency makes a retried POST a no-op rather than a double count. **No migration** — a `run_events` row is legal at any lifecycle point (`chat_reply` already proves it on terminal runs) and replays through SSE for free.
- **Reported as a separate line, not the headline — three reasons, in descending weight.** (1) Comparability: `workflow_runs.token_usage` answers "what does this workflow cost to run"; folding in a user's chattiness makes two runs of the same workflow non-comparable, and the noise is unbounded. (2) Terminal immutability: `_apply_terminal_completion` is documented as the SOLE writer of those columns, has already run, and never runs again — a post-terminal writer would be a straight INV-12 violation on a seam this codebase deliberately consolidated. (3) INV-3: the headline is priced inside `pipeline_complete`, which the 5 characterization goldens pin. The FE slot already exists and degrades to hidden (`ChatTokenWidget.tsx:38-48`).
- **The non-negotiable rule was encoded as a test, not a comment.** An absent `ctx.usage` writes **no** row, and a turn whose model reports no usage records zeros — never a figure derived from `len(chat_reply)`, which would put a fabricated number where a real one is one event-branch away and poison ISS-034's cache-savings percentage downstream.
- **Verification.** 22 tests (**TEST-017**), **every one seen RED first**. The flagship — feed a fake store 12,000 rows including a 480,000-char `agent_input` and assert every tool returns under 25k chars — named all three offenders in one failure: `read_events=3,607,954 chars, list_refs=400,140, get_ref=400,138`. Goldens **10 passed with 0 golden files moved**, `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken**, `test_banned_patterns.py` **14 passed** with **zero `create_deep_agent`** in this module (INV-13) — all identical to the pre-change commit `5b004e1c`. The 11 pre-existing engine/gate reds and the 3 pre-existing `TestRouting` reds are unmoved with identical ids.
- **The one surviving Concierge red was checked, not labelled.** `test_compose_system_prompt_injects_chain_hints_block` asserts `"follow-up" not in prompt`; both hits are FIX-213/FIX-115 base-prompt text ("follow-up questions", "follow-up workflow") in blocks this change never touched, and the rewrite adds neither `"follow-up"` nor `"chained into"` — verified by rendering the prompt and grepping it, so the failure mode is byte-identical to baseline.
- **Two existing tests were reconciled, never weakened.** `test_read_tools_go_through_scoped_store_and_deny_cross_owner` and `test_read_tools_serialize_rows_to_plain_dicts` named the deleted `read_events` tool; both were retargeted onto `read_recent_events`, keeping their default-deny and plain-dict-projection assertions intact.
- **The proof that costs nothing and settles the question.** The **shipped** tools were driven over real `backend/dev.db` rows at all 15 recorded `chat_message` points — a measurement of the code on production-shaped data, not a SQL model: worst case **2,494,799 → 4,710 est. tokens (530×)**, and **no fully tool-saturated turn anywhere in the corpus exceeds 4,785**. The largest single tool result is 12,690 chars against a 25,000-char test ceiling. Script kept out of the repo (scratchpad); the numbers are reproduced in TEST-017.
- **The honest tradeoff, stated because it is a prediction.** Tool-calling turns one huge model call into 2–4 small ones, so latency may rise even as spend falls 60–550×. That is now **measurable** rather than arguable, which is exactly why counting landed first.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved; not one Concierge message was sent; no browser was driven.** One build is 5–21M tokens and one chat question was the 2.3M-token defect itself. Every proof here is offline.
- **Filed, not fixed. ISS-100** (major) — the handoff pipeline's spend is 100% unmetered and `handoff_sessions` has no token column, so there is nowhere to put the number; deliberately split out because it shares no code, ctx or lifecycle with the Concierge and is unverifiable offline. **ISS-101** (minor) — `context_provider:conversation` still does a full `read_events` server-side; not a token cost and not a regression, but now unconditional per turn, and the bounded sibling to fix it already exists. **ISS-102** (major) — three `TestRouting` tests reach a real `build_model()` and attempt a live Bedrock call; they cost nothing here only because the SSO token was expired.
- **Deferred, deliberately.** Whether the live model actually PICKS the right tool for a given question is prompt-following and cannot be proven offline; offline proves the tools exist, are bounded, are run-scoped and are described. One supervised live question on an already-completed run would settle it and read the `chat_usage` row back — bounded at ~10–15k tokens, not a pipeline run. Belongs to the end-of-milestone live pass.

## Quick 260812-hsx — the shutdown code nobody's machine had ever run (FIX-234 / TEST-018)

- **The defect was reachability, not logic.** `shutdown_run_infrastructure()` is careful, well-reasoned code with 7 passing unit tests — and on a developer machine it had never executed once. uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown` defaults to `None` (`uvicorn/config.py:215`) and `H11Protocol.shutdown()` does NOT close a connection whose response is still streaming; it only clears keep-alive (`h11_impl.py:328-337`). A live `EventSourceResponse` therefore never leaves `server_state.connections`, `_wait_tasks_to_complete()` spins forever (`server.py:294-310`), and `await self.lifespan.shutdown()` on line 292 is never reached. **The tests covered the code that was never reached** — that is the whole lesson of this row.
- **Production was never affected; the gap was documentation.** `backend/docker-entrypoint.sh:35` has passed `--timeout-graceful-shutdown 5` since KAN-151 D8. No in-repo document told a developer to, and the command appeared nine different ways across thirteen files, matching what actually runs in none of them.
- **Measured, not asserted.** Throwaway uvicorn on port 8099 (the owner's `:8010` was never signalled): no flag → alive at **31.25s** with ONLY `startup_complete` recorded, `kill -9` required; with the flag → exit in **5.82s** with `lifespan_shutdown_entered` → `sse_generator_finally` → shutdown body completed.
- **`--reload` was dropped, not carried over, and that decision is measured too.** Untreated it produces **two** stuck processes rather than one — the reloader parent hangs on an unbounded `self.process.join()` (`supervisors/basereload.py:100-105`) while the child hangs on the same wait; neither exited within 20s. `watchfiles` is not installed, so `--reload` silently degrades to `StatReload` polling (`using StatReload` in the log). It also masks crashes, which `RESUME-QA-TEST-SHEET.md:20` already said.
- **The port was decided against the evidence, not against the running process.** Docs said 8000, this machine runs 8010. **8000 stays**: it is the committed default in `frontend/src/lib/env.ts:37`, `env-templates/.env.frontend:7` and `frontend/e2e/fixtures/live.ts:13`. Moving the docs to 8010 without moving those three would have created a new inconsistency while claiming to fix one; 8010 is recorded where it belongs, in the per-machine memory notes.
- **Ten doc locations edited, four classes deliberately left.** Left with reasons: `docs/LOCALSTACK_SMOKE_REPORT.md` (a dated report of what was run, not an instruction), `frontend/src/data/skills.ts` + `skills/ecc/flox-environments/SKILL.md` (seeded user-facing product content), `frontend/src/app/test-preview/page.tsx` (a preview fixture), and every `.planning/phases/**` / `.knowledge` point-in-time artifact. **The two out-of-repo memory notes were updated too** (`dev-runtime.md`, `local-run-bedrock.md`) — they carry the command agents actually use, so without them the fix would not have taken effect in practice.
- **The INV-12 deletion was the prerequisite, and it landed first.** `main.py:302-307` closed the checkpointer pool BEFORE `shutdown_run_infrastructure()`, whose step 4 closed it again where the module docstring promises it happens "LAST among the awaits". Idempotent, so nothing crashed — but the documented ordering was false in production as well, `main.py:296` still claimed to be "the SINGLE wiring site", and with stop-runs enabled `stop_pipeline_drivers()` would have driven runs against a pool whose `get_checkpointer()` raises. Deleted; step 4 is now the only site.
- **The blocking open question was settled, and the prior hypothesis was REVERSED.** The question was whether `asyncio.run`'s teardown already marks in-flight runs `cancelled` via the launch driver's `CancelledError` handler, making `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS=False` a lie. **Under SIGTERM it does not.** `capture_signals()` restores each signal's original disposition and then `signal.raise_signal(...)` — inside `serve()`, i.e. inside `asyncio.run` (`server.py:326-330`). SIGTERM's default disposition kills the process there, so `Runner.close()` → `_cancel_all_tasks` never runs. Proven three independent ways: driver markers absent under SIGTERM and present under SIGINT; a no-uvicorn control showing plain asyncio DOES run the handler; and a marker stamped after `server.run()` returns that never appears. **Under SIGINT it does fire — filed as ISS-103.**
- **`SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS` is now environment-differentiated (owner decision D3).** Declared default stays `False`, so every non-development ENV resolves to it and the production resume tier (Phases 45-50) is untouched; a `model_validator(mode="after")` promotes it to `True` only when `ENV=development` AND `"SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS" not in self.model_fields_set`. An explicit env var, `.env` entry or constructor argument wins in **both** directions — verified on the installed pydantic 2.12.5 / pydantic-settings 2.7.1 before the code was written.
- **The budget comment was wrong in a way a test now prevents.** It claimed "under 25s" while omitting both cancel-and-wait escalations AND the pump drain, and cited `docker-compose.yml:138` for a value at `:75`. The real figures are **24s** with stop-runs off and **30s** with it on, against a 30s `stop_grace_period` — i.e. exactly at the SIGKILL line, which is the arithmetic reason production keeps it off. The new test PARSES `stop_grace_period` from `docker-compose.yml` and the graceful window from `docker-entrypoint.sh`, so drift in either file fails it.
- **A dead branch became the live one, so it got its own coverage.** Step 3 of `shutdown_run_infrastructure()` had **zero** tests — `_drain_then_cancel` was only ever reached through the per-run `stop_run_driver`. Making the dev default `True` promoted it to the branch every developer machine runs, so `TestShutdownStopsRunsWhenEnabled` now covers both directions; both tests were seen RED under opposite mutations of the guard.
- **An existing test was reconciled, never weakened.** The env-differentiated default made every test in `test_run_shutdown.py` depend on the ambient `ENV` of whoever runs pytest; `test_pump_that_finishes_promptly_is_drained_not_cancelled` failed with a `CancelledError` because step 3 cancelled the task it had registered as its own driver. The autouse fixture now pins the branch each test asserts. No assertion was changed.

Goldens **10 passed / 0 golden files moved**, `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken**, the four known pre-existing red suites **11 failed / 54 passed** with identical ids — all compared against `9df9c1c8`.

Every experiment ran against a synthetic app mirroring only the lifespan + `EventSourceResponse` shape, on port 8099, with every pid reaped.

ISS-103** (major) — the SIGTERM/SIGINT divergence above: Ctrl-C already cancels runs, after the pool closes, and `_cancel_all_tasks` gathers with no timeout. **ISS-104** (trivial) — stale line-number cites in the shutdown-path comments. **ISS-105** (minor) — `lifespan.shutdown()` is entered before the SSE generators finish unwinding (reproduced twice, ~0.4 ms). **ISS-106** (minor) — found while correcting the budget comment this row was fixing: step 4's `pool.close()` has no timeout (`checkpointer.py:140-144`), so the documented 24s bounds only the drains and the true worst case is unbounded. The config comment and the budget test now say so rather than implying a total.
