A *production* run still resumes and finishes after a restart, because `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS` stays `False` there by design. That is **ISS-089** (durable cancel), judged worth more money than ISS-088. This row makes the shutdown path REACHABLE; only ISS-089 makes a Stop SURVIVE the process.

## Quick 260812-iqh — the reducer's accumulating fields got an identity of their own (FIX-235 / TEST-019)

- **The register row was right about the concern and wrong about three facts, and one of them was load-bearing.** It names **2** accumulating fields in `handlePipelineMessage`; there are **7**, six unprotected. Its cited evidence command finds **neither field it names** — re-run verbatim at `07197b0e`, `grep -nE '\+= 1|\.push\(|\.concat\(' src/hooks/useWorkflow.ts` returns a **comment** (`useWorkflow.ts:431`) and a **local array build** (`:954`), and zero real accumulators, because every one of them uses `[...prev.x, y]` or string `+` — an idiom that regex cannot see. That is the whole reason the sweep under-reported by 3.5x, and it is why GUARD-1 keys on a structural invariant instead of an idiom list.
- **The reducer's correctness was a property of its CALLERS.** There is exactly one dedup seam in the frontend (`shouldApplyEvent`, hoisted to the top of `handleWebSocketMessage` by CR-05), and `handlePipelineMessage` sits DOWNSTREAM of it while also being exported and called directly from two other places. That is the arrangement ISS-080 died of: it shipped behind 15 green tests and still put a wrong number on screen, because every one of those tests varied frame ORDER and never frame MULTIPLICITY.
- **`hook_run` was never protected by anything** — not, as the row says, "protected only by the class-level fix". `emit_hook_event` (`kernel_services.py:397-414`) pushes the frame straight onto the live queue instead of yielding it, so it never reaches `execute()`'s `seq`/`event_id` stamping chokepoint (`engine.py:1058-1065`): no `event_id`, no `seq`, no `run_events` row. `wsReplayState.ts:36` returns `true` unconditionally for an unstamped frame **by design**, and `run_stream.py`'s `replayed_event_ids` filter has nothing to match. Zero protection at any layer, and no frontend-only fix could have reached it.
- **A1 is 2 lines and stays TRANSIENT on purpose.** A uuid `event_id` in the frame's `data`. Routing it through `execute()` would persist a `run_events` row AND add a frame to the engine's yield stream — a golden event-multiset change (INV-3) that `_VOLATILE_STRIP_KEYS` (`_normalize.py:129-130`) strips `seq`/`event_id` from but cannot strip a whole row away. Verified before writing it: `hook_run` appears in **0 of the 10** golden files. `emit_hook_event` is the single emitter (`audit_logger` + the engine's tool call/result audit both route through it), so one stamp covers every producer. Stated trade-off: `hook_run` stays absent from the durable log, so hook rows still vanish on reload.
- **A2a is ONE gate, installed by decorating the dispatcher — not six open-coded checks.** That is what makes a future accumulating case protected by adding its type to `ACCUMULATING_FRAME_TYPES` and nothing else, and it is the difference between this and the rejected Option B (five more per-field keys), which reproduces the exact anti-pattern FIX-225's own root-cause note criticises.
- **The cursor is O(1) for a reason that is measured, not aesthetic.** `agent_chunk` is the highest-volume frame in the system (~24,791 events on run `d5dbc9f2`), so a per-frame id `Set` copied immutably on every frame is O(n^2) on replay. `lastAppliedSeq` is sound because `seq` comes from ONE monotonic per-run allocator (`engine.py:1028`, `next_seq = 1`), **both** transports carry it — live SSE stamps `data.seq`, and `getRunEvents` merges the authoritative `seq`/`event_id` COLUMNS over the payload (`api.ts:585`, verified before relying on it) — and both replay passes are seq-ordered. `appliedUnsequencedIds` catches the one frame the engine never stamps, which is why **A1 is a prerequisite, not an optional extra**.
- **The per-run boundary reuses the predicate that already existed.** Both cursor fields reset on a `pipeline_start` that is NOT `isSameRunReannounce` — the same test `agentStartEventIds` uses at `:369` (INV-2). Load-bearing, and proved so by mutation: removing the reset turns the run-2 case red. A fresh run restarts its `seq` at 1, so without the boundary run 1's high-water mark would swallow run 2's entire trace.
- **INV-12, precisely.** `agentStartEventIds` plays TWO roles — dedup key AND the data `deriveSpecRevisionCount` reads. FIX-225's `.includes(startIdentity)` guard is **DELETED** as redundant; the **ARRAY STAYS**, because deleting it would silently break ISS-083, which is queued next and reads a value derived from it. `deadRevisionRefs.source.test.ts`, which source-locks that field, is green.
- **A3's blast radius was LARGER than the investigation modelled, and that was found by looking rather than by trusting the brief.** The investigation described the shadow at `page.tsx:855` as breaking REST-replayed frames. It also breaks LIVE ones: `page.tsx:1682` rebuilds the subscribed message as `{ type, data }` and passes the run id as an ARGUMENT, so `_sourceRunId` is absent from `msg` on the live path too and per-agent payloads never carry `pipeline_run_id`. The shadow resolved to `undefined` for **every** per-agent frame on **both** paths, so the per-run store was never handed one — and FIX-201's second, deliberately UNDEDUPED replay loop existed only to work around that.
- **A3 was made MEASURABLE rather than argued.** The brief demanded measured evidence and the investigation admitted the claim was "reasoned, not tested". So the decision was extracted into `resolveFrameRunId` in `lib/wsReplayState.ts` — the module whose own docstring says the dashboard's closure "is not independently importable, so the dedup DECISION ... is extracted here as pure functions ... to be tested directly". 6 unit tests; reverting it to the pre-fix behaviour turns exactly 3 red, including the two pinning what the OLD code returned for a live and a REST-replayed agent frame. The extraction also removes the shadow **by construction** — there is no longer an inline expression that can lose the argument.
- **The bypass was deleted, and its safety was checked before deleting, not after.** The loop's `hasLiveAgents` guard skipped `pipeline_start` in the second pass so live agents were not reset to idle. That is subsumed by **ISS-075**: a `pipeline_start` naming the run already on screen MERGES the roster (`carried` map) instead of rebuilding it, so replaying it cannot reset anything.
- **A stale source-guard was RECONCILED and made TIGHTER, never deleted or loosened.** `liveRunSwitch.fix201.test.ts` asserted `expect(body).toContain("runStore.get(runId)")` — whose only occurrence in that function computed `hasLiveAgents` for the deleted bypass. Changed-behaviour, so the lock changes with it: it now forbids the second pass instead of requiring it, and it was proved non-vacuous by re-injecting the bypass (red) and removing it again (green).
- **One harness, not two.** `runFrames` was EXTRACTED from `useWorkflow.specRevisionCount.test.ts` into `src/hooks/__fixtures__/reducerHarness.ts` rather than copied — two replay harnesses would be two different definitions of "re-delivery", the one thing this suite must not have. The extraction failed loudly first (it missed two other users of `EMPTY_STATE`, 5 red) and is proven faithful by that spec's 21 tests passing on it.
- **GUARD-1 is the deliverable that stops the family recurring.** A source assertion in the shape this repo already sanctions (`deadRevisionRefs.source.test.ts` calls it "the sanctioned grep-style source assertion"), keyed on the structural invariant: **a property whose value both READS its own previous value and GROWS it**. Written against the seven known sites FIRST and validated to find **exactly 7 with zero false positives** before being trusted; both halves are asserted, so it can never silently match nothing. The one growth-only line it correctly excludes is `totalTokens: totalInput + totalOutput` — a recompute over overwritten values, which is the pattern the six broken fields should have imitated.
- **Verification, every number observed.** 12 tests seen RED first with the investigation's exact values (`output "Hello worldHello world"`, `thinkingText "step one\nstep one\n"`, `toolCalls 2`, `validationIssues 2`, `hookRuns 2` — and `hookRuns 2` on a FULL replay too, the only field nothing resets). Goldens **10 passed / 0 golden files moved**; `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken**; backend known reds **11 failed / 54 passed with an IDENTICAL ID set**; full vitest **147 failed / 824 passed -> 147 failed / 860 passed, ZERO newly-red and ZERO newly-green**; mocked Playwright **33 failed / 43 skipped / 108 passed, byte-identical**; `tsc` clean in every file touched. All compared against `07197b0e`.
- **The one Playwright ID that appeared to move was chased, not waved away.** `ts-l.token-usage` `:38` <-> `:65` swapped between full-suite runs. Run in isolation **three times on the reverted tree and three times on the changed tree**, the file gives the identical result both ways (`:65` + `:77` fail, `:38` passes). Full-suite parallelism noise. Establishing that required reverting the working tree to HEAD and restoring it from a backup — **never `git stash`**, which a gsd executor has previously used to sweep away work that was being relied on.
- **A new finding that REFUTES the investigation's stated blast radius. ISS-107**: `hook_run`'s payload never reaches the reducer. `page.tsx:915` dispatches `{ type, ...(msg.data || {}) }` — it FLATTENS `data` — while the `hook_run` case reads `msg.data`, which is therefore always `{}`. Verified empirically by driving the real reducer with both shapes: a `secret_scan`/`before_write`/`block` frame collapses to `{hook:"audit_logger", event:"", outcome:"continue", detail:{}}`. `RunChatLane.deriveSecurityBullets` filters `outcome === "block"`, so it can NEVER match. The investigation put the user-visible cost of a duplicated `hookRuns` row at "a repeated 'Secret scan blocked a write...' line"; measured, it is **zero** — the duplication was real, that consequence is not, and the only live consumer of `hookRuns` is structurally dead.
- **Filed, not folded. ISS-107** (minor) — the `hook_run` payload drop above. **ISS-108** (trivial) — `clarifications` accumulates with no per-run reset outside `startPipeline`; registered in the accumulator registry as `driver: "ui"` so GUARD-1 still sees it, but frame identity cannot reach a field grown by a direct UI call. **ISS-109** (minor, **ISS-087 neighbour — the ISS-087 fixer needs it**) — `validator_result` and `gate_passed` have ZERO producers in non-test backend code (`gate_blocked` has 3), so `validationIssues` may be dead on the wire and `checksPassed === true` structurally unreachable; the accumulator was fixed anyway, for consistency. **ISS-110** (trivial, **unobserved — flagged, not claimed**) — `hookRuns` has no per-run boundary in the reducer; deliberately not folded in, because ISS-107 means it currently drives nothing on screen and the fix would be unverifiable. Sequence it after ISS-107.
- **F2 and F3 were fixed here rather than filed** — the deliberate dedup bypass and the `frameRunId` shadow are the workaround and its cause, and leaving either would have left two implementations of one behaviour.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved; no Bedrock token spent; the backend on `:8010` was never signalled.** Everything was provable at the unit level, which is what the investigation predicted and what turned out to be true.
- **The rule, for whoever reads this next.** *A reducer field that accumulates is not done until a test has fed it the same input twice and it did not change.*

## Quick 260812-jn9 — the spec-revision cycle number loses its second producer (FIX-236 / TEST-020)

> **Commits `0312a0af` (code + tests) + `0d0d66f2` (docs), on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-083**. Files **ISS-111**, **ISS-112**, **ISS-113**, **ISS-114**. **Frontend-only: zero backend files, zero new event types, zero new deps, alembic head stays 0030.** Plan + summary: `.planning/quick/260812-jn9-iss-083-delete-the-dormant-cycle-prop-fr/`.

- **What / Why (settled).** ISS-083 reported that `ResultCard.tsx` renders `` `Revising spec — cycle ${cycle ?? 1}` `` for the `spec_revision` card while nothing passes `cycle`, and asked for it to be **wired** from `runStore.viewed.specRevisionCount`. **The facts are right; the fix is wrong, and the wiring was REJECTED.** `cycle` is not missing data — it is a **second, contradicting copy**. `spec_revision` is deliberately excluded from the inline-render branch (`:141`), so it falls through to the boxed card (`:185-200`) which renders the title **and** `message.content`; and `message.content` is the backend narrator's own text, which already reads `Revising spec — cycle {attempt}` (`chat_narrator.py:157`, unchanged since Phase 29). Had the card ever mounted, the header would have printed **"cycle 1"** (the FE `?? 1` default) directly above a body saying **"cycle 2"**. Textbook INV-12: the superseded copy is **deleted, not shadowed**.
- **Where (as-built).** `frontend/src/components/chat/ResultCard.tsx`: the `cycle` prop doc block + declaration (`:96-100`), the destructure (`:103`) and the `kind === "spec_revision" ? ... : ...` ternary (`:117-120`) are gone; `const title = spec?.title ?? "Update";` replaces the ternary, so the header falls back to `CARD_SPECS.spec_revision.title` ("Revising spec", already at `:83`); the stale file-header doc (`:16-19`) is corrected. `frontend/src/components/chat/ResultCard.test.tsx`: the self-feeding `cycle={3}` test rewritten into T1 + T1b, T2 appended, the `:13` header comment corrected. `frontend/e2e/tests/ts-chat-cards.spec.ts`: TS-CHAT-CARDS-02's stale assertion reconciled. **Nothing else was opened** — `useRunStateStore.ts`, `useWorkflow.ts`, `page.tsx`, `DashboardLayout.tsx`, `RunChatLane.tsx`, `ChatPanel.tsx` and `MessageBubble.tsx` are absent from the diff by design, and the 63 reducer specs holding green is the affirmative evidence of it.
- **Key locked decisions (do NOT contradict).** **(1) Do NOT wire `specRevisionCount` into this card.** Four independent grounds: the renderer cannot mount (see ISS-111); `IMPLEMENTATION-REGISTER.md:4214` forbids a third counter in as many words (*"ISS-063 must CONSUME `revision_cycle`, not invent a third counter"*) and the per-card value already rides the wire **twice** (the narrator `text` and `deep_link.target`, parsed to `deepLink.anchor` at `useRunChat.ts:286`); `specRevisionCount` is the run's **CURRENT** count while a chat card is a **HISTORICAL** transcript entry, so a transcript holding a cycle-1 and a cycle-2 card would paint **both** with the live number; and it would make ISS-082's accumulator (`agentStartEventIds`) load-bearing for a brand-new display for no user-visible gain. **(2) Do NOT delete the `spec_revision` card KIND.** It is a cross-stack contract declared and asserted in four places (`chat_narrator.CARD_KINDS:44-46`, `types/index.ts:79`, `useRunChat.ts:297-303`, `test_chat_narrator.py:122`), and its dormancy is a **deliberate, locked** state (FIX-220, `:4214`). Deleting a parked feature is an owner's decision with its own brief — filed as **ISS-111**, not folded in. **(3) The register row's line numbers `97-100,119` are STALE at both ends** — the doc block opens at `:96` and the row **misses the destructure at `:103`**, which any fix must touch. Two independent investigations produced two more disagreeing variants; **re-read the file, never inherit the numbers.** **(4) The em dash is U+2014** at `ResultCard.tsx:119`, `chat_narrator.py:157` and `ts-chat-cards.spec.ts:65` — checked by codepoint before the RED count was trusted, because an en dash would have matched once and gone **falsely green**. **(5) The mocked Playwright suite CAN reach this card** — see the method note below; a blanket "the backend never emits it, so e2e can't see it" is wrong.
- **Verification.** 3 frontend tests written FIRST and observed RED, then **re-observed independently by the orchestrator** on a reverted source with the new tests in place (`git checkout HEAD~1 -- ResultCard.tsx`, measure, restore — never `git stash`): **4 failed / 9 passed (13)**, with T1 failing as `expected [ <p …(1)></p>, <p></p> ] to have a length of 1 but got 2` — **the duplicate caught in the act** — T1b as `Unable to find an element with the text: Revising spec`, and T2 as `expected '"use client";…' not to match /cycle\?:\s*number/`. A **hard stop was pre-armed**: green, a throw, or a received length of 0/1 would have meant the dual-copy model was wrong and the fix had to be re-derived. After: `ResultCard.test.tsx` **1 failed / 10 passed (11) → 1 failed / 12 passed (13) with the failing ID UNCHANGED**; reducer specs **63 passed** both sides; goldens **10 passed / 0 moved**; `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken**; `test_chat_narrator.py` **36 passed** (the proof the change never crossed the wire); `tsc --noEmit` the same **2** pre-existing errors, no third. All compared against the pre-change commit `f12d99ae` and **every one re-run by the orchestrator rather than inherited from the executor**. No run launched, resumed or gate-approved; no Bedrock token spent; the backend on `:8010` never signalled.
- **Method note worth more than the counts — the brief's own instruction was wrong, and so was its first correction.** The task brief said to ignore the mocked Playwright suite because "it cannot exercise a card that is never emitted." **False:** `ts-chat-cards.spec.ts` calls `mockSse.chatReply({ cardKind: "spec_revision", … })`, which fabricates the narrator turn **client-side** and bypasses the backend narrator entirely, so it reaches the branch the backend cannot — and its `:65` assertion `toContainText("Revising spec — cycle 1")` was satisfiable **only by the `?? 1` default being deleted**, because the injected body carried no cycle string at all. The planner caught that. But its inference that the test was therefore **green** came from a stale recorded baseline file and was **also** false: measured, all three tests in that file are red on an unrelated pre-existing `beforeEach` (`getByTestId('run-chat-lane')` not found, `:27`), which **ISS-076 already names as a failing cluster**; the harness itself is healthy (`ts-b.selection.spec.ts` → 6 passed). So the edit is **landmine removal, not a regression fix** — leaving the stale assertion would have handed whoever repairs ISS-076 a **false green that silently re-blesses the dual copy this change exists to remove**. The test was corrected, never deleted or `test.fixme`d, and the gate is recorded as **UNVERIFIABLE-GREEN by execution**, proven instead by a before/after **identity** check (same 3 failures, same `beforeEach` error, no new failure mode). **The generalisable lesson: "the backend never emits X" does not imply "no test can render X" — the FE test harness is its own injection point.** Separately, `reuseExistingServer: true` was **safe here, and is not always** — it is a trap only when baselining from another worktree; with `workflow.use_worktrees=false` the running dev server serves the very tree under test on both sides.
- **The family analysis, which is the durable part. ISS-083 was the FIFTH dead counter in this family, not the third the row claims** — ISS-039 (reader deleted), FIX-164 (arm/consume over-count), FIX-163/ISS-063/FIX-221 (dead on every path for ~9 days on the flagship workflow), FIX-225 (replay double-count), and this. **The generator is a single design choice: the frontend keeps re-deriving a number the backend already computed as a string.** Three properties make it unusually rot-prone: **(a)** the authoritative value never reaches the FE **as data** — it rides `ectx` and dies at the checkpoint-thread suffix, and FIX-220 then had to *deliberately misname* its keys to keep the one reader that wants it asleep; **(b)** the counter's correct value is **0 on the overwhelming majority of runs**, so a broken counter is indistinguishable from a correct one by casual observation, which is how ISS-063 stood for nine days; **(c)** every incarnation had **zero wiring coverage** — the superseded test passed `cycle={3}` to itself, proving the renderer works *when fed* and never that anything feeds it. **The rule this earns: a test that supplies a component's input itself proves nothing about wiring — every displayed value needs one test that starts from a frame or a fixture and ends at the pixel.** **What would end the family:** put the cycle on the wire as event data and let both the banner and the card read that one field, with `deriveSpecRevisionCount` deleted rather than shadowed. That is a real design change with a real risk (arming `_revision_index` is exactly the precedence landmine in ISS-111) and needs its own brief — it was **not** smuggled in here.
- **Filed, not folded.** **ISS-111** (minor) — the kind's end-to-end unreachability **and** its branch outranking every other card kind at `chat_narrator.py:151-159`; the real ISS-083 finding, and it outlives the prop deletion. **ISS-112** (minor, user-facing) — `attachmentRefs` dormant on `StartingPointCard`, so the "image not retained" placeholder can never render and `hasContent` is under-counted. **ISS-113** (minor) — `runMeta` dormant on `AuditTab` (owner + workspace permanently null), plus the mirror-image defect that `hookRuns` is passed by `PreviewPanel.tsx:1173` but never destructured at `:443`. **ISS-114** (trivial) — the unowned `ResultCard.test.tsx` deliverable/LOCK-F red, whose open question is whether KAN-154 broke the LOCK-F guarantee or retired it; it was left red **on purpose** and used as this change's own no-regression gate. Lower-confidence sweep leftovers, mentioned once and not filed: `initialOverrides` (`AgentModelPicker`), `initialTab` (`PreviewPanel`), `showToggle` (`WizardStepper`), and the dead fallback arm of `deliverableVersion` (`RunChatLane`).

- **A finding that REFUTES the investigation's stated blast radius.** It asserted `frontend/e2e` pins none of these surfaces. **Wrong** — `e2e/tests/ts-n.review-gate.spec.ts` `TS-N-02` renders `TasksPreview` through the gate plan-preview. It was run: **8 passed / 1 skipped**, a real browser proof that the extraction is behaviour-preserving. Check the harness; do not trust a grep.
- **Filed, not folded.** **ISS-115** (trivial) — the two non-equivalent `## Task N:` parsers, named INV-12 debt. **ISS-116** (minor) — the checks badge is dead code, with the producer evidence. **ISS-117** (minor) — `validator_result`/`gate_passed`/`gate_blocked` are absent from `pipelineFrameTypes` (`useRunStateStore.ts:395-403`) and dropped by the `:405` early return, so no run reopened from history can ever show a gate verdict; **upgraded from the investigation's "suspected" to confirmed** by reading the filter.
- **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved; no Bedrock token spent; the backend on `:8010` was never signalled.** Every proof came from the read-only DB, vitest, and one mocked-SSE Playwright spec.
- **The rule, for whoever reads this next.** *A count and its label must name the same quantity. "N planned" fed from a completed-task stream is not a versioning bug — it is a category error that a version picker merely exposed.*

## Quick 260812-lfv — the test suite can no longer spend the owner's money (FIX-238 / TEST-022)

> **Commits `fb545b6e` (guard + fixture) and `73305b41` (the guard's own tests), on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-102** (and corrects two errors in its row). Files **ISS-118**, **ISS-119**. Test-infrastructure only — **zero production files touched**.

- **What / Why (settled).** Two tests in `tests/unit/test_chat_messages_endpoint.py::TestRouting` reached a **real, billable AWS Bedrock `ConverseStream`** on every suite run. They did not monkeypatch `run_commands._resolve_concierge` (all three sibling classes do), so the endpoint resolved the real `ConciergeCapability` → `model=None` → `build_model()` → `ChatBedrockConverse`. The calls had always failed on an expired SSO token, so they cost nothing and nobody looked; SSO went live on this machine on 2026-08-12 and the safety net vanished.
- **The framing in the ISS-102 row was wrong twice, and both corrections matter.** It is **two** tests, not three — `test_terminal_routes_to_revision` dies earlier at `run_commands.py:2497` on `AttributeError: '_FakeUser' object has no attribute 'tier'` and never reaches a model. And it is **two calls**, not "four attempts per run" — the 4 was a grep miscount (2 ERROR lines + the same 2 exceptions echoed inside their tracebacks). Both established by per-test log attribution before any edit.
- **Where (as-built).** `backend/tests/conftest.py` — the root conftest for `testpaths = ["tests"]` — gains `_forbid_live_model_clients`, a function-scoped autouse fixture, plus `LiveModelClientConstructed`, `_guarded_classes()` and the `_CONSTRUCTS_BUT_NEVER_INVOKES` allow-list. `tests/unit/test_chat_messages_endpoint.py::TestRouting` gains a class-placed autouse `_no_live_concierge`. `tests/unit/test_iss102_live_model_guard.py` is new (6 cases).
- **The chokepoint decision is the whole point, and it was ESTABLISHED, not assumed.** The obvious guard — "fail any test that reaches `build_model()`" — is **theatre**, and the evidence says so: `agents/planner/smart_planner.py:167-201` builds its own `ChatAnthropic`/`ChatBedrockConverse` **without** `build_model`, and `deepagents.create_deep_agent(model="anthropic:…")` has langchain's `init_chat_model` build a `ChatAnthropic` from a string. A sweep found **10** offending tests; a `build_model` guard would have missed **6** of them. It would also be defeated by the by-value `from app.agents.model_factory import build_model` imports at `deep_agent_runner.py:58` and `cached_invoke.py:44`. The app has no other route — no `init_chat_model` call, no direct boto3 `bedrock-runtime` invoke, no raw anthropic/httpx call — so **the three provider CLASSES are the true single chokepoint**.
- **Why it patches `__init__` and never the class object.** Replacing the class breaks `isinstance(request.model, ChatBedrockConverse)` at `deep_agent_runner._maybe_apply:234` and `cached_invoke:79` (a non-class second argument raises `TypeError`), and breaks `tests/agents/test_bedrock_cache_and_thinking.py::_bedrock_instance`, which builds an uninitialised instance with `object.__new__`. Patching the method keeps class identity, so both survive — verified before the design was chosen, and now pinned by `test_guard_preserves_isinstance_and_object_new`. Tests that swap the whole class attribute on the source module (`test_model_factory.py:77/83/89`, the `cap` fixture) are untouched: the factory picks up their stub and never reaches the real class.
- **The exception derives from `BaseException`, and that is not a style choice.** `run_commands.py:1513` wraps `concierge.converse(...)` — inside which `build_model()` runs — in a bare `except Exception`, and `deep_agent_runner.py:586` does the same. That pair is **exactly how the original `ExpiredTokenException` became a log line instead of a test failure**. An `Exception`-derived guard error would have been swallowed on the very path it exists to police, and the guard would have been silent. Verified on pytest 8.3.4: a custom `BaseException` subclass is reported as a normal `FAILED` and the session continues; the same probe showed an `Exception` subclass being silently eaten.
- **Three allowances, no others** (`RUN_LIVE_BEDROCK=1`; the `requires_api_key` marker; exact-nodeid membership in `_CONSTRUCTS_BUT_NEVER_INVOKES`). The first two are the project's **existing** live gates, established by reading `test_clarify_llm_live.py:65`, `test_phase3_token_delta_live.py:78`, `test_phase8_live.py` and `test_pipeline_workflows.py:53` — not invented here. All three were exercised independently.
- **Why a nodeid dict rather than a marker on each test.** The whole guard stays in ONE reviewable, greppable file instead of scattering exemptions across four test files, and it **fails CLOSED**: rename an exempted test and it drops out of the dict, so the guard fires loudly instead of keeping an exemption it should have lost. `test_allow_list_entries_all_still_exist` turns that property into an assertion.
- **Filed, not folded.** **ISS-118** — the other 8 offline tests that construct a live client but never invoke it (5 of them through the SmartPlanner bypass). They are green today and were left green and unmodified; patching 8 tests across 4 files inside a money fix is the silent long tail. **ISS-119** — the two `TestRouting` tests **stay red on purpose**: they assert `answers`/`gate` where `chat_router.route_chat_turn` now deliberately returns `concierge`, because a bare-text turn must not auto-answer a questionnaire or default a gate to `approve`. Reconciling a safety-critical routing contract is an owner decision, not a side effect.
- **Verification.** All 6 new cases pass; the 4 "blocks" cases were **seen RED first** by standing the guard down through its own `RUN_LIVE_BEDROCK=1` allowance — 4 failed / 2 passed with it down, 6 passed with it up, and **zero** network calls either way because every case constructs without invoking. `tests/unit` 62 failed / 1167 passed → 62 / **1173** (+6 = exactly the new file) with the FAILED **id set identical**; `tests/agents`+`properties`+`integration` **57 / 1723 / 42 unchanged, id set identical, 0 guard trips**; goldens **10 passed / 0 files moved** (15 checksums byte-identical to `d31a5a7b`); lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**. The money proof: `ExpiredTokenException|ConverseStream` grep hits in the target file went **4 → 0**.
- **How the defect was proven without spending anything.** The credentials in the resolved `default` profile were expired, verified BEFORE any test ran (`aws sts get-caller-identity` with no profile → exit **254**, `ExpiredToken`), and `AWS_PROFILE` was never exported. AWS rejects at authentication, before inference, and does not bill rejected auth. A second, stronger proof needed no wire at all: a prototype guard patched the constructor and recorded the reach, so the call was refused **before** a client existed.
- **The fact that makes this permanent, not a one-off.** The suite has **no offline-by-default state**. `AWS_REGION` (`app/core/config.py:130`), `BEDROCK_INFERENCE_PROFILE_ID` (`:123`) and `BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` (`:118`) are hardcoded **code** defaults and there is no `backend/.env`, so unsetting environment variables can never make `build_model()` offline. Before this change, the only thing between the test suite and an AWS bill was whether credentials happened to resolve.
- **The rule, for whoever reads this next.** *A test that is red for an unrelated reason is a test nobody reads the output of — which is where a money leak hides indefinitely. And a guard is only as good as its narrowest bypass: guard the seam every path must cross, not the one the tidy path happens to use.*

## Quick 260812-mq5 — prompt caching's dollar effect becomes visible, and it is NEGATIVE on most runs (FIX-239 / TEST-023)

> **Commit `c5b4a818` on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-034** (and refutes its own framing). Files **ISS-120**. Scoped by owner decision **D2**: backend half + a SIGNED line on the Analytics page only, **no per-run badge**.

- **What / Why (settled).** The two run-cost sites priced only what was *actually paid*, with no counterfactual, so the effect of `BEDROCK_PROMPT_CACHE_ENABLED` was unobservable anywhere in the product. ISS-034 asked for a "saved $Y (Z%)" surface. **That framing is refuted by the repo's own data and was deliberately not built.** Re-derived read-only from `backend/dev.db` through the **real** shared `estimate_cost_usd` (not a re-implementation), with **0 reconciliation mismatches across all 11 persisted rows**: **6 of 11 runs are strictly NEGATIVE** (-4.98% .. -8.86%), **1 exactly zero**, **4 positive**. The **+80.34%** aggregate ($17.689716 cached vs $89.978487 uncached) is carried by two long prototype runs — **the fleet number hides a real per-run regression.** A UI that could only say "saved" would be wrong on the **majority** of runs in the only dataset that exists.
- **The discriminator is run LENGTH, not workflow type.** `ec7fb984` is an `od_prototype` cancelled early (`cache_read=11,225`, `cache_write=148,379`) at **-4.98%**, while every `user_stories` run has `cache_read=0` with a non-zero `cache_write`. Mechanism: a cache entry bills at `cache_write_5m = 1.25x` the input rate (`agents/capabilities/model_catalog.py:82`), so any turn that writes a cache entry nothing later re-reads is a pure 25% surcharge on that content. **This is why ISS-120 must not be keyed on a workflow name (INV-1).**
- **Where (as-built).** `engine.py:2881-2891` emits `estimated_cost_full_usd` on `pipeline_complete`; `run_commands.py:2179-2189` persists it in `workflow_runs.token_usage` (the documented **SOLE** writer of those columns — confirmed: the only other `token_usage =` in the tree is `runs.py:1361`, a **reader**). `_normalize.py:218-227` strips it. `analytics.py` gains `spend_full` + `metered_runs` and the legacy-safe fold. `api.ts` mirrors the two fields; `AnalyticsPage.tsx` renders the signed line beneath the existing "Total spend" row.
- **Every cited line number had drifted, and a third cost site existed that nobody had mentioned.** The analysis said `engine.py:2842-2855` / `run_commands.py:2100-2115`; D2 said `:2847-2854` / `:2107-2114`; **actual at `c05906c0` was `:2873-2880` and `:2171-2178`.** A **third** `estimate_cost_usd` at `run_commands.py:1574` is the Concierge `chat_usage` per-message writer (FIX-233) — a *different* writer on a *different* record, correctly left untouched. **Grep the cost sites; do not trust a cited range.**
- **The catastrophic-number trap was real, and was reproduced before it was prevented.** `analytics.py:_num` coerces an absent field to `0.0`, and **0 of 11 existing rows carry the new key** (measured, not assumed). With the naive `spend_full = sum(_num(usage.get("estimated_cost_full_usd")))`, the legacy-window test failed with **`spend_full = 0.0` against `spend = 15.0`** — the **-100%** figure D2 predicted — and the mixed-window test with `0.32011` against `2.32011`. The fix is one clause: `r_cost_full = _num(...) or r_cost`, so **an unmeasured run contributes exactly zero delta, never a fabricated $0 baseline**, plus `metered_runs` so the UI states its coverage instead of implying the whole window.
- **Golden neutrality was PROVEN in both directions, not asserted.** Key emitted **and** stripped → **10 passed**, and all **15** golden files verified **byte-identical by SHA-256** (a stronger claim than "the suite passed"). Key emitted and **NOT** stripped, as a deliberate control → **5 failed / 5 passed**: every `*_event_snapshot` red, the 5 survivors being the deliverable BYTE snapshots which do not read the event payload. That pair is what proves the green run is caused by the strip rather than by the key silently never being emitted. **Zero regeneration; `SNAPSHOT_UPDATE` appears nowhere in the diff.**
- **D2's mandated footnote was stale, and was corrected against the code rather than pasted.** D2 required "Concierge chat and handoff runs are not yet metered". Verified at HEAD: the Concierge **is** metered per message — `concierge.py:578-609` accumulates a `usage_total` onto `ctx.usage` and `run_commands.py:1559-1583` writes a `chat_usage` event carrying its own `estimated_cost_usd` (FIX-233) — but `chat_usage` has **ZERO readers** anywhere, and Analytics reads only `workflow_runs.token_usage`, so chat spend is **recorded and excluded**, not unmetered. Handoff is genuinely unmetered: `app/services/handoff_pipeline.py` has **zero** token metering and writes **no** `WorkflowRun` rows, so handoff runs are outside the Analytics population entirely. (The analysis grepped `agents/execution_engine/handoff_pipeline.py`, **which does not exist** — the file is under `app/services/`.) Shipped wording: *"Engine agent tokens only — Concierge chat is recorded per message but not included here; handoff runs are not metered."*
- **Why the delta is honest even though the token base is incomplete (ISS-092).** Both terms are computed from the **same** base, so any token missing from the base is missing from **both**. The reported delta is therefore a true statement about the tokens that *were* measured — incomplete in magnitude, never fabricated. The *headline* run cost, by contrast, is understated by an unknown amount; this change neither worsens nor depends on that. The **percentage** is the primary figure for exactly this reason (numerator and denominator scale together); the dollar is secondary.
- **One deliberate deviation from the brief.** The render gate is on the **percentage** (`>= 0.5%`), not the dollar. An initial `>= $0.005` threshold would have suppressed run `27cb7863` (**-$0.001181, -8.86%**) — hiding precisely the negative signal D2 exists to surface, and contradicting its own "percentage primary" instruction.
- **Filed, not folded.** **ISS-120** — `BEDROCK_PROMPT_CACHE_ENABLED` (`app/core/config.py:158`) is one process-wide boolean read at exactly two sites (`deep_agent_runner.py:227`, `cached_invoke.py:71`) with **no** per-workflow/step/agent override, and caching is a measured net cost increase on short runs. A behaviour change to the model-call path has its own risk surface and its own proof obligation, so it does not ride along on a telemetry-only change — and it is now *measurable*, which was the argument for landing the telemetry first.
- **Verification.** 17 tests (8 backend + 4 analytics API + 5 frontend). The 4 feature reds were **seen RED first** (`4 failed / 4 passed` — the 4 passes are pure sign arithmetic, already true at HEAD, so they corroborate the -7.47% / +83.25% / 0.00% claims independently of the feature). The legacy-row guard and the frontend signed-copy were each proven by **mutation**: reverting `or r_cost` reproduced the -100% number; forcing `cacheSaved = true` turned the "cost more" case red and left the other 8 green. Goldens **10 passed / 0 of 15 files moved** vs `c05906c0`; lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken** vs `c05906c0`; targeted pricing/analytics suite **71 → 83 passed**; `AnalyticsPage.test.tsx` **4 → 9 passed**; `test_wire_parity.py` **4 F / 2 P with an identical failing-id set** (pre-existing, stale `*.wsframes.json` goldens — **not** regenerated); `tsc --noEmit` the same **2** pre-existing errors. **No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved and no Bedrock token was spent** — the 11 persisted rows were sufficient evidence.
- **Deferred, stated plainly.** No live Bedrock run was exercised end-to-end, so what is *not* proven offline is that a real cached run's emitted `estimated_cost_full_usd` reconciles against a fresh `workflow_runs` row. Deferred to the end-of-milestone live pass per the standing rule. The arithmetic is anchored to observed production numbers rather than invented fixtures, which is the strongest offline substitute available.
- **The rule, for whoever reads this next.** *When a metric can go both ways, the copy must branch on the sign of the data — an unconditional label is a claim the data has not made. And a new field added to an old blob is a silent zero for every row that predates it: decide what "absent" means before you sum it.*


## Quick 260812-ppu — every chat turn during a live run destroyed one engine event (FIX-240 / TEST-024)

> **Commit `88521920` (code + tests) plus this docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-121**, whose stated root cause was **WRONG and is corrected in place**. Files **ISS-123**, **ISS-124**, **ISS-125**, **ISS-126**. Plan + measured baselines: `.planning/quick/260812-ppu-iss-121-engine-sink-drops-event-on-seq-col/`.

- **What / Why (settled).** Two `run_events` writers allocated from **one** per-run `seq` space using **two different algorithms**. The chat lane (`ScopedStore.append_event_next_seq`, `agents/authz.py:433`) takes `max(seq)+1` and **retries past an `IntegrityError`**. The engine's `_RunEventSink.persist` (`engine.py:429-462`) used a fixed in-memory counter and **swallowed the collision**: it catches `SQLAlchemyError`, `IntegrityError` is one, so a genuine `uq_run_events_scope_seq` rejection took the branch written for *"the offline harness has no schema"* and was indistinguishable in the logs from it. Net effect: **every app-layer `run_events` row written while a run is live silently destroyed exactly one subsequent engine event.** The victim is whatever the engine emits next; at a gate the engine is idle, so it is **deterministically the terminal frame**.

- **The register row's root cause was wrong, and correcting it is half the value of this task.** ISS-121 read *"`pipeline_cancelled` is NEVER WRITTEN to the durable `run_events` log … the fix is to make the reopen path consult `GET /api/runs/{id}`"*. **Every measurement in that row is correct; the causal claim built on top of them is not.** `pipeline_cancelled` is written by all eight engine terminal emitters. The prescribed fix would have installed a **second source of truth for terminal state** — squarely what INV-12 exists to prevent — while leaving a corrupt durable log feeding `_reconcile_terminal_status`, the kernel restart re-arm, the conversation context provider, the Concierge and `GET /runs/{id}/events`.

- **The fingerprint that settles it.** The row claimed the log *ends* at `review_gate_ready` (seq 278). It does not. Seq 279 is a narrator `chat_reply` card, 280 is the user's `chat_message` "Not what I wanted — stop.", and **281 is a `chat_reply` milestone card reading "Cancelled by you"** — projected from the very `pipeline_cancelled` event whose row is missing, because the narrator projects from the *live* event while only the DB write was rejected. A milestone card whose immediately-preceding row is a `chat_message` is structurally impossible unless the engine event that produced it was dropped. Also corrected: the rejection arrived through **`POST /api/runs/{id}/messages`**, not `POST /gate` — of the three gate-adjacent endpoints only `/messages` writes a durable row, so only it can reproduce this. `POST /gate` and `POST /cancel` write none.

- **Where (as-built).** `agents/authz.py` gains `append_event_at_or_after` (retry-past-a-raced-seq allocation returning the seq actually used) and the private `_max_event_seq` index probe; the stale accepted-loss note at `:462-465` is rewritten. `_RunEventSink.persist` returns `int | None` and delegates to it. Both drive loops re-stamp: `execute()` (the launch chokepoint) and `_drive_resumed_stream` (the resume driver). `app/api/run_stream.py` gains a `run_is_terminal` parameter that suppresses the D-14g gate re-arm.

- **The re-stamp is mandatory, not cosmetic.** `run_stream.py:198` renders the SSE `id:` cursor from `row.seq` on durable replay and `:264` from `data["seq"]` on the live drain. A retry that persisted at a different seq without re-stamping the outgoing frame would make those two disagree and corrupt `Last-Event-ID` resumption — a worse bug than the one being fixed. The idiom used is the one already three lines away at `engine.py:1078-1079`, where the milestone-card path advances the same counter (INV-12: no second mechanism).

- **The obvious retry was rejected on cost, and the replacement is bounded.** Having the sink allocate through `append_event_next_seq` was considered and refused: that method calls `read_events(run_id, after_seq=0)`, materialising every row of the run — the local corpus holds a 26k-row and a 36k-row run — per write. `_max_event_seq` is a `func.max` aggregate over the `uq_run_events_scope_seq` index instead, and it runs **only** on a rejection, never on the happy path.

- **The discriminator is the load-bearing part, and it was MEASURED rather than reasoned about.** A rejection is retried only when the measured tail actually reaches the attempted seq; otherwise nothing occupies that seq, the constraint that fired was a different one, and it re-raises immediately. This matters because the characterization harness's persist failure was captured directly (`pytest -o log_cli=true --log-cli-level=WARNING`) and is a `sqlite3.IntegrityError` **FOREIGN KEY constraint failed** — the `workflow_runs` parent row is absent — **not** the `OperationalError` that the degrade branch's own comment ("no schema") implies. A naive "retry on IntegrityError" would therefore have burned 8 attempts per event across every golden **and** re-stamped `data["seq"]`, breaking `assert_seq_contiguous`.

- **The claimed INV-3 hazard was refuted before the design was chosen; the real one is different.** The concern that persisting a new row perturbs the golden event multiset is false here: goldens snapshot the **yielded stream** and the deliverable bytes, run against no database (every persist already degrades), strip `seq`/`event_id` via `_VOLATILE_STRIP_KEYS`, and contain zero `review_gate_ready` and zero `pipeline_cancelled` because they compile `gate_agent_ids=[]`. Row is not frame. **The real hazard is `assert_seq_contiguous`** (`characterization/_normalize.py:297-320`), which pins `data["seq"]` DELTAS at exactly 1 on the RAW, pre-normalize stream — so a *retry-and-re-stamp* design is safe while a *pre-allocate / reserve-gaps* design would not be. Goldens are therefore the **neutrality** gate for this fix, never the detection gate.

- **Part (b) is data repair only, and deliberately small.** Rows already lost are not retroactively recoverable, so the D-14g SSE gate re-arm now consults the persisted `WorkflowRun.status`, reusing the exported `chat_router.TERMINAL_STATUSES` rather than restating a third copy of it. `agents/capabilities/gate_pendency.py` stays **pure** — the import-linter contract forbids `agents.capabilities` importing `app.*`, so the status cross-check belongs to the caller. **No synthetic event is back-filled**: fabricating durable rows with no `event_id` provenance would make the log lie about what the engine emitted. The other `derive_open_gate` call site (`run_commands.py:1257`) was checked and deliberately left alone — it is already fenced by KAN-100 through `route_chat_turn`'s `dispatch.fenced`, and a second guard there would be the duplication this fix exists to remove.

- **Why it shipped, which is the durable lesson.** `tests/unit/test_run_events.py::test_append_event_next_seq_retries_past_a_raced_seq` has existed since Phase 29 and proves the chat writer **WINS** a seq collision. Nothing ever asked what happened to the **loser**. The whole defect lived in that missing half.

- **Verification.** 3 new backend unit tests, **all seen RED at `9e3dc9b0` before any production edit**, and all asserting the durable **ROW** rather than the yielded frame — the live stream is intact on every path, which is exactly why ISS-091's three offline probes could not have seen this. The first RED surfaces as a `PendingRollbackError` (the rejected flush poisons the shared test session) with `UNIQUE constraint failed: run_events.run_id, run_events.owner_id, run_events.workspace_id, run_events.seq` named verbatim, so each assertion was **additionally** proven to discriminate by mutating the shipped code: retry disabled → `the engine's terminal event was silently DROPPED by the seq collision` and `assert 'pipeline_cancelled' in {'agent_chunk': 3, 'chat_message': 2, 'review_gate_ready': 1}`; guard removed → `a terminal run must NOT re-arm a dangling gate`. Both mutations reverted and re-verified (`55 passed`). Goldens **10 passed / 0 golden files moved** vs `9e3dc9b0`; lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken**; the 9-file pre-existing-red sweep **22 failed / 176 passed with an IDENTICAL ID set**, re-measured in a detached worktree (never a stash); `test_mechanical_router.py`'s 3 reds, absent from the briefed list, **verified pre-existing** by the same method; `test_restart_resume.py` and `test_resumability.py` fully green. Frontend **0 files changed**, so the known `ResultCard.test.tsx` red and the 2 `tsc` errors cannot have moved. FIX-232 untouched.

- **Filed, not folded.** **ISS-123** — up to **29 already-destroyed engine events across 10 runs** (`chat_message` 19, concierge `chat_reply` 8, `chat_usage` 2, against 233,325 rows in 16 runs), three identified by name (`questionnaire_complete` ×2, one `pipeline_cancelled`, one `agent_chunk`); not retroactively recoverable and deliberately not back-filled. **ISS-124** — `run_commands.py:2435` and `:2666` synthesise a terminal frame onto the SSE queue with no `seq`, no `event_id` and no durable row at all; same reopen symptom, different cause, and outside an engine-sink fix. **ISS-125** — `_stamp_resume_marker` (`engine.py:6309-6311`) still reads the entire log to derive one integer and appends at a fixed seq through the non-retrying primitive. **ISS-126** — the part-(b) guard covers only the **cursored** reattach (`after_seq > 0`); a fresh reopen from history sends no `Last-Event-ID`, so the symptom on already-corrupted runs comes from the durable replay itself and needs an FE-side fix, since filtering the replay would break `Last-Event-ID` semantics and synthesising a frame would install the second source of truth INV-12 forbids.

- **Money.** No run launched, resumed or gate-approved; no Bedrock token spent. Every pytest invocation was prefixed `env -u AWS_PROFILE -u AWS_REGION -u RUN_LIVE_BEDROCK ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""` and FIX-238's guard never tripped.


## Quick 260812-sgu — a HITL gate that approved every misspelled denial (FIX-241 / TEST-025)

> **Commit `c500fafa` (code + tests) plus this docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-070**, whose **scope was over-generalised** and whose **tag was wrong**; both corrected in place. Files **ISS-127**. Plan + measured baselines: `.planning/quick/260812-sgu-iss-070-gate-action-fail-closed/`.

- **What / Why (settled).** `POST /api/runs/{id}/gate` dispatched on the `action` discriminator with `else:  # approve (default)` as the terminal fallback (`run_commands.py:272`) — an exact, case-sensitive, unstripped string match. Anything that was not one of the three strings the chain checks for was treated as **consent**. Observed against the real endpoint, not reasoned: `'Reject'`, `'REJECT'`, `' reject'`, `'reject\n'`, `'rejct'`, `'no'`, `'deny'`, `'Redo'`, `'redo '`, `'update-specs'` **all returned `HTTP200` with `approved=True` and resolved the pause.** The user believes they stopped the run; the run resumes and spends the remainder of a 5–21M-token `od_prototype` budget (measured ceiling 37.3M).

- **The row understated it: the audit record was LAUNDERED.** The `else` never passed `action=`, so `store.set_review_response`'s own default (`store.py:123`) persisted `action="approve"`, while `resolve_gate:278` echoed the raw garbage string back in the HTTP response. A throwaway in-process probe printed what the store actually received: `action='rejct' → HTTP200 approved=True stored_action='approve' gate_still_armed=False`. **Response and durable row disagree, and the durable row is the clean one** — which is very likely why this has never been noticed in a live log. On the **declared**-gate path it compounds: an unknown action emits none of `_gate_rejected`/`_gate_redo`/`_gate_update_specs`, so `human.py:104-141` computes a formal **`GATE_PASS`** and writes an honest-looking audit row — the precise failure the in-file comment at `human.py:52` says the `_UPDATE_SPECS` branch exists to prevent.

- **The row's scope was wrong, and correcting it is half the value.** ISS-070 read as though the endpoint *family* was defective. **Only one of the three `set_review_response` ingresses was.** `/messages` `CHANNEL_GATE` (`:1322`) is fenced by `chat_router.py:234` — established by reading **both** `Dispatch(channel=CHANNEL_GATE)` construction sites (`chat_router.py:244` and `:255`), each of which requires `turn.action in GATE_ACTIONS`, so `dispatch.action` arriving at `:1322` is provably a member. The Concierge confirm (`:1101`) is fenced twice over: `concierge.py:348-356` normalises anything outside `_GATE_ACTIONS` to `request_changes`, and the params come from a durable, server-written proposal row (H1), never the request body. Those two are **latent hazards**, not live defects — each `else` is a fail-open default whose safety lives in a different file.

- **Retagged `api,auth` → `api,validation`, with evidence.** This is **not** an authorization defect. `resolve_gate:222` calls `_review_gate_owned_by(gate_key, current_user.id)` **before any write**, and that predicate (`run_engine.py:765`) filters `WorkflowRun.id == run_id, WorkflowRun.user_id == user_id`, returning `False` for a missing *or* cross-owner run → a non-revealing 404 with no existence oracle. **A third party cannot approve your gate.** The affected principal is the run's own owner. Severity stays **major** on three grounds: a safety gate fails OPEN; the cost is real, one-sided and unrated; and it is invisible afterwards.

- **Where (as-built).** Two files. `app/api/run_commands.py`: `GateCommand.action` becomes `Literal["approve","reject","redo","update_specs"]`; a new `_deny_unknown_gate_action` helper joins `_deny_unknown_gate` / `_deny_update_specs_not_offered` in the module's existing denial idiom; all three `set_review_response` ingresses gain an explicit `elif ... == "approve"` plus a fail-closed `else`. `tests/unit/test_rest_gate_commands.py`: 13 new cases. **Frontend: 0 files changed** — `api.ts:694` already declared the closed union; this makes the server *enforce* what the TS type only annotated.

- **Two layers, because neither alone is sufficient — and each was MUTATION-PROVED.** Layer A (schema) rejects at the wire with 422 and publishes the `enum` in OpenAPI, but validates the wire rather than the dispatch: a fifth `Literal` member, an in-process caller, or a `model_construct` bypass reopens it silently. Layer B (dispatch) holds against all of those but is a later stop and leaves `action: str` advertising an open domain. Reverting **only A** → all ten variants **HTTP400** from B; reverting **only B** → all ten **HTTP422** from A. Both mutations reverted and re-verified.

- **It REFUSES; it must never degrade to a reject.** FIX-232 makes a rejection **terminal**, so degrading an unparseable action into a denial would destroy the run on a typo — strictly worse than the bug. Refusing the *request* and leaving the gate **armed** is the only degrade that preserves every legitimate option, which is the same choice the engine already made for an ineligible `update_specs` at `engine.py:5830-5838`. 400 rather than 409 with `recoverable: true`, because re-issuing the request correctly *will* succeed — distinct from the `pipeline_not_running` / `update_specs_not_offered` state conflicts beside it.

- **`chat_router.py` was deliberately NOT touched.** Its `:234` guard **is** the ISS-119 routing contract ("a bare-text turn at a gate must NOT default to approve"), and reconciling ISS-119's two red tests is that issue's decision to make, not a side effect of this one. ISS-070 and ISS-119 are the same design intent in adjacent code; this fix stays on `resolve_gate`'s side of the line.

- **The if/elif chain was NOT restructured, on purpose.** `tests/unit/test_rest_gate_commands.py:362` is a **grep-ratchet** that reads `resolve_gate`'s *source text* and requires the literal substring `action == "redo"`. A dict dispatch, a `match` statement or a shared handler map — all of which look like the "clean" version of this fix — turn it red. Only the `else` branches changed; `:253`/`:257`/`:268` are byte-identical.

- **The default was KEPT; only the domain was constrained.** `tests/agents/test_attach_replay_matrix.py:551` posts `{"gate_key": ...}` with **no `action` key at all** and asserts 200 on the Pydantic default. A `Literal[...] = "approve"` keeps it green; making `action` **required** would break it *and* the published OpenAPI contract. Verified after the change: the schema still reports `required: ['gate_key']` with `"default": "approve"` alongside the new `enum`. A dedicated regression pin (`test_bare_gate_post_still_defaults_to_approve`) is the one new test that is green **before and after** — deliberately.

- **INV-12 — the vocabulary keeps exactly one home.** `chat_router.GATE_ACTIONS` (`:59`) is the single authority. `Literal` requires static values, so the schema necessarily spells the four strings out; rather than accept a fifth copy, `test_gate_action_literal_matches_the_single_vocabulary_authority` asserts set-equality between `get_args(GateCommand.model_fields["action"].annotation)` and `GATE_ACTIONS`. It was **seen RED at HEAD** as `set() != {'redo','update_specs','reject','approve'}` — a bare `str` annotation has no `get_args`. The three fail-closed branches share **one** `_deny_unknown_gate_action` helper, not three copies of an `HTTPException`.

- **Goldens are the neutrality gate here, never the detection gate — stated as a limitation.** `grep -c review_gate_ready` returns **0 for all 15 golden files**: they compile `gate_agent_ids=[]`, so no golden contains any gate event at all. They can prove nothing else moved; they could never have caught this. Same framing FIX-232 and FIX-240 both recorded.

- **Verification.** 13 new backend unit tests, **12 seen RED first at `e6b24ae5`** (`12 failed, 16 passed`), ten of them failing as `action='...' was accepted: {"ok":true,...}` / `assert 200 in (400, 422)`. After: `test_rest_gate_commands` **15 → 28 passed**, every variant refused with nothing written and the gate still armed. Goldens **10 passed / 0 of the 15 golden files modified** vs `e6b24ae5` (`git status --porcelain -- golden/` empty). lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken** vs `e6b24ae5`. `test_update_specs_ingress_fence` **13 passed**. The pre-existing-red set across the five gate-adjacent suites (`test_chat_messages_endpoint`, `test_gates`, `test_declared_gate_streaming`, `test_mechanical_router`, `test_rest_run_launch`) is **14 failed / 104 passed with a byte-identical failing-id set**, re-measured by swapping in `git show HEAD:...run_commands.py` and diffing the sorted `FAILED` lines — never a stash. `test_concierge_proposal_channels` + `test_attach_replay_matrix` **2 failed / 70 passed** with the same two known ids. `ruff` reports the same **3** pre-existing errors, all outside the changed regions.

- **Filed, not folded. ISS-127** — `GateCommand.analysis_report` (and its `MessageCommand` sibling) has **no length cap anywhere** on the path `run_commands.py:115` → `:264` → `engine.py:5387` → the composed prompt at `engine.py:9096`; a `grep` for slicing / `MAX_*` / `len(...)` over `agents/` + `app/` on that path returns nothing. It is a genuine cost-amplification gap but a **different defect with a different fix** (a cap plus a 422, and an owner decision about the limit), and folding it in would have obscured the RED/GREEN proof of the discriminator change. Also recorded rather than fixed: a legitimate `reject` **also** stores `action="approve"` (the reject branch likewise omits `action=`) — functionally inert, since the engine keys its terminal decision on `approved` (`engine.py:5852`/`:5859`), and changing the persisted record would be scope creep with a real blast radius on the declared-gate outcome computation.

- **Money.** No run was launched, resumed or gate-approved; no Bedrock token was spent. Every pytest invocation was prefixed `env -u AWS_PROFILE -u AWS_REGION -u RUN_LIVE_BEDROCK ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=""` and FIX-238's guard never tripped. The paused run `41f77342-…` on port 8010 was never touched.

- **The rule, for whoever reads this next.** *A dispatch's terminal `else` is a decision about the inputs you did not think of. On a safety gate, "everything else means yes" is the one answer that is never right — and if the branch also declines to record what it received, the mistake erases its own evidence.*

## Quick 260812-syf — the fan-out review gate nobody could see (FIX-242 / TEST-026)

> **Commit `91a1a1fa` (code + tests) plus this docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-097** and **raises its severity major → critical**, because the row's predicted consequence was wrong in the direction that matters. Files **ISS-129**, **ISS-130**, **ISS-131**, **ISS-132**. Plan + measured baselines: `.planning/quick/260812-syf-iss-097-fanout-worker-invocations-arm-in/260812-syf-PLAN.md`.

- **What / Why (settled).** `gate_agent_ids` was designed as a per-**step** selection — the UI's own words are "Checked agents pause the pipeline for your review after they finish" (`ReviewGatesSection.tsx:128-129`) — but `_should_gate` (`engine.py`) implements it as a per-**invocation** predicate on `spec.id`. Those two readings were identical for every workflow that existed when the selector shipped, because every step invoked its agent exactly once. Fan-out (Phase 11) broke the equivalence: `fanout.py` resolves `agent: self` to `step.agent_id`, so every worker of a self×N fan-out runs the SAME `spec.id` as its parent step and every one independently reaches `_should_gate → True`.

- **The filed row predicted "N simultaneous gates, each awaiting a human". The reality is worse.** Every worker's `review_gate_ready` is consumed and **discarded** by `run_fanout`'s worker loop, which reads only `agent_complete` for token accounting and forwards nothing. Zero gate frames reach the SSE stream; zero rows reach durable `run_events`; `derive_open_gate` returns `(None, None)`; the run stops dead with `workflow_runs.status` = `waiting_for_user` indefinitely. All N workers share ONE gate key `f"{run_id}:{agent_id}"`, so they are N arms of one slot, not N gates. **Measured offline at `eb12bc7e`** (`sample_wave`, single-wave plan, 4 workers): `_run_review_gate` entered 4×, 1 gate key, **0** frames on the wire, HUNG. Control with `gate_agent_ids=[]` completes.

- **Undiscoverable, not unresolvable.** `review_event_pending(gate_key)` returns True and the REST gate endpoint would accept a resolution — a user who *guesses* the entirely predictable key can free the run. That is an expert escape hatch, not a product behaviour. It does not compound across restarts (the restore path needs `derive_open_gate` to return a gate before re-arming, so the run parks harmlessly), but the `run_fanout` `finally` teardown never runs: every worker workspace stays allocated and every `subagent_runs` row stays `running` forever.

- **Reachable, and sticky.** The gate picker lists **every** pipeline agent with no filter (`ReviewGatesSection.tsx:131`); the visual composer's fan-out toggle (`CanvasConfigRail.tsx:284-295`) sits one click away in the same launch UI; and a saved workflow replays `gateAgentIds` on every subsequent launch (`DashboardLayout.tsx:1227-1228`). That combination is the shipped Phase-51 builder-composed fan-out, which reproduces the same hang.

- **The fix is one keyword-only invocation-scope flag.** `invocation_gated`, threaded from the two kernel sites that create invocations which are **not steps** — `run_worker` (the only non-test caller of the worker path) and `run_merge_agent` (identical invisible-hang shape: its events are consumed with a bare `pass`) — through `run_agent` into `_run_agent`, reaching all three inline gate sites (restart re-entry, revision re-open, live post-stream). **INV-12: the existing predicate is narrowed in place** (`return invocation_gated and selected`), both original branches preserved verbatim. Default `True`, so every step-shaped invocation is byte-unchanged.

- **Three designs were evaluated and rejected — recorded so they are not retried.** (a) Making `_should_gate` read `step.gates` **cannot work**: `run_worker` reuses the **parent step object, gates included**, whenever the worker is `agent: self` with no isolated workspace — exactly the offline and `shared_read` path. It is also a different mechanism (the step-boundary declared gate), and wiring one source to both is the dual implementation INV-12 forbids. (b) Parking the flag on `ExecutionContext` **races**: N workers share ONE `ectx` under `asyncio.gather`, so a save/restore field could be cleared by worker A's `finally` while worker B is mid-flight. (c) Renaming worker agent ids breaks `_spec_for`, the `allowed_workers` allow-list, fragment artifact provenance and the wave resume cursor.

- **The harness lies unless you un-shadow it — and this was measured, not assumed.** `_ResumeHarness.make_engine` assigns an empty async generator to `engine._run_review_gate` as an **instance** attribute, silently shadowing the real bound method. With `del engine._run_review_gate` removed, the *identical* test passes **GREEN in 1.07 s** against a live 4-arm hang. That is why the original investigation nearly filed ISS-097 "not reachable", and why the row's own suggested test ("count `review_gate_ready`; 1 is correct, N is the bug") would have measured **zero** and read as a pass. Any future gate assertion on that harness must un-shadow first; `_count_gate_entries` now owns and documents it.

- **A guard caught the first attempt, which is the guard working.** `test_gate_stub_signature_drift.py` — the AST census that exists for exactly this defect family — rejected an initial CLASS-level `_run_review_gate` double whose leading `engine_self` could not bind the engine's all-keyword call. The test was rewritten to the file's dominant instance-patch idiom with `*a, **kw`. Separately, the signature change exposed four test doubles pinning a stale arity (`test_fanout.py`, `test_pipeline_failure_semantics.py` ×3); all were repaired, and the two worker/merge doubles now **assert** `invocation_gated is False` rather than merely tolerating it.

- **Deliberate residual, filed not folded (ISS-131).** The step-boundary dedupe still passes `inline_gated=self._should_gate(spec, ectx)`, so a fan-out step that both declares `gates:[human]` **and** has its agent ticked now dedupes its declared gate against an inline gate that no longer fires — that step gets no gate at all. Strictly better than the pre-fix hang, but a silent loss. Left byte-unchanged so FIX-242's INV-3 dormancy argument stayed exact; the clean correction needs the **strategy** to declare whether it runs its agent inline, because the kernel must not infer that from a capability-name list. No file manifest declares gates on a fan-out step today (verified across `agents/workflows/`).

- **Also filed rather than folded.** **ISS-129** — `run_fanout`'s worker loop swallows *every* worker event including `agent_error` and `pipeline_cancelled`; it is the amplifier that turned this from an annoyance into a silent hang, and that half is still live. **ISS-130** — `run_agent` mutates shared `ExecutionContext` scratch under parallel fan-out; no contamination was observed across five instrumented runs, and the believed reason (the scratch is consumed before `_run_agent`'s first `await`) is **believed but not verified** — an undocumented invariant that any earlier `await` would silently break. **ISS-132** — the task-loop sibling gives N *visible* sequential gates on one key; suppressing it is a product decision, not a defect with one right answer.

- **Verification, and what it cannot prove.** Goldens 10 passed with **0 of the 15 golden files moved** (sha256 manifest diffed) and lint-imports 4 kept / 0 broken, both identical to `eb12bc7e` — but they are the **neutrality** gate only: `_scripted_model.py:649` is literally `gate_agent_ids=[],  # suppress all gates`, so no golden contains a single gate event and none could ever have detected this. INV-3 is argued from the flag's default-`True` dormancy. The 27-id pre-existing-red set is unchanged by ID, and the 5 reds in the seam-adjacent suites were re-measured **in a detached worktree at `eb12bc7e`** (5 failed / 38 passed, same ids, both sides) rather than claimed. FIX-232 is undisturbed — this adds a parameter and changes nothing about cancellation, terminality or the `run_fanout` teardown (`test_fanout_cancel` 9 → 9). Live verification deliberately not run: the offline harness reproduces the full defect path through the real kernel at zero spend.

## Quick 260812-tni — a Stop that survives the process (FIX-243 / TEST-027; ISS-089 closed, ISS-103 reassessed)

> **Commit `8d84b1a6` (code + tests) plus this docs commit, on `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss` — NOT pushed.** Closes **ISS-089**. Retags **ISS-103** major → minor and records why its code change is deferred. Files **ISS-133** and **ISS-134**.

- **The one sentence that generates both rows.** `WorkflowRun.status` is a projection of an in-process asyncio task's lifetime, never a durable record of what the system was **asked** to do. Every terminal-status write executes inside a task — the launch and revision drivers' `CancelledError` handlers, `_reconcile_terminal_status`, the three restore branches — and the HTTP command layer wrote none. A truth no task was alive to record simply was not recorded.

- **Two defects, and they must NOT be unified.** ISS-089 is that fact at the **command layer**: the owner's Stop reaches a process with no task to carry it. ISS-103 is the same fact at the **process-lifecycle layer**. They pull in **opposite directions on the same variable** — ISS-089 wants a *specific* run terminal because a human asked; ISS-103 concerns *all* runs at process exit, where production deliberately wants them left non-terminal so the boot scan resumes them. A single "make cancels durable at shutdown" fix would collapse the two and re-open the deploy-invisibility hole `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS=False` exists to protect. **The boundary to keep:** terminal-because-a-signal belongs to ISS-103 and must respect `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS`; terminal-because-a-human-asked belongs to ISS-089 and must ignore it.

- **The row's own proposed fix was the worse of the two available, and is recorded as rejected so it is not retried.** Option B — a durable `cancel_requested` marker checked inside `restore_non_terminal_runs` — needs a migration or a new event type; edits the resume tier's most delicate three-branch classifier to add a fourth outcome; **misses branch (a)**, because `waiting_for_user` spawns `_rearm_gate_run` without ever calling `_stamp_resume_marker`, so a marker checked before the stamp misses every gate-parked run (the row's stated ordering constraint is true but insufficient); and **leaves the row lying** — `running` to history, analytics, `/resume` eligibility and the UI until the next boot, possibly forever. Option A is strictly more correct for strictly less code.

- **What shipped: write the terminal status at cancel time.** `cancel_run`'s not-live branch now delegates to `_cancel_run_without_a_live_driver`. Terminal (or absent) row ⇒ the pre-existing `not_running` ack, **byte-identical, key order included**, no write. Non-terminal ⇒ (a) a durable `pipeline_cancelled` row through **`ScopedStore.append_event_at_or_after`** — the collision-safe append, because FIX-240/ISS-121 proved a `uq_run_events_scope_seq` rejection here is swallowed by the persist degrade — best-effort, audit + SSE replay + `_reconcile_terminal_status` agreement only; (b) `status="cancelled"` + `completed_at` through the existing `_persist_resume_status` idiom, **authoritative** — a failure answers HTTP 500 `cancel_not_persisted` rather than inheriting `_reconcile_terminal_status`'s best-effort degrade; (c) `accepted:true, cancelled:true, status:"cancelled"`.

- **Nothing new was needed, and that is the argument for the design.** **No migration** (alembic head stays `0030`), no new table, column or event type, and **no change to `restore_non_terminal_runs` at all** — `cancelled` is already outside the non-terminal set and `POST /resume` already accepts `cancelled`, so the boot scan consults the decision through the filter it already has. The run moves from **AUTOMATIC** resume to **EXPLICIT, owner-authenticated** resume, which is what a Stop should mean. The deploy-invisibility tier is untouched: a run interrupted by a deploy is still non-terminal and still adopted; the two sets are complementary by construction.

- **The prerequisite was INV-12, and it was load-bearing.** The non-terminal status tuple was an inline literal inside an 8,000-line method **and** a second copy in `scripts/cutover_legacy_runs.py:28`. Five different `file:line` values for it had been recorded in one week — `engine.py:5263`, `:5710-5713`, `:5838-5841`, `:5899-5902`, and the actual value at `2df5324b`, **`:5921`**. Copying it into the endpoint would have made three definitions. It is now one module constant, `agents.execution_engine.engine.NON_TERMINAL_RUN_STATUSES`, imported by both callers, pinned by an **AST source guard** that matches on the *value* rather than the identifier — so a copy under any name is caught. `app.api → agents.execution_engine` is the permitted direction; the banned one is the reverse, and lint-imports stayed 4 kept / 0 broken.

- **The proof is a task count, not prose.** The boot-scan test seeds a run that is genuinely **resumable in-flight** (compilable type + one durable `run_events` row — branch (b)'s actual admission condition), cancels it, then runs a fresh `restore_non_terminal_runs()` with an `asyncio.create_task` spy. Post-fix: zero tasks. At `2df5324b`, with the same setup, it observed `ExecutionEngine.restore_non_terminal_runs.<locals>._admitted_resume` being spawned for a run whose Stop had just answered `not_running`. That single line is the whole defect. Every new case was seen RED first in a **detached worktree** at `2df5324b` — never a stash — and the source guard was **mutation-tested** against the surviving duplicate rather than merely observed green.

- **Two existing tests were RECONCILED, not loosened, and the distinction matters.** `test_cancel_does_not_claim_success_without_a_live_driver` and `test_cancel_is_idempotent_with_no_active_event` both seeded `status="running"` and asserted `accepted:false` — **that assertion is the defect**. Both now seed a **terminal** run, which preserves ISS-084's anti-lie invariant ("never claim an outcome nothing achieved") in the case where it still holds; for a non-terminal run `cancelled:true` is now *earned*, because the endpoint really does make the cancellation durable. No assertion was weakened and no test deleted.

- **A test-harness hazard worth carrying forward.** The `env` fixture had to also patch `run_commands._get_db` **and** `app.models.database.SessionLocal`. Before ISS-089 the cancel endpoint never wrote, so patching `run_engine._get_db` alone was sufficient; `run_commands` binds `_get_db` at import, and `ScopedStore` / `_recover_workspace_id` open `SessionLocal()` themselves. Either seam left unpatched points the new writer at the real `dev.db`. **Whenever an endpoint gains a write, re-audit the fixture's seams — a read-only test harness is not a write-safe one.**

- **Cost framing corrected in the registers.** The recurring "5–21M tokens" understates the tokens and overstates the drama. Measured on this corpus: ceiling **37.3M tokens / $7.07** for one `od_prototype` build; the `d5dbc9f2` incident that motivated the row cost **$3.58**, of which **≈$1.61 (~45%) was billed after the API answered `cancelled: true`**; all 14 metered runs, all time, total **$17.75**. Cache reads dominate. So this is a **correctness-and-trust defect first and a cost defect second on a Haiku workload** — roughly an order of magnitude worse on an Opus-tier model, which is what the fix insures against. Say the dollars, not just the tokens, and do not inflate them.

- **Scope boundary, recorded so it cannot be assumed away (ISS-134).** Single-process only. `_is_run_live` is process-local, and today the deployment is single-process (`exec uvicorn`, no `--workers`, no replicas), so "not live here" == "not live anywhere". Under the **locked ECS Fargate to-be**, a Stop landing on instance B would mark a row cancelled while instance A kept billing, and A's own terminal write would later overwrite it. Neither ISS-089 option fixes that; it needs a cross-process liveness fact (lease/heartbeat). The constraint is in `_cancel_run_without_a_live_driver`'s docstring as well as the register.

- **ISS-103: direction fixed, severity lowered, code change deferred — with a mechanical reason, not a shrug.** The direction is **SIGINT must be made to match SIGTERM, never the reverse** (the reverse cancels every run on every deploy and pushes the teardown budget from 24 s to 30 s, onto the SIGKILL line). Severity `major → minor`: production never sends SIGINT (`exec uvicorn` ⇒ PID 1; `docker stop`/ECS send SIGTERM; a repo-wide grep for `StopSignal`/`stopSignal`/`stop_signal` returns **zero** hits), and FIX-234 already defused it locally (`settings.SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS` verified `True` at HEAD under `ENV=development`, so drivers are cancelled cooperatively inside the lifespan first). **The clean fix is unreachable from inside the application:** `uvicorn 0.34.0`'s `capture_signals()` snapshots the original handlers and reinstalls **that snapshot** in its `finally` before `raise_signal`, so any handler the app installs is discarded — and the snapshot is taken **before our code exists**, because `serve()` is `with self.capture_signals(): await self._serve(...)` and `_serve` is what calls `config.load()`, the call that imports `app.main`. The only clean alternative is to stop launching uvicorn from its CLI and run a `uvicorn.Server` we own, changing the production start command, the PID-1 process and the `--proxy-headers` / `--forwarded-allow-ips` / `--timeout-graceful-shutdown` plumbing — outward-facing, and out of scope for a quick task. **Explicitly not done:** no second terminal-write path was added beside `_drain_then_cancel`, which remains the only escalation policy.

- **ISS-103's open question is now answered by measurement: NO checkpoint is written on a driver's cancellation unwind.** A no-network, no-model probe built a LangGraph `StateGraph` on a spy checkpointer, streamed it inside a task, cancelled mid-node and gathered with no timeout (the `_cancel_all_tasks` shape). Both `astream_events` and `ainvoke`: 5 checkpoint writes total, **0 after the cancel**. LangGraph's pregel loop checkpoints around node completion; a node cancelled mid-flight writes nothing on the way out. With `get_checkpointer()` having exactly **one** non-test caller in the backend (`engine.py:1512`, the run **entry** path), sub-claim (b) stays latent — now by measurement rather than assumption. Caveat: `InMemorySaver` + a plain async node, so it pins LangGraph's write **sites**, not a hypothetical `finally` inside deepagents middleware.

- **Verification, and the money rules.** Baselines vs `2df5324b`: goldens **10 passed / 0 of the 15 golden files moved**; lint-imports **4 kept / 0 broken** (run from `backend/`); `test_run_shutdown` 9, `test_shutdown_reachability` 8, `test_restart_resume` 66, `test_fanout_cancel` 9, `test_rest_gate_commands` 28 — all unchanged; `test_rest_answers_cancel` 10 → 20. The **32-id pre-existing-red set is unchanged by ID**, and a 12-suite blast-radius sweep is 138 passed / 3 failed, those 3 being the ISS-093 stale clarify-round tests **re-measured in a detached worktree at `2df5324b`** as the same 3 ids. **No run was launched, resumed, cancelled or gate-approved.** The live backend on port 8010 was never signalled — pid 1848, uptime predating the session.
