## quick-260812-wir — durable driver terminals, terminal-reopen render, and the lost-event audit (FIX-244 / FIX-245 / FIX-246)

**Closes** ISS-124 (FIX-244), ISS-126 (FIX-245), ISS-123 (FIX-246, audited not repaired). **Files** ISS-135..141.
**Commits** `e3c38594` (backend), `2b25d3d0` (frontend), `f5df7c85` (audit script). Branch `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss`, baseline `ce2db22e`.

- **Read this before touching run-terminal state anywhere.** `workflow_runs.status` is the lifecycle authority — the boot restore scan, the `RunState` fence, the history badges and FIX-240's SSE guard all treat it that way. The run SCREEN was the one consumer that inverted it and treated the terminal EVENT as the source. FIX-245 does not add a new authority; it makes the screen agree with the existing one.

- **ISS-124 was filed `minor` and was not.** The missing durable row is only half of it. `stop_run_driver` calls `_reconcile_terminal_status` once the driver is provably gone, and that function decides purely from the durable tail — so with no `pipeline_cancelled` row it computed the D2 fail-safe `"failed"` and wrote it through an **unconditional** `_persist_resume_status`, overwriting the `"cancelled"` the driver had just set. The owner's Stop was recorded as a failure. Pointer: `app/api/run_commands.py`, the two `except asyncio.CancelledError:` branches.

- **One durable-terminal writer, three callers.** `_record_cancellation_in_the_durable_tail` (FIX-243) was EXTENDED with a `reason` parameter, not copied. Default keeps the no-live-driver payload byte-identical. **No duplicate-suppression guard on purpose:** the `pipeline_cancelled` FRAME was already emitted unconditionally on both branches, so the change only makes the row agree with the frame that already shipped, and every verified consumer is `any()`/`max()`-shaped.

- **An `await` inside `except asyncio.CancelledError` DOES complete here — verified, not assumed.** The escalation path is `task.cancel()`, so the durable append had to be observed landing under genuine cancellation. Related fact discovered the same way: **the driver deliberately CONVERTS the cancellation into a terminal rather than re-raising it** (`_drain_then_cancel` only needs `task.done()`), so a test asserting a re-raise is wrong.

- **ISS-126's filed locus was wrong, and it changed the fix.** A terminal run NEVER opens an SSE stream (`page.tsx:2171`), so `run_stream.py` is not on this path at all; the screen is fed by `GET /api/runs/{id}/events` replayed at `page.tsx:2234-2247`. **Both previously-rejected backend options were aimed at a path the symptom does not traverse.** Do not re-litigate them.

- **The INV-12 shape that made this safe:** `terminalMarkers(status)` is now the single terminal-marker vocabulary and the three live terminal event cases route through it (deciders 3 -> 1); the reopen gate reuses the existing `REOPEN_TERMINAL_STATUSES` and a test pins the two sets EQUAL. `applyTerminalStatus` is ONE-WAY — a non-terminal status returns `prev` by identity, so a slow `getWorkflow` on a live run can never clear a legitimately open gate.

- **THE TRAP THAT COST A FALSE GREEN, and the reason live verification is not optional here (ISS-138).** The fix was written, 20 unit tests were green, and it was still INVISIBLE on screen. The FIX-201 bridge (`page.tsx:1663-1672`) copies the LEGACY `useWorkflow.pipelineState` into the run store **WHOLESALE** once the viewport switches — a total replacement, not a merge — so it silently discarded the store-only patch. **Any future store-only correction to `pipelineState` will be clobbered the same way.**

- **The second live-only finding: `laneClarifyOpen` is the ONE lane branch not AND-ed with `isRunning`** (`DashboardLayout.tsx:1862`), deliberately, because clarify precedes `pipeline_start` (on `808612bf`: `questionnaire_ready` @5, `pipeline_start` @11) — gating it would break a LIVE clarify. So resolving `isRunning` alone only moved the header from "Awaiting approval" to **"Clarifying"**, Stop still armed. Terminal reopen now clears the run's `questionnaireData`. **`reviewGateData` is deliberately NOT cleared** — already masked by the gate branch, and clearing it alone is WORSE than nothing (lane falls to `"building"` -> "Running").

- **Two verified FE traps, now pinned by tests.** `page.tsx`'s `case "pipeline_cancelled": case "pipeline_failed":` switch arm is **unreachable dead code** (both types are in `pipelineTypes`, whose branch returns before the switch) — a fix applied there does nothing (ISS-139). And the LIVE terminal path clears only the legacy React state while the lane reads the store (ISS-140).

- **ISS-123: audited, deliberately NOT repaired.** `backend/scripts/audit_lost_run_events.py`, read-only. **15 destroyed events across 9 runs, not ~29 across 10** — the 29 counted seq-stealing app ROWS, an upper bound, not the loss. **The reason for refusing back-fill is corrected:** the CONTENT is recoverable for 11 of the 15 (they are `agent_chunk` fragments; `artifact_refs.content` is an independent authoritative record, and the audit sizes each hole against it — reproducing the lost strings exactly by length: 1, 4, 14, 26, 27). **The IDENTITY is not recoverable, and `event_id` is the key the entire replay contract rests on.** `workflow_clarifications` is empty corpus-wide; `gate_events` records no approve outcome for any run. **Never insert `run_events` rows.**

- **Three ways the audit itself can lie, all documented in the script.** Post-FIX-240 runs show the identical walked-onto shape but lost nothing (only creation time discriminates — hence `--fix240-utc`; counting them gives 16/10). A destroyed `review_gate_approved` sits TWO rows after its `review_gate_ready` because the narrator card is between them. Sizing a hole against the SUM of `artifact_refs` versions reported a 1-character hole as 18,718.

- **Verification.** Baselines vs `ce2db22e`: goldens **10 passed / 0 of the golden files moved** (SHA-256); `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken** (from `backend/`); combined backend selection **183 passed** (`test_run_events` 12, `test_sse_stream` 43, `test_restart_resume` 66, `test_rest_gate_commands` 28, `test_rest_answers_cancel` 20 -> 24). Frontend: full vitest **871 -> 894 passed**, failing set **147 -> 147 with byte-identical failing IDs**, measured in a **detached worktree at `e3c38594`** — never a stash; `tsc` the same 2 pre-existing errors. **Live A/B (no money spent, no run launched/resumed/approved):** `808612bf` corrupted -> `lane-run-status` "Cancelled" (tone=neutral), no Stop, no gate actions; `1ea6d262` clean control UNCHANGED.

## quick-260813-1b1 — a cancel at the clarify gate finally repaints the screen (FIX-247 / TEST-030)

**Closes** ISS-139 and ISS-140 (ISS-140 re-severitied minor -> **major**, its filed masking claim disproven). **Files** ISS-143, ISS-144, ISS-145.
**Commits** `d2d2da53` (plan), `ae208b53` (TS-R-05, RED), `d467ce4f` (fix + two source-lock reconciliations). Branch `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss`, baseline `d2d2da53`. **Frontend only — zero backend files, zero golden files, no new branch. NOT pushed.**
**Plan:** `.planning/quick/260813-1b1-fix-cancel-at-clarify-view-never-repaint/260813-1b1-PLAN.md`. (No `SUMMARY.md` exists for this task — writing one was blocked by a harness guard on report-shaped files, hit independently by two agents. The PLAN plus this entry are the record.)

- **Read this before touching the terminal handler in `page.tsx`.** The live `pipeline_cancelled`/`pipeline_failed` handler is the **`if (pipelineTypes.includes(msg.type))` block, NOT the `switch` below it.** Both message types are members of `pipelineTypes`, and that branch always `return`s before the switch is ever entered. Any edit made in the switch is dead on arrival — which is exactly what ISS-139 was.

- **Where the lane actually reads its state, and why that decided the fix.** `laneClarifyOpen` (`DashboardLayout.tsx:1862`) is the **ONE** branch of the `runLaneState` ternary (`DashboardLayout.tsx:1864-1871`) **not AND-ed with `isRunning`** — deliberately, because clarify precedes `pipeline_start` — and it is evaluated **before** the terminal branch. So a lingering **store** `questionnaireData` outranks terminal markers the same cancelled frame already applied correctly. The lane reads `runStore.viewed.questionnaireData` (`page.tsx:2731`); the three legacy setters the handler did call are invisible to it. That is the whole defect, and it is why clearing legacy React state alone could never have fixed it.

- **What shipped.** `if (frameRunId) runStore.update(frameRunId, { questionnaireData: null })`, run-scoped inside the existing `if (!isForeignFrame)` guard (`page.tsx:1206`), plus deletion of the entire 36-line unreachable arm — with its two genuinely live-relevant effects (`setLastCancelledRunId`, `detachRunRef.current?.()`) **rescued** onto the reachable path. This is **the first time either of those two calls has ever executed on a live cancel.**

- **`reviewGateData` is deliberately NOT in the store patch, and that is a decision, not an omission.** That half really is masked, by the gate branch's own `&& isPipelineRunning`. Clearing it would erase the historical gate card from a reopened transcript — forbidden by an existing lock in `terminalReopenReconcile.source.test.ts`. `activePipelineRunId` is likewise not added: no store write for it exists anywhere in the tree, and none is needed once `questionnaireData` is cleared.

- **TWO source-lock tests were GREEN while pinning code that had never once executed.** `terminalReopenReconcile.source.test.ts` was the known one (TEST-029 pinned the dead arm's existence as part of ISS-126's proof). `liveRunSwitch.fix201.test.ts` was **not anticipated by the plan** — a second lock on the same dead string, found only mid-execution. Both were reconciled **TIGHTER, never relaxed** — from "the dead arm exists and is where it should be" to "the dead arm is GONE and the live block carries the store write" — and the `liveRunSwitch` one additionally asserts the write stays inside `if (!isForeignFrame)`. **The general lesson: a source lock satisfied only by unreachable code proves nothing about behaviour.**

- **The regression proof is PAIRED, because the recorded baselines are not trustworthy (ISS-145).** Documentation elsewhere in this repo claims "~8 vitest reds" and "mocked e2e 132/0"; measured fresh here, twice, independently: **147 vitest reds** and a **34-failed** e2e baseline. A baseline that cannot be trusted cannot certify a regression, so both suites were measured **in the same session, reverted vs HEAD**, and the verdict is a **set-diff of failing test NAMES**: 34 failed / 108 passed -> 31 failed / 111 passed, **zero newly failing**, three flips baseline-only (TS-R-05 itself plus two proven parallel-worker flakes).

- **Verification.** Goldens **10 passed / 0 failed** (10 items collected — not a false-pass from bad path collection), IDENTICAL to `d2d2da53`, **0 golden files touched**; `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken** (from `backend/`); TS-R-05 seen **RED independently twice** with an identical failure (lane stuck at "Clarifying", `data-status-tone="running"`, timeout waiting for `/Cancelled/`) then green (4 passed, 1 pre-existing fixme skipped); the two reconciled source-lock files 35 passed. **Live on Bedrock:** two fresh cheap `user_stories` runs (~$0.01 each), each sampled at t+3s/8s/15s/25s after Stop — FIXPROBE (clarify armed: 15 chips / 4 questions / AWAITING YOU) and GATEPROBE (review gate armed; the **regression control** on the path this fix does not touch) both settle to "Cancelled", Stop absent, clarify submit absent, gate actions absent, terminal-cancelled card present, API status `cancelled`. **No `od_prototype` run was launched, resumed or approved;** the paused run `41f77342-b3c4-42ee-bf9c-215209dfc2aa` was asserted un-matched by both probes and confirmed read-only before and after at `waiting_for_user`.

- **Three findings filed rather than folded.** **ISS-143** — the header "N Running" pill goes stale after any live cancel (`AppHeader.tsx` reads `recentRuns`, and the cancelled arm never refreshes it); reproduced on the GATEPROBE control, so it is independent of this defect. **ISS-144** — `POST /api/runs/{id}/answers` has no terminal-run 409 guard, unlike `/gate`, though the helper is already imported in the same module; it answers 200 and silently no-ops, losing the user's answers. **ISS-145** — the stale frontend baselines above, filed `major` because they can certify a regression that is not there or hide one that is.

## quick-260813-3wo — a replayed narrator card must carry its row's identity (FIX-248 / TEST-031)

**Closes** ISS-146. **Files** ISS-147. **Live verification BLOCKED, not skipped — see below.**
**Commits** `f07d0ccd` (plan), `8d9b8930` (RED backend test), `5c367839` (the one-line fix + line-180 reconciliation), `57498dd8` (RED e2e + mock fidelity), `2b88c6f5` (GREEN — mock mirrors the fix, temporary flag deleted). Branch `bugfix/spec-revision-context-loss`, baseline `f87d1880`. **Backend + frontend-e2e-harness only — zero frontend PRODUCTION files. NOT pushed.**
**Investigation:** the two-stage issue-closing pipeline (parallel read-only `velocity-ai-analyze` investigator → this serial `gsd-quick` resolver), root cause independently spot-checked by the orchestrator before resolution began; ALL load-bearing claims held.

- **Read this before touching the SSE durable-replay endpoint or the narrator.** `run_stream.py`'s `_iter_sse_frames` has TWO distinct sources for what a client receives: step 1 (durable replay, `payload_json` from the DB) and step 4 (live-queue drain, whatever the producer stamped into `data` before queueing). They are not the same projection. The REST twin `GET /api/runs/{id}/events` (`api.ts:583-590`) has always merged the row's `event_id`/`seq` COLUMNS over `payload_json`; the SSE durable-replay step did not, until this fix. If you add a new app-layer `run_events` writer, check whether its payload embeds its own identity — `chat_narrator.persist_milestone_card` did not, and that omission is the entire root cause.

- **The fix is one line, and the reason it is safe to be one line is the merge ORDER.** `{**(r.payload_json or {}), "event_id": r.event_id, "seq": r.seq}` — the columns are spread LAST, so they win over any same-named payload key. For an engine-authored row (identity already stamped into the payload at `engine.py:1085-1086`) this is a provable no-op; it only repairs the four app-layer types that embed no identity (`chat_reply`, `chat_message`, `chat_usage`, `run_resuming`). `run_stream.py`'s other 3 `_sse_frame` call sites (`:220` the synthesized `stream_attached` handshake, `:258` the D-14g gate re-arm's deliberate re-send of an already-seen row, `:279` the live-drain yield whose `event` dict already carries identity) and `run_commands.py`'s 3 sites (the Concierge's own one-shot streamed-POST reply, whose dict literals already embed `event_id` explicitly) were all read and confirmed unaffected — none touched.

- **The production trigger is narrower than "any SSE reconnect," and getting the e2e test to reproduce it needed the real mechanism, not an approximation.** `pipeline_complete` is a member of the SSE endpoint's own `_STREAM_TERMINAL_TYPES` (`run_stream.py:79`), so the live drain returns the instant it drains that frame — the narrator card, queued by the engine immediately after (`engine.py:1104-1132`), is **never delivered live on that connection at all**. The client reconnects because `useRunStream.ts:301` does not treat `pipeline_complete` as a non-live close (filed separately as **ISS-147**, deliberately not fixed here — it is the TRIGGER, this fix is the DEFECT). The reconnect's replay races the completion backfill (`page.tsx` → `getRunEvents`, FIX-172's "additive insurance" after `detachRun`). That insurance is defeated whenever the run's id is ALSO in `RunConnectionProvider.autoIdsRef` — armed only by an `online`/`visibilitychange` wake firing WHILE the run is still active (`RunConnectionProvider.tsx:236,259-300,319-322`) — because `detachRun` (`page.tsx:972`) clears ONLY the sticky-focus half of `liveRunIds = union(autoIdsRef, focusedRunIdRef)`. This is exactly why the live A/B differs: `DROP=1` (a mid-run network blip fires `online`) reconnects and duplicates; `DROP=0` (no blip) does not.

- **The first e2e construction attempt correctly stopped rather than forcing a fake red — this is the intended behavior of the "STOP and report" discipline, not a failure.** The naive "emit card, then `mockSse.drop()`" shape cannot reproduce the bug: `useRunStream.ts` advances its cursor from every dispatched frame, so an already-processed card is never replayed. Three bounded variants all converged on 1 card (the CONTROL-run shape) because none armed `autoIdsRef`. The corrected test launches through the real UI flow (`dashboard.runWith`, so `sessionStorage["tab_launched_run_ids"]` is genuinely populated), fires a real `online` event while the run is still active and PROVES `refreshLiveRuns()` actually ran (`mockSse.runListFetchCount` incrementing, not just the dispatch), then drives to completion and emits the card — reproducing the real mechanism, not a simplified stand-in.

- **The mocked e2e harness had never been able to express this bug class, for two independent reasons, both fixed as part of this change.** (1) `mockSse.ts`'s `emit()` stamped a fresh `event_id`/`seq` onto EVERY frame unconditionally — it could only ever model the POST-fix wire. Added replay-vs-live awareness (a frame already pending when a stream response begins is a REPLAY; one that wakes a parked long-poll is LIVE) paired with a temporary `simulatePreFixReplay` flag — DELETED in the GREEN commit, no dead toggle left behind; the final `serialize()` diff for that removal is deletions plus one invariant comment. (2) `GET /api/runs/{id}/events` (the durable REST twin the completion backfill reads) was UNMOCKED entirely — it fell through to `mockApi`, which does not implement it either — so that whole delivery path was invisible to the mocked suite, not just to this test. Added `handleRunEvents` GLOBALLY (not opt-in), with evidence: full mocked suite 34 failed/108 passed (baseline) → 33 failed/110 passed (final, Task-6 state), zero pass→fail in either measurement taken. **Self-corrected claim:** an interim measurement (taken while the temporary stripping flag was still active) showed 30 failed/112 passed with 3 `ts-t.history` rows flipped green, and a commit message wrongly called that "fixed" — those rows are FLAKY under this suite's parallel workers, not durably fixed, and read red again in the final measurement (independently confirmed by the orchestrating agent re-running `ts-t.history.spec.ts` alone: 5 failed/2 passed).

- **Deliberately NOT added: a `useRunChat.test.ts` hook-level unit test hand-building mismatched-identity frames.** Considered and rejected — FIX-248 is server-only, so such a test would stay red forever with no path to green inside this change's scope, and this codebase has no precedent for an intentionally-red vitest unit test. The mounted e2e test is the correct, buildable proof instead; it exercises the same reducer code through the real transport, which is strictly better coverage.

- **Live verification is BLOCKED, not skipped, and the two are recorded differently on purpose.** Two `user_stories` attempts failed before reaching a deliverable — `botocore.errorfactory.InvalidGrantException: Invalid refresh token provided` on both the `hex-uki` and `hex-ai-fe` AWS SSO profiles, confirmed as infrastructure (not code) via a direct `aws sts get-caller-identity` probe and an `aws sso login` attempt that requires an interactive browser step no agent can complete. A first attempt also surfaced a pre-existing gap in the standard live-reproduction script (`20-live-control.mjs` only clicks "skip all" once; this pipeline can ask a second clarify round) — corrected in `scratchpad/24-live-control-v2.mjs`, ready but not yet run to completion. **FIX-248 must not be described as live-proven until a human completes an SSO login and this follow-up runs.**

- **Verification.** `backend/tests/unit/test_sse_stream.py` isolated: 43 passed/0 failed (baseline) → 44 passed/0 failed (post-fix), independently re-measured by the orchestrating agent, not just the executor. Goldens **10 passed / 0 failed**, IDENTICAL — 0 golden files touched (the right invocation is the 5 `test_characterization_*.py` files under `tests/agents/`; the bare `tests/agents/characterization/` directory collects 0 items, the ISS-145 collected-0/exit-0 trap, caught before being mistaken for a pass). `lint-imports` **4 kept / 0 broken** (from `backend/`), independently re-run. Mocked e2e `ts-sse-resilience.spec.ts` isolated, both via `npx playwright test` and `npm run e2e -- ts-sse-resilience`: **5 passed (7.6s)** — TS-SSE-RESILIENCE-01/02/03/04 unperturbed, TS-SSE-RESILIENCE-06 (new) green. **Live:** not completed — see above.
